a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: Roger. Clear the tower. I got a pitch and a roll program, and this baby's really going.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_000_00_00.text: Pete Conrad reports the yaw program is in. Tower clear.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: It's a lovely lift-off. It's not bad at all. [Pause.]

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_000_00_00.text: Pete Conrad reporting the pitch and roll program to put Apollo 12 on the proper course. Altitude at one half mile.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Gordon
a12a_000_00_00.text: Everything's looking great. Sky's getting lighter.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Gordon
a12a_000_00_00.text: I lost a whole bunch of stuff; I don't know...

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: Roger. We had a whole bunch of buses drop out.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Gordon
a12a_000_00_00.text: I can't see; there's something wrong.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: AC Bus 1 light, all the fuel cells...

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_000_00_00.text: Altitude, a mile and a half [nautical, 2.8 km] now. Velocity, 1,592 feet per second [485 m/s].

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: Okay, we just lost the platform, gang. I don't know what happened here; we had everything in the world drop out.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Gordon
a12a_000_00_00.text: I can't - There's nothing I can tell is wrong, Pete.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: I got three fuel cell lights, an AC bus light, a fuel cell disconnect, AC bus overload 1 and 2, Main Bus A and B out. [Long pause.]

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: Maybe it's just the indicator. What do you got on the main bus?

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Bean
a12a_000_00_00.text: Main bus is - The volt indicated is 24 volts.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: We've got a short on it of some kind. But I can't believe the volt...

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_00_00.text: Apollo 12, Houston. Try SCE to Auxiliary. Over.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: Try the buses. Get the buses back on the line.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: Stand by for the - I've lost the event timer; I've lost the...

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_000_00_00.text: Comm reports the reading is back."

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Gordon
a12a_000_00_00.text: Two minutes. EDS, Auto, is Off.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: Roger. Go for staging we had some really big glitch, gang?

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_000_00_00.text: Flight Director Gerry Griffin taking a staging status now; Apollo 12 down range 17 miles. Altitude 20 miles.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Gordon
a12a_000_00_00.text: What do the buses read, Al?

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_00_00.text: Apollo 12, Houston. Try to reset your fuel cells now. [Long pause.]

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: Got a clock running over here?

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Gordon
a12a_000_00_00.text: There's 41. Hang on, there it is.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_00_00.text: Roger. We copy, Pete. You're looking good.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_000_00_00.text: Good staging and good thrust on the second stage.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: Okay. Now we'll straighten out our problems here. I don't know what happened; I'm not sure we didn't get hit by lightning.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_00_00.text: Your thrust is looking good, Pete.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: Okay. I have a good GDC, and Al has got the fuel cells back on, and we'll be working on our AC buses.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_00_00.text: Right, Pete. Your fuel cells look good down here.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: Think we need to do a little more all-weather testing.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: There goes the tower, gang; that's away clean. It looked good.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: There goes the tower, gang; that's away clean. It looked good.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_00_00.text: Good show, Pete. You're in mode 2.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_000_00_00.text: Launch escape tower has been jettisoned on schedule. And we confirm the engines for separation also. Down range 122 [nautical] miles [226 km]; altitude 61 [nautical] miles [113 km]; velocity 10,000 feet per second [3,000 m/s].

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: Roger. In mode 2. No sweat. [Long pause.]

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Gordon
a12a_000_00_00.text: I'll tell you what I think happened. We lost all the fuel cells.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: They sure did; they dropped right off the...

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Gordon
a12a_000_00_00.text: We still got them back? We got them back now?

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: Okay. We've got an ISS light on, and we've got a cycling CO 2 partial pressure high, which I don't - bother me particularly, and we have reset all the fuel cells. We have all the buses back on the line, and we'll just square up the platform when we get into orbit.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: Hey, that's one of the better SIM's, believe me.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: Phew! Man alive! I'll tell you what happened...

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_00_00.text: We've had a couple of cardiac arrests down here, too, Pete.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: There wasn't any time for that up here. We've got a good clock running here, and correct me, I'm going to give you a mark at 4 plus 30. I've lost my event timer. And...

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: Okay. We're all organized again, gang.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Gordon
a12a_000_00_00.text: The only thing we've lost now is the ISS. That number 1 ball is just drifting all over the place, and we'll have to catch it later.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_00_00.text: We'd like to have the G&C guys think about how we're going to get that thing, because it's just drifting, just floating.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_000_00_00.text: The trajectory is right down the lines on the plot board. Altitude is 85 [nautical] miles [157 km] now.

a12a_000_00_00.speaker: Bean
a12a_000_00_00.text: Can't say that I've ever seen that before. Man alive...

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_52_39.text: Hello, Houston. Do you read Apollo 12 through Carnarvon?

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_52_39.text: Hello, Stormy. We're reading you loud and clear.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_52_39.text: Roger. Read you the same. We just finished a P51 with a four balls 1 star angle difference. Dick just did a P52 on stars 14 and 15 with another star angle difference of 1. The torquing angles were plus 00755, plus 00941, minus 00366; the time 52 plus 29; and things are back to normal.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_52_39.text: Roger, Pete. We copy your data. Your torquing angles : plus 00755, plus 00941, minus 00366 at 52:29.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_52_39.text: That's affirmative. And we're getting on with our TLI checks.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_52_39.text: Roger, Pete. Would you turn your tape recorder off and set your bit rate at High. We don't have a command - computer at Carnarvon. So you'll have to do it for us.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_52_39.text: Okay. We just got a Program Alarm 20430, whatever that is?

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_52_39.text: Roger, Pete. We'll check it out. 12, Houston. Can you give us a Verb 96, Enter, to stop your integration? And we'd like you to do an E-MOD dump. Give us a 3, 2, 1, Mark when you do your Verb 74; and if we get it done now, we should have an answer for you on your Erasable Memory by the time you get to Guaymas.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_52_39.text: Okay. Verb 74 coming at you. 1...

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_52_39.text: Do a Verb 96 first. [Long pause.]

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_52_39.text: 12, Houston. Your Program Alarm was an integration problem.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_52_39.text: I saw some illumination out the window; I'd almost be positive that we got hit by lightning some place.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_52_39.text: Roger, Pete. I don't think we got all of that transmission.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_52_39.text: Okay. I'm just saying - in thinking back to when we had our big glitch, I remember seeing it get light outside the window. We were in the clouds; I'm pretty sure we got hit by lightning.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_52_39.text: Roger. Copy. Pete, here's our plan. When you finish your E-Mod dump, then we want to get you up on Honeysuckle - and make sure, by the way, that you get your S-band volume up for Honeysuckle - We want to up-link you a state vector at Honeysuckle, and then the next dark pass, we want you to do a P52 Option 3.Over.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_52_39.text: Okay. We'll do a P52 Option 3 on the next dark pass, and that'll give you a drift check. Is that right?

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_52_39.text: That's affirmative, Pete. All the memory we can see so far looks okay, and we should have a real verdict for you at Guaymas after this E-MOD dump.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_52_39.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_52_39.text: 12, Houston.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_52_39.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_52_39.text: We're going to be passing you up some data later on in your checklist, little pieces that you can take out and go through in order to exercise some of your electrical system to give us a chance to see how it all looks.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_52_39.text: Okay. Of course, we - we're on the time line, and we've exercised fuel cell purges and things like that, and all that seems to be functioning okay.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_52_39.text: Okay, Pete. It looks down here like the reason for your IMU problem was strictly a power supply problem.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_52_39.text: Yes. We understand that. The voltage on the main buses went down to 24 volts.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_52_39.text: Yes.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_52_39.text: And when we got the fuel cells back on the line, then - all three fuel cells just flat fell off the line.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_52_39.text: Roger. Pete. We're going to lose you here in about 30 seconds; we'll pick you up on Honeysuckle, S-band only, at 59:33.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_52_39.text: Okay. We got the - we got the S-band up for Honeysuckle and - I was wrong. We're completing the fuel cell purges at this time; you can see some Master Alarms.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_52_39.text: Roger.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_52_39.text: 12, Houston. We got your E-Mod dump.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_52_39.text: Roger.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Carr
a12a_000_52_39.text: Pete, when you hit Honeysuckle, give us P00 and Accept.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Conrad
a12a_000_52_39.text: Roger.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_000_52_39.text: This is Apollo Control at 58 minutes, Carnarvon has had LOS. The Honeysuckle Station in Australia will acquire within a couple of minutes. During the Carnarvon pass, Apollo 12 did dump their Erasable Memory in the computer to the ground; it will be checked here and verified, and we should know by the time Apollo 12 is in acquisition at the Guaymas, Mexico station whether that computer memory is good or not. Over Honeysuckle we will pass them up a new state vector: their position and velocity. We should be picking up at Honeysuckle within a few seconds now. We'll continue to stand by.

a12a_000_52_39.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_000_52_39.text: The Honeysuckle has acquired Apollo12."

a12a_001_00_51.speaker: Carr
a12a_001_00_51.text: Apollo 12, Houston through Honeysuckle. How do you read?

a12a_001_00_51.speaker: Conrad
a12a_001_00_51.text: Hello, Houston. Read you loud and clear on the S-band. The computer is P00 and Accept, and I see another Program Alarm. I guess it went back into P00 again.

a12a_001_00_51.speaker: Conrad
a12a_001_00_51.text: He just gave it a Verb 96; let me look at the alarm. Yes, it's 20430 again. I just - you're - in P00 and Accept right now, and you can go ahead and take it.

a12a_001_00_51.speaker: Conrad
a12a_001_00_51.text: Okay. I had just recalled P00, and I started integration again. My fault.

a12a_001_00_51.speaker: Carr
a12a_001_00_51.text: 12, Houston. After we get the state vector up, we'll give you your 66 and your 45. [Long pause.]

a12a_001_00_51.speaker: Conrad
a12a_001_00_51.text: We had a normal Docking-Probe Extension.

a12a_001_00_51.speaker: Carr
a12a_001_00_51.text: Apollo 12, Houston. We're about 20 seconds from LOS on Honeysuckle. You're going to have to put your bit rate back down to Low and tape recorder to Forward, and we'll be picking you up on Guaymas at 01:20, correction 01:28:21.

a12a_001_00_51.speaker: Conrad
a12a_001_00_51.text: 01:28:21. Roger-Roger. And is the computer mine?

a12a_002_24_48.speaker: Conrad
a12a_002_24_48.text: Roger. I got some torquing angles for you.

a12a_002_24_48.speaker: Carr
a12a_002_24_48.text: Roger. Would you do some more work for us? Tape recorder off and High Bit Rate.

a12a_002_24_48.speaker: Conrad
a12a_002_24_48.text: Tape recorder off; High Bit Rate. We used star 01 star 45. Mr. Gordon is getting better. He had five balls, and we have a minus 0001.4 minus 0002[8]. and a plus 0001.8. And the time is 2 plus 20 plus 20 -And we had the O 2 High Flow light come On, as advertised, at about 2 plus 21.

a12a_002_24_48.speaker: Gordon
a12a_002_24_48.text: That time on that torquing was 2 hours 00 minutes 20 seconds.

a12a_002_24_48.speaker: Conrad
a12a_002_24_48.text: Yes, and excuse me. Got that one wrong.

a12a_002_24_48.speaker: Gordon
a12a_002_24_48.text: And Houston, if you're not going to use the computer, I'd like to go ahead and put in the Timebase 6 program that we have in our erasable, just to watch it.

a12a_002_24_48.speaker: Carr
a12a_002_24_48.text: Roger. The computer's all yours, and we copy your torquing angles: minus 0001.4, minus 0002.8, plus 0001.8. Done at 2 plus 00 plus 20, and copy your O 2 high.

a12a_011_11_09.speaker: Conrad
a12a_011_11_09.text: We also, Houston, think that our PCM gauge is out. It's been reading zero. We changed our canister at the proper time and we had - when was it? During powered flight, then?

a12a_011_11_09.speaker: Conrad
a12a_011_11_09.text: Yes, during launch we had a flashing CO 2 light along with a few others. This thing jumped all over the place and then all of a sudden it went to zero and then it moved off the peg, so I kind of got the suspicion that the PT CO 2 gauge was out.

a12a_011_11_09.speaker: Gibson
a12a_011_11_09.text: Roger, Pete. We confirm or suspect that down here.

a12a_011_11_09.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_011_11_09.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. That's Pete Conrad now back in the Command Module doing this trouble shooting with Ed Gibson on the ground. We are now at 11 hours, 13 minutes into the flight of Apollo 12. Presently 53,187 nautical miles [98,502 km] above the Earth and now traveling at 7,870 feet per second [2,399 m/s]. This is Apollo Control, Houston; continuing to monitor.

a12a_011_58_41.speaker: Bean
a12a_011_58_41.text: The Earth doesn't seem to be getting smaller too fast right now, but it is sort of funny. It just seems to hang out there. It doesn't - You can't see it rotate, you can't see it move or anything. It just sort of hangs out there in this black space, and the Moon just doesn't seem to be any bigger than it was when we left, but it looks more like a sphere also. It sort of looks like a ball that is being hung out there somehow. It's really crazy.

a12a_011_58_41.speaker: Gibson
a12a_011_58_41.text: Al, which way does it look like it is hanging from?

a12a_011_58_41.speaker: Bean
a12a_011_58_41.text: North Pole, naturally. Otherwise the string would get all tangled up.

a12a_011_58_41.speaker: Gordon
a12a_011_58_41.text: Just scientists are supposed to know that.

a12a_011_58_41.speaker: Bean
a12a_011_58_41.text: That sub-solar point is over the water now, and it glints on the surface of the Earth just like a light on a billiard ball or something. There is a little spot there that gives you a little specular reflection, and then it's got a bright halo, or just a bright area, around it.

a12a_011_58_41.speaker: Bean
a12a_011_58_41.text: It looks like we can see the coast of China and Japan now. It's kind of hard to tell. You can see red Earth pretty well, but if there's greens or grays, it is very difficult to discern them from the blues.

a12a_011_58_41.speaker: Gibson
a12a_011_58_41.text: Roger, Al. That glint, is that about a quarter of the way off the - about half-way between the terminator and the edge?

a12a_012_08_02.speaker: Gibson
a12a_012_08_02.text: Pete, all the folks down here feel that isn't half bad.

a12a_012_08_02.speaker: Conrad
a12a_012_08_02.text: Well, I'll tell you what it's done. It's precipitated a big search for the rest of the tapes. Al and Dick are scurrying all over the spacecraft.

a12a_014_46_04.speaker: Gordon
a12a_014_46_04.text: I was looking at the Earth a few moments ago. You can see the entire top of Australia. Sure is pretty, and hardly any clouds at all over it. And looks to me like it's to be about one and a half to two times the size of a golf ball at arm's length.

a12a_014_46_04.speaker: Lind
a12a_014_46_04.text: Should be a pretty impressive view from that altitude. [Long pause]

a12a_014_46_04.speaker: Lind
a12a_014_46_04.text: Apollo 12, would you select Omni Alpha, please?

a12a_014_46_04.speaker: Gordon
a12a_014_46_04.text: Roger. Didn't seem to change anything.

a12a_014_46_04.speaker: Gordon
a12a_014_46_04.text: Roger. We were watching the signal strength, and it didn't seem to affect it much.

a12a_015_52_52.speaker: Lind
a12a_015_52_52.text: Roger. It looks like we're ready for PTC now, and when you start the maneuver we would suggest Omni Bravo.

a12a_015_55_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_015_55_03.text: Okay. If they're happy, I'm happy. [Pause.]

a12a_015_55_03.speaker: Lind
a12a_015_55_03.text: 12, we've got an uplink to the gyro drift whenever you can give us the computer.

a12a_015_55_03.speaker: Lind
a12a_015_55_03.text: Apollo 12, the computer's yours again. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a12a_015_55_03.speaker: Lind
a12a_015_55_03.text: Apollo 12, Houston. We're finished with the computer. It's yours again.

a12a_015_55_03.speaker: Lind
a12a_015_55_03.text: This is Houston, 12. Did you call?

a12a_015_55_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_015_55_03.text: That's negative, Houston. Some other spacecraft must have called in.

a12a_015_55_03.speaker: Lind
a12a_015_55_03.text: Roger. [Laughter] I was hearing you occasionally weak, and we're not sure whether it's you or the others.

a12a_016_26_29.speaker: Lind
a12a_016_26_29.text: Listen, those transmissions you thought you heard a couple of minutes ago were us running some keying checks. We didn't think they were getting out, but apparently a couple of them did; so apparently, nobody is up there flying with you.

a12a_017_06_32.speaker: Lind
a12a_017_06_32.text: Okay. I've got your RCS propellants for you. The total is 83.2 percent; Alpha is 80.5; Bravo is 85.3; Charlie is 81.4; Delta is 85.4. That's the status as of about 2 minutes ago and also, we got your E-dump successfully.

a12a_028_00_11.speaker: Weitz
a12a_028_00_11.text: Okay. Yes, I got several paragraphs in there. Let me start over again and I'll read it on down to where - the election in Houston. World attention is on the flight of Apollo 12. The Soviet Union held the crew as courageous; and Tass, the official Soviet news agency, reported the start of the mission in a brief factual report in both of its Russian and foreign language reports. Czechoslovak television carried live coverage of the lift-off, complete with explanation of technical details. In West Germany, all radio and television networks carried the launch live, as did the Japanese Broadcasting

a12a_028_00_11.speaker: Weitz
a12a_028_00_11.text: And I got a Flight Plan update when you have a chance.

a12a_028_00_11.speaker: Weitz
a12a_028_00_11.text: Okay, Dick. At 30:30, we call for a waste water dump, which is back to our normal procedure of dumping down to 25 per cent on that one. And at 31:30, want to start a charge on battery Alpha. Over.

a12a_028_00_11.speaker: Conrad
a12a_028_00_11.text: Waste water dump 30:30, 25 per cent. Battery A charge, 31:30.

a12a_028_00_11.speaker: Weitz
a12a_028_00_11.text: 12, Houston. Your PCO 2 sensor is powered through a circuit breaker on panel 5. If you haven't already checked it, would you check Transducer Pressure Group 2; Main Alpha circuit breaker?

a12a_059_44_09.speaker: Stafford
a12a_059_44_09.text: Did you get that drift report? Your platform is less than 1.2 mERU on all axes.

a12a_059_44_09.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_059_44_09.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. The gentleman in Mission Control Center who prefaced this conversation with Beano, this is your old Social Director is Colonel Tom Stafford who, as you will recall, was the Commander on Apollo 12. Shortly after Tom came on the line, the Commander of Apollo 12, Pete Conrad, chimed into the conversation. We are at 59 hours, 44 minutes...

a12a_059_44_09.speaker: Stafford
a12a_059_44_09.text: Apollo 12, Houston. How's your sleeping bags working out up there, Pete?

a12a_059_44_09.speaker: Conrad
a12a_059_44_09.text: Real good, Tom. The first night I slept in a bag, and Al slept in a bag, and Dick slept up in the seat. He didn't sleep too well. And last night, I slept up in the seat, and Dick slept in my bag, and all of us like the bags. And one of the problems with the seat is that - and we're going to take care of that tonight - it's rattling around in here, and every time somebody stirs down below, why the seat bangs off the wall and that naturally wakes up the guy that's sleeping in it. It's kind of spring loaded, anyhow.

a12a_059_44_09.speaker: Stafford
a12a_059_44_09.text: Roger. Looks - you getting plenty of sleep? Over.

a12a_059_44_09.speaker: Conrad
a12a_059_44_09.text: Yes, plenty. We're getting more than I need.

a12a_059_44_09.speaker: Stafford
a12a_059_44_09.text: Good. The reports look real good down here. [Long pause.]

a12a_059_44_09.speaker: Gordon
a12a_059_44_09.text: Hey, Tom. What do you think of our RAD count?

a12a_059_44_09.speaker: Gordon
a12a_059_44_09.text: What do you think of our PRD count?

a12a_059_44_09.speaker: Stafford
a12a_059_44_09.text: Well, from down here, it looks like the total Rad count showed that you got practically nothing up there.

a12a_059_44_09.speaker: Gordon
a12a_059_44_09.text: Well, I wouldn't go so far as to say we've got nothing.

a12a_059_44_09.speaker: Stafford
a12a_059_44_09.text: At least, they call it 90 millirads.

a12a_059_44_09.speaker: Stafford
a12a_059_44_09.text: That's less than 1/300th of what atomic workers can get.

a12a_059_44_09.speaker: Stafford
a12a_059_44_09.text: And I'd nearly bet that the calorie count that you people can see up there just nearly zero.

a12a_062_24_38.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_24_38.text: Apollo 12, Houston, with a Flight Plan update.

a12a_062_24_38.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_24_38.text: Roger. Your TV pass at 63 plus 00. Number 1, stop your PTC roll at 285, and this is what you need to put the Sun through the hatch window. Step number 2 is your High-Gain antenna angles are pitch 19, yaw 268. Step number 3, put the ALC switch to the In position, and open the camera aperture to Full Open for your tunnel pictures.

a12a_062_34_31.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_34_31.text: When do you want us to start this show, now?

a12a_062_34_31.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_34_31.text: Pete, we're ready whenever you are. Your option.

a12a_062_34_31.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_34_31.text: Okay. That's what I figured. So, we're starting to pressurize the Command Module now, and we'll start here directly.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. We're coming up Vox at this time, and we're getting ready to give you the TV. Al will get it going in just a second.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Roger. Standing by. [Long pause.]

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: [Garbled] properly dressed.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Jerry, we've got to dress Al yet. We have to put on his hat.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Roger. Lights! Camera! Action! [Pause.]

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: I'm down here [garble] up in here, I guess.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Let him get over here where the Sun comes in.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Shortly too.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: There you go.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Who, me? Okay? [Long pause.]

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. You putting it out? Wait a minute. You got it on the ground yet, Houston?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Not yet, Pete.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. We'll hold until you get the picture.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. We're not copying any FM downlink as yet. [Pause.]

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: 12, Houston. We have you in blushing black and white. And the color's coming in now.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Roger.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: What happened to the color?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: There you go.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Takes a little for the processing.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. As you can see, Dick's up there in the tunnel, and he's opening the vent valve now, and he's starting to pressurize the LM.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: And we have a Delta-P of about 2.3 at the moment.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. It's going down to about 2.2.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Well, no. The Delta-P went up when we pumped up the cabin.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Delta-P is 1.8.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: What's the cabin? Okay. Just about do it. We're down to 1.3 Delta-P. Okay, 1 psi Delta-P.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: While we're equalizing the cabin, Houston, the attitude that you have us in, out our number 1 window, we have the Earth; and out the number 3 window, we have the Sun shining in; and out the number 5 window, we have the Moon. And, of course, we're too far from either the Earth or the Moon to see any motion, so it just seems to us that we're in suspended animation out here.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Roger.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: What's the cabin pressure, Al?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Yes, it is. And you just brought the cabin Reg on and that ought to be okay so ...

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: We're reading you 4.7 on your cabin pressure now; and, Al, we're not reading you at all.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: [Garbled] How do you read me now?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, now, Al.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. And the hatch is open.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: What in the heck is this thing doing up here? Here it goes - there's another one right there. You may not want to move it. There you go.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: All right.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. Pretty good - How's the lighting down there, Houston? Looks pretty good on the monitor.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: It's very good. We have a good picture of the hatch.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: That's your feet up on the window there, Pete.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Sorry about that.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. Let me get the hatch bag open so we can get it in.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: This big old hatch wrestles pretty easily here in zero g.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Beats one g all to heck, doesn't it?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Sure does, Jerry.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: MS
a12a_062_50_01.text: [Garble]

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Dick's putting it under the left-hand couch now. If we move down there, we can [garble]

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: I just noticed, 12 ...

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: There you go.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: The outer side of that hatch makes a pretty good light reflector. So you might keep that in mind if you ever need a light at that place.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: It sure does. Did you notice that, too?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Affirmative. It really lighted things up.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, now, we'll get back up there. We'll get up there again and take the probe out. As you recall, we've had it in and out of there several times already. And the procedures are fairly simple. Now that we've done it, we've already bled the nitrogen out, but all I do is hit that button anyway just for procedural purposes. And the pre-load handle's all set and everything. We'll, unlock the temperature latch lock, and we'll extend the strut. The umbilicals are already disconnected and stowed.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: The lighting in the tunnel is just a tad dim, but we can make out what you're doing. [Pause.]

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: That's wide open on the f-stop now, Houston.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Roger.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: I think part of the problem is there's a lot of contrast between that dark tunnel and the white garment of Dick's. It's giving the camera a little fit.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, turn the capture latch release 180 degrees, and all I have to do is pull the probe out of there. Okay, away she comes. [Long pause.]

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: All right, while Dick's stowing that, I'll go up and get the drogue.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: You got any late-night watchers, Jerry?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: That's affirmative.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Al, can you pull up your [garble], please?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. Just a second; I'll have to move the camera.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: I'll hold the camera; here, hand it to me. I've got it.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. How's that, Dick?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: I've got it just fine.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. Dick's putting the probe now under the right-hand seat, and he's going to have to strap that in with something - just enough to hold it there. Let's see if I can scoot around and give you a shot of it. Not quite as light down in there.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, Pete. We're ready for the drogue.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Coming down. [Pause.]

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: [Garbled] you juggle with this thing every time.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Al, you got it on the umbilical cover; that's one reason. On your right hand; there you go.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Boy. Hey, move back that way, and I'll take it away from you.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Sounds like you're handling empty milk cans up there.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: There you go.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Hey, you want to look at the drogue after a docking?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: That's right. Turn it around, but don't let any light hit on it, Dick, or I can't see it.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: How's that?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Too much light. Sort of tip it up or move it over to the left or right. It's got a little circle of light on it.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: How's that? Is that better?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: I'll move in [garbled] there's the drogue after one docking.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Roger. We can't see too much because of the big light spot on it.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, why don't you stash that, Al or Dick, and stick ...

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: There's Dick Gordon looking through the hole.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Hello, there.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: The only mark on it is - show them where the mark is, Dick. You hit it almost dead center when you did the docking. Yes, right there. That's funny. That mark looks just like a nose; about the same length, too.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, Al. You want to stick her up here and we'll [garbled]. [Pause.]

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, go ahead, Pete.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: All right.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, 12. The lighting in the tunnel looks pretty good now.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. And if you'll hold it just a minute, I'll get the window shades down in the LM here.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: There he goes. I don't think so. Not today. I have to transfer over these things, Dick, right here. Okay, well, I'm going over, but you'll have to hand us these goodies. We'll stick them in the LM. Hey, it looks like there's good lighting up there.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Roger, 12. Lighting is very good.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, we're going to -.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Hand me those hoses first. Let me get some air going.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Here, I'll get up there. Just sling me the book, Dick.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: And do you want to hand the long hoses up? We're putting these CSM hoses down inside the LM, since there's no ventilation in there now. We just lay them around down there where we're going to be working with the LM, and it makes it real nice for cooling and gives you clean air down in there. Without them, it gets a little stale after a while. Okay. Why don't I just go through and show them how it looks ...

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: ...when you go through the tunnel.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Go on. [Pause.]

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. It's pretty easy. Just float on up. Only problem is, when you get in here, we're going to be upside down and then you got to turn around and decide ...

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Hand me the camera.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: ...which way is right side up.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: There you go. Now I'm going to check this line. It may not be as long as we'd like. That's it right there. That's it, Pete.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: You'll probably have to turn around upside down, let me dive in there.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: I tell you what. Let me scout those items, and I'll hand them in to you, Pete.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: All right, what are you looking for?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Hand me the book, and I'll do it, toss them in to you, and you can put them up.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: 12, Houston. We had a pretty good view of your ECS module there; and now, we're getting a good view of the main panels upside down.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: We discovered an interesting thing while we were in here the other day. The AOT looks right into the Command Module rendezvous window, and I was looking out to see what I could see, and I saw this face looking back at me, and it was Dick in the other window.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Roger. Did it scare you?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: It should have.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: [Garble] it's hot in here. It's quite warm in here today. The way we stopped has the Sun coming in through one window, and it's heating it up pretty good in here.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Roger. Looks like the Sun's coming in through the CDR's window.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Yes. That's right.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Here's a box of Kleenex, Pete. Coming in, right by you.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Got it.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Next one's two towels. I'll go get them.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: We just had a good view of the PLSS fastened down there on the floor between your legs.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Yes. I can't go down any further. My Comm line won't allow me to go any further than I am right now, so I got myself Velcroed to the top of Al's PLSS.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. That's a good view of it right there.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: I'm just giving you a two-bit tour, Jerry.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Roger.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: When we were in the other day, we rigged the...

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Hey, here comes...

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: What you got, Al?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: ...yes, here comes a couple of towels. Both of that and the Kleenex go in the left-hand side storage compartment. Let me get the 16-millimeter magazines and 70-millimeter magazines.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Hey, Al. Why don't you come up here, and let me get those for you?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. That's a good idea, and then maybe I can say a few words about this here.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Well, as a matter of fact, you're going to have to do that, Al, because I can't get any lower on this Comm cable. You're the only one that can get down there.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: All right.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: I'll hold the camera, Dick. We have a three-way switch here in the tunnel.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, I'll just come on past. Okay?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Dick?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay? [Long pause.]

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: We just had a good view of your helmet stowage bag down there a couple seconds ago.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Al, here's the Kleenex and the towels.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Looks like you're trying to pack a telephone booth.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: I'll get the camera in here, Jerry, and bring it around the corner.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. Let me put those in their proper spots.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Roger.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, I'll just stick this down in here.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: You can also see in the picture the restraint straps that are hooked up above that, used to hold us in for landing.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: There you go. Yes, this is what Pete's talking about. Okay, you got some more goodies? 70-millimeter magazines. There's two of them. These are the two that go here in the TSB, Temporary Stowage Bag [garble].

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Two of them go in the ISA.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Right, just a second. TSB safely stuffed away. Take a look in here, and let's see how this looks. Let's poke them right in here; then they'll be here tomorrow. Open this up.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: 12, Houston. Our color TV is running about 11 seconds behind your voice; and so what you're talking about, we're seeing about anywhere from l0 to ll seconds later.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. That's interesting. Was that due to the processing?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: That's affirmative.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: What we are doing now is putting the - two of the 70-millimeter magazines for Hasselblads in the stowage container here. Those are the two that we're going to use when we first get on the lunar surface. Here's three more, and these three will be used the second EVA, and so we'll stick them over here in the right-hand side stowage compartment. The right-hand side doesn't - isn't removable at all, as you probably know. We'll go ahead - The cameras and film that we bring back from the lunar surface, we'll put all of that material over here on the right-hand side, or a lot of it anyway, because th

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Roger.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, here's the 16-millimeter film.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: The same thing with the 16-millimeter film, you'll be seeing in a moment.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, there's just one of those, Dick, and that's in A-8.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: That's the whole package, just here?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: That's it.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, as you see, I'm just about to put the 16-millimeter magazines in their stowage compartment. In spacecraft, as you can see, there is not a lot of room, so you end up having to put every item in its own little place. As you can see, as the film - as magazines go in, they fit into a tidy little ...

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: We need one of those. We need a spare.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: ...[garble] bracket. And if Pete gives you a complete look at that right-hand stowage compartment, you can see we've got quite a lot of goodies here. Down here, we've got a spare ...

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: We're getting a good view of the right-hand compartment now, and we can see your helmet stowage bag down there in the corner, that spherical white bag.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Right. Right in here, we keep some spare bulbs for the COAS. A little bit higher up, we've got Sun filter for our telescope.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Yes, and it's marked.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: There's the COAS filter. It's the pilot's sighting device. The waste stowage bags are stored in the bottom two compartments. In here, I hope, is our Hasselblad camera, at least one of them. We have two of them. Yes, there it is. Got to put it together right now. It is - just the camera itself; we'll have to put the magazine on later, and the handle, and all the attachments allowed to be fixed to our PLSS. RCU, PLSS RCU.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Is that all of the transfer?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Roger, Al. That's the color camera you're going to use out on the lunar surface, isn't it?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: No, Jerry. We don't have the color camera that we're going to use on the lunar surface inside the LM. It is outside on the MESA, and it's going to be just like Apollo 11. When Pete goes down the ladder, he'll pull a handle; it will lower the MESA, and then the TV will be pointing right at the lower part of the ladder so that everyone can see when he steps on the surface. We'll later put that out on the lunar surface on a tripod, and we'll be able to move it around so that everybody can see for both of our EVA's. Those two cameras - I only showed you one; the other is right next to it - are the

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Jerry, I'm showing you a picture of the instrument panel right now; but what I'm more interested in, on my monitor, I can see some dust particles; maybe you can see them down there on the TV. I think that's pretty good resolution.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: That's affirmative, Pete.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: They happened to be floating in the sunlight - they just happened to be floating in the sunlight that's in here. Of course, there is a little bit of - it's very light dust, but it looks big on the TV screen because the Sun is illuminating it; and, of course, as soon as we start running the ECS system in here, it will clean it all out.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, I am going to start doing that right now. Just opened the descent H 2 O. I'm opening the descent O 2 , Pete, and going to Cabin Repress, Auto; and, when I do, you are going to hear a bang, so ...

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Stand by for the bang.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: ... Dick? Get ready for the bang.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Stand by for the bang.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Ready.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay,. That's it. And the Cabin Repress circuit breaker is going to go closed, Suit isolation valve, O 2 , Flow, and then actuate override.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: If you will just wait a minute, let me - I've got to get the camera on all that good stuff.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: All right..

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: 12, Houston. We can see the dust particles very well.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: This is a shot of the suit disconnect valves.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Did you show them where both of our PLSS's were stowed? We got one over here, Pete, on the side and one on the bottom. I didn't know - one of the floor right in front of the hatch.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: 12, Houston. We've seen the one on the floor ...

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: So, if you can show us the one over on the side, we'll be in good shape.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: And pull this latch right?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: I don't know; you will have to back it up [garble] and show that, Pete?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: It's pretty tight quarters in there.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: I don't know; you're going to have to back the camera up.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. Why don't I do that.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Take a look at the monitor.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, what we've got on this side, Jerry, is what we call a left-hand side stowage compartment, and it's pretty unique in that it's made out of Beta cloth, and from these snaps, you can see we can remove it. So what we do after the first EVA, we put a lot of our things that we don't need anymore inside these bags, and then we can put them outside on the lunar surface; and after the second EVA, we can put some other things in this other or the backend side of this stowage compartment, and then put it out on the lunar surface, also, until we end up being able to very tidily put some of our gear

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Be sure we don't get too much ...

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: That's a good picture.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: [Garble] get that last item.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Yes, Pete's PLSS is on the wall behind him. When we suit up, we won't have a lot of time to talk to you on the lunar surface. What we do is, Pete gets over on his side, which is the left side of the spacecraft, this side over here. I'll be over on the right; I'll take my PLSS off the floor and put my OPS on top of it. Pete will do the same thing with his; then he'll put - hold my PLSS up while I put it on; this takes about 10 or 15 minutes to get my PLSS on and connected. Then I kind of back over in my corner and hold his PLSS; he turns around and puts it on. It's not a lot of room here, as yo

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Hey, Al, I wonder if it's at all possible for you to stop the camera down and show them the window.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: The markings on the window? That's a good idea.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Yes. The RTG is really illuminated there in the Sun.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. Why don't you see if you can get over there near it?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: All right.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Maybe we can show where you're standing there. Okay, the light just went out, Houston, because I've stopped the camera way down.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Roger.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: What I'm going to try to show you, without bothering the camera. Yes, but we don't need since I've got it [garble].

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: 12, Houston. What's the configuration of your suit ISOL valves, now?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: We opened and closed them, per the checklist. They are both in Suit Disconnect.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: It is getting awful bright.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: I know it. It's liable to bother that camera.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: There you go.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Is that too bright on the ground, Houston?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: It is f:22,

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Can't tell, Pete.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: You're looking at, Houston.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Roger. We can see the scribe marks on the window.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. What happens is, Pete stands right behind those scribe marks you can see right at the top; There's - where the horizontal line is, that's 0 degrees, and then there's a 10 down, 20 down, and 30, 40, and on down. Right at the top then, left and right, there is also some angular marks. As we proceed in the descent and we pitch over where the lunar surface is visible, about 7,000 feet, Pete's going to be looking out through the window at those marks. I'll be reading from the computer, and the computer will say where it's taking us to land, relative to those marks. For example, probably the f

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Apollo 12, Houston.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Got any questions on that LPD, Houston? Go ahead.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Roger. I hate to change the subject on you guys, but it looks like you don't have your Auto Repress capability now. When you activated your Suit ISOL valve, it looks like what you should have done is gone to the Suit, Flow, and then used your actuator override, in order to set it up.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: How does that look to you, Houston?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: We don't have TM; we saw that on your TV picture when you were over there fooling with it; and, so far, we haven't seen it again.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. We fixed it up for you.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. Thanks. I think you pretty well covered that LPD situation. I don't know that there could be any questions.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. We're readjusting it back inside now, Houston. Back over here, Al.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, let me run up one of these window shades so I can cheek this AOT. Cut down your light, and maybe I can just leave it open a little bit. Just the other day, this AOT was beautiful. Push around over here. Scribe works, focus [garble].

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, Dick. I'm shining the camera down the tunnel at you now. The hats awful bright in the Sun. That's it, see? Yes.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Hello, Dick. We can see it. [Pause.]

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: You shine - you reflect the Sun, Dick. I can't keep it on you; you reflect the Sun off your suit so bright. I'm afraid it's going to burn a spot on the tube.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Pete, you going to let Dick get any LM time?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Yes, he's been in and out with us.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. Pete. I think we're finished checking this thing out.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: They've got to Jerry. They get Command Module time.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: That's right, babes; equal time.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Ready to close up shop?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. Are you going to open - are you going to open that window or not?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: That's it, no. We're through with those.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Yes, we're finished.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Jerry, do you have any more questions on the LM? Does anybody have any more questions down here or anything they want to see?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: No, I guess not, 12. Very good travelog, gang.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: We're going to start to button her up, and I'm gonna ...

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: All right, Dick. We can ...

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Hey, Pete ...

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: ...go on and button that up and then bring that camera in here and

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: I'm going to send the camera over to you right now.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: ...take a look at the Earth and the Moon.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. Here. Here comes the camera, followed by me. Toot. Toot. Watch it. It's at f:20 wide open so - stop her down. There you go. [Pause.]

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: 12, Houston.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. I'm going to close the cabin - - going to close Cabin Repress now.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Stand by for a bang, Dick.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: That's it.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: 12, Houston. We heard the bang that time.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Yes. It sounds like about a .32 going off in your ear.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Roger. And, Pete, on your way through there, would you give us another tunnel index reading?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: It was minus 0.3 the other day, Pete. I hope it hasn't changed.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Fortunately, it hasn't. It's still minus 0.3.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Hey, Jerry?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Go ahead.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Hey, Jerry?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Go ahead, Dick.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Did you see that number 1 window on the television? ...

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: That's affirmative.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: ...number 1 window on the television? That's what it looks like.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Say, Dick.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: What's this thing out the window?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Pete, I need your damp rag. We ought to clean this CSF tunnel hatch seal. It's got a bunch of junk stuck on it.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Thank you. Looks like all these circuit breakers are just exactly like we left them.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: That makes sense.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. Floodlight's, on; window shades, up; cabin dump valve, Open. Is it still open, Pete?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Cabin dump valve is still open.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. The IVT and press on.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: 12, Houston. That's a real good picture of the number 1 window there.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: What have you got in the picture? Be careful, Charlie.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: There is a big white thing out there. It looks like a piece of pie.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Yes. That's right.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. Hand me the hose, Al.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. Just double-checking all these things to make sure they were tidy. Got them?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, Jerry. I'll go over to the number 5 window now.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Roger.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Notice the stuff on the number 1 window is kind of linear looking. Linear striations or something.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Yes. It's still open.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Did you light the seal yet?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Yes, I've got to finish it in just a minute.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. I was going to lift this hatch to you.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Either the problem there, Dick, is - that television line is around Al's Comm [garble] Okay, Houston. What do you have on number 5 window?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Roger. We can see the Moon out there.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: How does it look?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Very, very slender segment. And it's a real good picture of it.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Was the picture of the Earth any good?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Yes, it was pretty bright.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Before?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Couldn't really see much except just the segment of it.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, I had it stopped all the way down. Hey, Dick, will you take that hose and stick it someplace? Thank you. There you go. Now watch it. Your wire is - let me go through there.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: SC
a12a_062_50_01.text: .[laughter].

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Looks like a snake pit. [Pause.]

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: That ought to do it.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Yes.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Hey. you and I are tangled up.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: SC
a12a_062_50_01.text: .[laughter].

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: There you go.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay. Let me slide back down there and finish the seal off.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: All right.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Hey, are you doing good?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: [Garble] your feet out now.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Hey, Jerry, I have the Earth again. Is that a better picture?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: That's a much better picture. [Pause.]

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: That landmass you're looking at there is Australia.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Roger. We can't...

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: SC
a12a_062_50_01.text: ...[garble]...

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: ...determine anything on the Earth there, but it looked quite a bit more like the Earth now than it did before. It looks like you got it stopped down considerably more.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: 12, Houston. The word is Australia is getting your TV show live.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Roger. They're getting it live, and I wish they could see their landmass. It's almost right in the middle of the Earth. And they ought to recognize the snow cap of South Amer - of the South Pole just below them.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: SC
a12a_062_50_01.text: Oh, ho.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: I know it's been said before, but this is a really spectacular sight.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Australia is getting this live? I'd like to say hello to all my friends down there at the tracking station at Carnarvon, if they're down ...

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: How about handing me the drogue, Al, and I'll get that ...

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: ... [garble] right now. Okay, here it comes.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: 12, Houston. Don't forget the troops at Honeysuckle.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Hello to all the troops at Honeysuckle. Haven't been to Honeysuckle, though.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: What he's saying, Jerry, He's asking for a trip.[laughter].

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: That's what I figured - to Honeysuckle.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: This one isn't long enough.[laughter]. This one's not long enough for him.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Getting that in there, Pete?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Yes.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Jerry, when we go back to the other side, turn to that monitor again. We may have a better picture this time.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, Dick. [Pause.]

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Here's the problem, right here. Get it through here this way.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: And then stand like you want.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, very good.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: There you go.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: There we go.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Stand any way you like it.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Oh, there we go. [Long pause.]

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: I hope I did. Are you [garble]?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, Dick. We're copying the Moon now.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: How's it look?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: [Garble] as much as he's going to see.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: This is even a much better shot than the last one.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Well, do you see a place there you'd like to go?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: I'd like to go anyplace there.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, one drogue's in, and somebody's pencil is floating by. Here you go. Is it yours, Al?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: I'll check and see.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, [garble] rest of that stuff now?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Yes. I'll hold the camera, and you can get the ...

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: No, no.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: ...get the ...

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: We're going to change stations, Jerry.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Roger.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: I'll put this circuit back under the seat where it belongs. Hey, Al, let me get up out of your way.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: 12, Houston. On that Moon shot, it looked like we could see part of the lunar surface that's in the terminator and behind the terminator.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Good luck. We're having trouble doing that ourselves. [Pause.]

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: I didn't realize that waste water dump was so propulsive. That really upset us there awhile back.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: It sure did.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_062_50_01.text: Did you clean that seal real good, Pete?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Yes. That seal looked like the perfect dust collector or something. It was really dirty.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: FIDO says he really appreciated that dump.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay, [garble] put the - say again?

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: FIDO said he really appreciated that dump.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: SC
a12a_062_50_01.text: [laughter].

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: [Garble] the TV, Dick Gordon, and all - give you some tunnel shots again.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Bean
a12a_062_50_01.text: [Garble] out of the tunnel.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Conrad
a12a_062_50_01.text: Go back inside and bring up the f-stop a bit. [Garble] out. Refocus. Giving you some more tunnel work, Houston.

a12a_062_50_01.speaker: Carr
a12a_062_50_01.text: Okay.

a12a_083_03_11.speaker: Weitz
a12a_083_03_11.text: Okay, Pete. We'll see you at 43:57.

a12a_083_09_52.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_083_09_52.text: We're coming up now on 36 seconds until Loss Of Signal. All flight controllers here in Mission Control getting one last look at their data before the spacecraft goes behind the Moon. All systems looking very good, prior to this Lunar Orbit Insertion maneuver. And our Network Controller reports we have Loss Of Signal right on schedule. We should reacquire Apollo 12 in about 32 minutes. Without the burn, the reacquisition time would be 24 minutes, 40 seconds from now. At last look, just before we lost data, the spacecraft was at an altitude of 471.9 nautical miles velocity at 7,188 feet per seco

a12a_083_44_19.speaker: Conrad
a12a_083_44_19.text: Hello, Houston. Yankee Clipper with Intrepid in tow has arrived on time. Are you ready for the burn status report?

a12a_083_44_19.speaker: Conrad
a12a_083_44_19.text: Okay. The burn was on time. The burn time was 5 plus 52. The residuals were minus 0.1, plus 0.1, plus 0.1; Delta-V c was plus 1.0; the fuel, 38.4; the oxidizer, 38.7; the unbalance was increase 80 pounds. Over.

a12a_083_44_19.speaker: Conrad
a12a_083_44_19.text: Computer says we're in a 170 by 61.8.

a12a_083_44_19.speaker: Conrad
a12a_083_44_19.text: I guess like everybody else that just arrived, we're - All three of us are plastered to the windows looking.

a12a_083_44_19.speaker: Bean
a12a_083_44_19.text: Yes, but to Navy troops - It doesn't look like a very good place to pull liberty, though.

a12a_083_44_19.speaker: Weitz
a12a_083_44_19.text: Okay. We'll give you an okay three wire on that one.

a12a_083_44_19.speaker: Bean
a12a_083_44_19.text: Very good. I hope we can say the same thing tomorrow. Save those for tomorrow.

a12a_083_52_17.speaker: Conrad
a12a_083_52_17.text: Well, Houston, I was just looking at one very, very, odd, and it looks like a very fresh impact crater that is sort of collapsed on one side -that we've been looking at and discussing a little bit. It's got some fairly high raised sides on it, and we haven't quite got ourselves oriented to the proper size yet. I think these craters are much bigger than anything we've ever seen on Earth, so we're - We're just sitting here discussing various sizes and getting ourselves oriented on the map. I just broke out the monocular, and we're starting to look with it.

a12a_083_52_17.speaker: Bean
a12a_083_52_17.text: One interesting thing, Paul, was that in some of these large craters - the old ones, it looks like - as you look towards the distance, you can see that they - at least from here - appear darker, and it looks very flat like the mare looked from Earth, but the same size ones that you pass right over, they don't look a bit darker than any other of the terrain. So I guess it must have something to do with the way the Sun refracts off the - the surface. We're passing a beautiful impact crater here on our right side now. It's got many, many long rays; it's a beauty.

a12a_083_52_17.speaker: Bean
a12a_083_52_17.text: It's - This impact crater that we're going over right now, which has such a fantastic ejecta pattern that we can see it so well, the ejecta pattern's got to go out 50 or 60 crater diameters, very easily discernible with the eye. And you can almost - You can pretty well tell the direction of the impact from looking at the ejecta blanket, but it - it's rea1ly spectacular.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: 12, Houston. For information, you should be crossing 60-degrees east at 84:02:08.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: We agree. [Pause.]

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: What do you see on the tube, Houston? I can't tell too much from the monitor.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay. We're getting the - the lunar surface. It appears that we can see the subsolar point, or could at one time there. We can see numerous small light-colored craters. Okay...

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: I'm going to hand it over to Dick. He's got Langrenus out the window.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay. Very good.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: We're coming up on Vox to you, Houston.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: All right.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Dick's got the camera. He's pointing it over toward Langrenus now. This Petavius over here is a beautiful thing. Whenever you get finished, I'll see if I can shoot it.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: It's got high peaks in the middle.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: What happened to the monocular?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Here it is. [Long pause.]

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: [Garble] there's the central peaks right in Langrenus right there...

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: I can see those pretty well.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Roger. We're picking it up. On the screen, the colors appear to be green to brown. Can you describe the colors in the scene that you're seeing there now?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: That'll do for now. The - mountain that's sort of [garble] sort of in the center of Langrenus I'm looking at through the monocular, and apparently, they look very smooth with the naked eye, but by looking through the monocular, I can pick up these black dots. They're very black, and I - they're obviously very large boulders sitting that are around on it.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Roger. The picture on the TV screen...

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: ...of the central peak - it looked kind of -it appeared to be rather rounded.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Yes. It appears to be rounded, but it's got a lot of big boulders sitting on it. I'll hand the camera over to Al, now. He's got some stuff out his window.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Oops, that's one for the geologists, the materials out his window he wants to shine it down on.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: I see...

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: I [garble] myself. [Pause.]

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: You were asking what color it looks like from here. It's changed slightly as we went around it. At first, it had a very, very light gray-white concrete appearance. Now, it has more of a - it's still a light-gray concrete, but it has a little - just a touch of brown in it. At least, that's the way it appears to me. That's the - the Moon that's directly below us. Of course, there's several places that are very, very white, and I'll point the camera at one of them now. It's a small crater, and it's very symmetrical. It just looks like a cone with a flat bottom.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Roger.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: If you can see that.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay. It's going out the top of the screen. Can you move up and pick it up just a little? There, that's good.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: There you go.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: I understand that...

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: We're going over Theophilus.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: Yes, Pete.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Fifty minutes.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay. Understand that this...

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: There goes the color again.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Tweak! Tweak!

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: ...crater appears to be white down inside, Al. Is that right?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Well, it's pretty bright. It's white, and then it's got some radial streaks of a more darker material. It's rolling down, or at least runs from the rim down to the center - down to the flat bottom. I think you can see those on the TV. Let me show you a real bright crater that's more towards the horizon, but it's one of the very, very bright ones. Can you see that? I'll try to put it right in the center.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay. I can see one that's just a little bit above the edge of the window there.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Row's that now?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Right. Another interesting thing is - This white or gray-white Moon, it contrasts very starkly with the black sky just like everyone's reported. And maybe even so on the TV down there. But the black is about as black as you've ever seen in your life. It's just - doesn't have any - any hues or anything to it. It's just solid straight dull black, and then the Moon is just sort of very light concrete color. In fact, if I wanted to look at something that I thought was about the same color as the Moon, I'd go out and look at my driveway.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay. We'll send...

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Not near as - even Earth orbit - Even Earth orbit at night or the daytime, the sky was never as black as it is here. This is the blackest black I ever saw. Al described it as dull, and it doesn't even seem like a dull black when you look at it on the horizon, to me. It's like an ebony black. It's as coal black as I've ever seen.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay. I'm going to pass the TV over to Dick now.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Show you - There's a very interesting crater that Dick's got down there. There's another one that I'm looking into; it's the first one I've seen with the fractures in the bottom of it that we've flown right directly over. And there's a fracture pattern that runs right through the middle of the crater including the rim of it, perpendicular to it, crosses all the way across the crater, so it gives me the feeling that - that the fracture pattern - that particular fracture doesn't have anything to do with the crater.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Roger.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay. What are looking at there now, 12? Is that the bottom of the crater or a Mare area?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: That's at the bottom of a crater, a large Mare area actually, Paul. And in the crater, there are two - in the Maria, there are two brand new craters that have fairly detailed ray patterns I going out from them.
