They're quite start - quite I startling when you see them, because they are I perfect radial patterns from two of them, right next to each other.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: The edge is pretty interesting. As a matter of fact, that one ray pattern looks like it's only one direction. It look that way to you, Dick?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: Yes. It looks like it's pointing towards us.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Yes.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: That double-ray pattern is just a single one.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Roger, 12.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Oh! That is a beautiful crater over here to the right. It's not particularly spectacular, but it's pretty symmetrical, and it's got some interesting sloping in on the sides. It looks like an old, old one. We're getting ready to pass over the Sea of Fertility right now. I guess we are over it. There's a lot of rilles and some cracks in here we ought to be able to pick up on the TV. [Pause.]

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: We're passing over the Sea of Fertility now, and it is a little bit darker than the terra that we've been over, but not so much. It's more of a - just a slightly darker gray.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Roger, 12.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Looks like the beach sand down at Galveston when-ever it's wet.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay. We had a team of geologists checking your driveway. We'll send them to Galveston now.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: [Laughter]. Okay.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Looking down into a real fresh impact crater in the Sea of Fertility; and, with the monocular, I can see some pretty large boulders. So I guess, as high as we are, if I can see those boulders, they must be pretty darn big.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Roger. We can see that crater in the lower left part of the screen right now.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: Yes, let me show this impact crater or you got something you want to show them, Pete? Hey, let me show you...

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: One is fairly bright.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: You can sure see the direction that one came in from, can't you, Pete? There's hardly any ejecta to our right, which would be - to the south, I guess.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: That one you're looking into now, Houston, that's the one I was saying. It's really got some big boulders in the bottom of it.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Roger. You're breaking up a little on Vox, Pete.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Sorry.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay. We see that crater there which has a ray pattern through about everything but about a 110-120- degrees of it off to the right. Is that the one to which you're referring?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: That's - yes, that's right. That's correct.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Understand that you can see larger boulders in the bottom of the crater?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Yes, and also along the sides of it. [Pause.]

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Hey, there's a big one we have right there now.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Yes, that one just came into view. I guess that's still in the Sea of Fertility. Yes, it's still in.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: And there's this big one...

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: We're getting ready to pass over Theophilus here, Pete. It's going to be right down at your lower 1 o'clock. That's a good picture, too.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: Lower 7 o'clock.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Yes, you - That's a beauty.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Oh, there it is.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: See it?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Yes.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: There's Theophilus.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: That one we were showing you a moment ago doesn't have a name, and it's - it's interesting just to the - behind that small one you were showing is sort of a whole streak of light-colored material that runs for hundreds of miles there and it's a different shape. Maybe it's just the elevation in that area; I don't know. It's near the central peak, so I'll use the monocular on it.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay, and...

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: [Garble] the central peaks in Theophilus.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Roger. We got them good in the screen, and we saw that large white ray as you switched windows there. The peaks of Theophilus [Pause.]

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: It's kind of interesting if you look right on - one thing about the peaks, I'm looking at them through the monocular; and, on the top of the peaks, you can see a great number of what appear to be boulders, and they must be huge to be visible from the altitude we're at right now.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay. Understand there are boulders on the tops of the peaks, and they look like some fairly well defined ridge lines in that central peak. Is that how they look through the monocular?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: That's right. That's right. That TV must be coming through real well, because from here it looks like very sharp ridge lines; and, if you look at either side of the ridge line, you can see sort of a terracing, a mild terracing effect that's parallel to the ridge line. It could be some form of something or - in fact, some sort of transportational mechanism there, I don't know what it is. Probably gravity. Obviously, you can see some - what would be termed rilles and [garble] running down from the ridge line. They're running perpendicular to it, more or less.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Roger. We're looking at [Pause.]

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: You ought to be able to look over to your side real far over there...

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: And them.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: ...and see the Sea of Serenity and some of those craters over in there. They ought to be pretty good contrast where that dark bar is. There any over there?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: There're plenty of them.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Yes, that ought - that might be interesting. Hey, there's some pretty good cracks over there.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Hey, look at that rille over there, Dick. Get -get that.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: We're going to change windows here. There's some beautiful rilles over in the other side, north side.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: I don't know, maybe we ought to try this one. Let me see. Can you see them out of that one better?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: Boy, that is beautiful. Oh!

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: [Garble] TV camera, I don't know. Where'd it go?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: There's some grabens over here, big long ones that come down the [Pause.]

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: [Whisper] Don't [garble] that.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: There's a very sharp crater you can see in the top left part of the screen right now. [Pause.]

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: In the view, we can see now, there appear to be a dark line running from the lower left up toward the top center. Can you make anything out of that?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Yes. That's what I'm trying to show you.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay. We're...

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Looks like some fair looks like some fairly deep rilles and droppings over there, particularly the ones that you ask about. They're very, very deep. There's a nice wide one over there, Pete. Can you see it? Over by that fresh impact with the raised rim?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Maybe you'd better take the camera in the other window.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: Over here?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Yes. Put if over there with Dick.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: 12, Houston. In that scene you just shifted from, there appeared to be two parallel rilles. You confirm that?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: That's - that's correct. As a matter of fact, in looking at it, there are two parallel rilles and then they actually pick up, well not quite a third one. It's like one ends on one side, and the middle one goes all the way through, and then one picks up on the right-hand side.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Roger. Understand. The picture's...

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: Well, there's two parallel grabens in this sea.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Also - also on that - that rille - one of the last things we saw and, Hous- or at the Cape when we talked with the geologist was the little experiment that the guy did blowing air through the sand, gases that - Sure enough I've got some examples of that right here in those trench-like structures. There's some crater chains running through them and alongside of them, just like we talked about...

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: We've got some examples. There's a big giant up here just blowing sand all over the place.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay, understand. Now, we can see - just a minute ago a - furrow or trench coming from the lower left side of the screen up toward the center and kind of ending in a string of rather poorly defined craters.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: Roger. There's one up here that's actually a double - double graben; it's not offset. There are two of them running parallel to each other.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Hey, Dick. You see the double craters right there? Do you see the grabens running alongside of them? And you. see the little string? It looks like a string of craters. Two sets of them. Can you give them that on the TV? I may get it out of this window. Wait a minute. Let me try the center window.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: 12, Houston. While you are setting up, how - how's the view out of your windows now?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Pretty much the same, Houston. Window number 5 is a good one, window number 4 is poor, window number 3, which is the hatch window, it's not -it's bad - it's still the same condition it was at launch. All of them are. But, because we've got a bright background instead of the dark background we had before, the marks on them aren't quite as noticeable.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay. We're getting very good pictures here.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Number 1 is by far the worst window. Number 2...

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay. This is up north. What you're seeing is - a rille here with a whole bunch of - looks like vent holes running along these rilles. Can you see those from the ground, Paul?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: That's affirm. We could see them before - You just moved off of what appears to be a rill moving to the right now. And we could see the...

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: [Garble] over on your side there, Dick. Yes. There's the - there's several - there's a whole bunch of areas in here, just looking out the window generally, that give you the feeling that, as we've talked about with the geologists, that some of this is volcanic action in here.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay. Now, we can see a crater just to the left of the screen there that's rather poorly defined and appears to be a good-sized rille or fracture running across the floor.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Hey, we've got the straight wall coming up on this side, Houston. When it gets a little bit closer, I'll show it to you. it's a beautiful straight line.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Very good.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Also, we've got a couple - here; let me borrow that thing, Dick, a minute.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Kind of ridiculous not to be taking pictures. [Pause.]

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: Is the camera over there, Al?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Yes. Wait a minute. I'll get it for you. Now, I don't know where he put it. Where'd you put the Hasselblad?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Can you see the straight wall now, Houston?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Yes, sir. We can see it very good. Just beyond that large crater was another smaller crater and its rim, and we can see the wall on beyond it.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: ...picture that. Does anybody know?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: You got this little chart right here. We've been - since the update, we've been here 56 minutes, so leave it 56 minutes, Data.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: I'm going to move off the straight wall, now, Houston, and look down at a crater. I don't have my chart here, so I don't know the name of it, but it's got extremely well defined terraced walls. It's got a nice central peak in the middle. And let me see if I can get it better for you. There it is.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Oh. Roger. We have a good one there, Al.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: And it also has a nice crack right down at the bottom.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Roger. We see that.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: That's a pretty impressive looking crater. We're in the terra now, and you can tell that the ground is much more hummocky and quite a bit rougher than the Mare which we're getting ready to approach in a few moments.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: Here's another one with a good central peak. In fact, this is one of the highest central peaks that - that's a hard one to show because the radar antenna of the LM partially eclipsing it. Can you see that central peak there?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: That's affirm. We're...

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: [Garble] high [garble].

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: We're getting a good...

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: It's almost as high as the rim itself. Okay. [Pause.]

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Sun's getting a lot lower now, as we approach the terminator...

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: I can see the terminator.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: ...things are much more in relief. Let me point the camera back past the straight wall again. Let me give you another view of that, because it's coming into even greater relief from this angle. Then, I'll go back and give you the horizon, because that's one of the most impressive things right here. Take a look at those mountains.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: We have them. [Pause.]

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: I'll move a little bit around and see if I can - here's some of those mountains we talked about earlier that look like, from the distance, like little clouds over the Mare. You can see how bright they are relative to the Mare surface; and, maybe even on the TV, they look like puffy clouds. However, they're not. They look like hard rock down there.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Roger. Understand they are not clouds.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: [Laughter].

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Got something out your window, Pete?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Too dark.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: It's getting dark. Boy. There's a high mountain right there on the horizon. I bet you - do you see that very high mountain on the horizon, Houston? It's about the center of the screen now. All you can see is reflected light.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Affirmative. We have it. 12, Houston. Can you open your f-stops any - get in this dim light?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: That will happen. We'll try it. [Pause.]

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: How's that look, Houston?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: That's better.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Sure looks better here. Here's an interesting feature down there that you're looking at near that large crater. The hole is - seems to be a general trending of ridges in this area, all in the same direction. They'd be running, I guess, on your camera from the top right-hand corner to the lower left. And it's particularly evident down there by the large crater that's in your picture.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Roger. We see that.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: There it is right - you see it?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: That's affirm.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Interesting. There's - I guess it's probably parallel to - let me show you some more of these clouds. I think you'll like them. They just seem to be large bumps on top of the Mare.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: Hey, let me show them Mosting over here, Al.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay. Here you go.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: Mosting is coming into view.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Yes.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: Schroter's Valley's up to the north.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: [Garble] temperature down.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: All right. Down.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: You can open it again, if you want it. It's the close one in. Boy, it's beautiful right in - look at that crater. Wowee.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: Straight wall pretty impressive in this light.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: Yes, that's a...

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: There you go, Houston.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Yes. We got it.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: I believe that's Mosting.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Roger.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: Mosting.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Now, it's starting to get a little dark outside.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay, whenever you get finished - whenever you get finished, there's a beauty over here, Dick. Whenever you get finished, there's a beauty over here. We're getting to where we get that low Sun angle; we can see those little craters within the big ones. I don't - I think they're probably in all of them; we just can't see them. There's the Sun in this one. It looks like it's somebody hit it with a bunch of buckshot right...

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: I wonder which - I wonder which one of those shadows down there is a 5-degree Sun Angle?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: I don't know. Go 5-degrees from the terminator.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Hello, 12; Houston. You just passed over 5-degree Sun angle on the surface.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay, that's what I was just trying to look at here and see what I could see.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: Boy, there's...

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Yes, there's some beauties over here. [Long pause.]

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: We got a beauty for you, Houston. Right in the terminator. See if I can run up the f-stop for you.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Okay, that's coming in good, Al.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Take a look at - down in that crater, the number of other small craters.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Roger. We see them.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: That's fantastic. Let me - soon as you look at that one, I'll show you the horizon; and near the terminator on the hori - distant horizon, you can easily see the curvature of the Moon, and you can also see the stark contrast between the horizon and the bright rocks and the dark crater. I'm moving over there now. There's the straight wall again.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: Hey Paul, all I can say, it's another fighter pilot's life: Hours and hours.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: [Laughter] Roger.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: How's that look, Houston?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: That's looking good, Al.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: That crater's a beauty out there. The rim is illuminated by the low Sun while, down inside the crater it's dark. And you can see the ray patterns from here, and you can see the mare surface. It almost looks like somebody took a - some cake icing and spread it with a big knife, laid it all around out there, and then somebody shot some BB's in it. It really is beautiful. It's got that layering all over it.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Mosting, and that [garble] up Schroter's Valley.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Got something over there? Let me hand it back to you. Okay. Now the [garble] down in the terminator. You ought to have Copernicus out there somewhere.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: You should see all that stuff that's on the window. That's why that window isn't any good for photography out of it. The Sun's really shining right on it now.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Roger. We can see all that stuff, Pete. However, we're getting a good picture through it in the open spaces.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: I guess Copernicus is too far out there to see, isn't it, Dick? Or can you see it?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: It's on the horizon. You can't even - yes. Guess we passed it a minute ago.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: That silly thing floating outside the window.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Where'd the Moon go?

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: There it is over there.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Oh.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Are we maneuvering some way? Now where'd that little piece of blue and gold stuff - whatever it is.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: Must be Mylar. No.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: Well, Houston, that looks like that's about it for this pass.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Roger, 12. Very good show.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_00_28.text: Boy, I'll tell you. You sure can't see anything on the other side of the terminator. That's black, too.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_084_00_28.text: Let's go off Vox now. [Long pause.]

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_00_28.text: Hello, 12; Houston. For information, all spacecraft systems are in excellent shape.

a12a_084_00_28.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_00_28.text: 12. Roger. Thank you.

a12a_084_35_43.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_35_43.text: 12, Houston. Map update when you're ready.

a12a_084_35_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_084_35_43.text: Just a second, Houston. Go ahead.

a12a_084_35_43.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_35_43.text: Hello, 12; Houston. On the ground, we're seeing some changes in signal strength, both up and down. Have you changed any of your communications modes recently?

a12a_084_35_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_35_43.text: You mean over the last few minutes or what?

a12a_084_35_43.speaker: Weitz
a12a_084_35_43.text: Yes, 12. Just in the last 5-10 minutes.

a12a_084_35_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_35_43.text: The only thing we've done is turn the TV off. Let me double cheek.

a12a_084_35_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_35_43.text: All the other Comm switches appear to be in the normal position, and the only thing we did was turn TV off.

a12a_084_35_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_084_35_43.text: Your Comm to us has been super.

a12a_085_03_46.speaker: Conrad
a12a_085_03_46.text: Roger-Roger. We're settled down to a nice meal, and we're allowing ourselves a little music on the tape recorder. And we'll see you on the other side.

a12a_085_03_46.speaker: Weitz
a12a_085_03_46.text: Okay, who won the vote on what you're playing on the tape recorder?

a12a_085_03_46.speaker: Conrad
a12a_085_03_46.text: We've been very democratic. We play a little bit of Al's, and a little bit of Dick's, and a little bit of mine.

a12a_086_28_52.speaker: Weitz
a12a_086_28_52.text: Okay, Pete, throughout the flight, your oxygen consumption has been slightly higher than previous flights, by approximately 10 percent. This is no problem, as extrapolating that to end of mission still gives us plenty of oxygen available. In an attempt to try to figure out why, though, we have a couple of questions, primarily with respect to your use of the URA. Approximately how long after use do you leave the cover valve in Vent before you close it? Over.

a12a_086_28_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_086_28_52.text: We usually keep it on until the O 2 High light comes on, which is a couple of minutes worth of venting.

a12a_086_28_52.speaker: Weitz
a12a_086_28_52.text: Okay, and what position do you - do you leave the cover valve and the waste management over-board drain valve when you're not using the URA?

a12a_086_28_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_086_28_52.text: Usually shut the dump valve, Off. Leave the cover in Vent.

a12a_086_28_52.speaker: Weitz
a12a_086_28_52.text: Roger, we got that. We will massage that, thank you.

a12a_086_28_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_086_28_52.text: Okay, we probably have used a little more oxygen through that, and we noticed on our plot that we were running a little low on oxygen, also.

a12a_086_50_51.speaker: Weitz
a12a_086_50_51.text: Hello, Apollo 12; Houston. You're rolling into the High Gain limits. Give me Omni Charlie, please.

a12a_086_58_59.speaker: Conrad
a12a_086_58_59.text: Roger. You can see quite well in Earth's shine, up here. The LM is illuminated very brightly because it's fairly reflective, but the Moon itself is fairly easy to see in earthshine; it's quite beautiful, real soft, and sort of gives it a greenish tinge, gray-green.

a12a_086_58_59.speaker: Weitz
a12a_086_58_59.text: Roger. Understand. And do you say that the LM is illuminated by earthshine?

a12a_086_58_59.speaker: Conrad
a12a_086_58_59.text: Yes. Real well. It's very reflective itself, and so it looks almost like the soft sunlight if there is such a thing. But you can, for example, look out and read the marks on the Commander's overhead window; you can see all the Quads, the struts. And real pretty up here in earthshine. Kind of gives it sort of a gray-green cast, though.

a12a_086_58_59.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_086_58_59.text: This is Apollo Control at 87 hours, 9 minutes. We're now 8 minutes away from Loss Of Signal. Here in Mission Control presently changing shifts. Flight director Pete Frank will be replacing flight director Glynn Lunney. The Capsule Communicator on this shift will continue to be astronaut Paul Weitz for the first part of the shift. Don Lind taking over at about 4:30 this morning. The Lunar Orbit Insertion number 2 maneuver scheduled to occur 39 minutes from now. That burn is targeted for an Orbit of 54 by 66 nautical miles. Time Of Ignition is tentatively set at 87 hours, 48 minutes, 47 seconds

a12a_087_12_10.speaker: Conrad
a12a_087_12_10.text: Okay, Houston. We just called up P40 for you to take a look at it before we disappear.

a12a_087_12_10.speaker: Weitz
a12a_087_12_10.text: Hello, Apollo 12; Houston. You're Go for LOI-2, and your PIPA's look real good.

a12a_087_12_10.speaker: Conrad
a12a_087_12_10.text: Roger, Houston. Go for LI - LOI-2.

a12a_087_12_10.speaker: Weitz
a12a_087_12_10.text: Yes, it's been a long night here, too.

a12a_088_01_31.speaker: Conrad
a12a_088_01_31.text: Hello, Houston; Apollo 12. LOI-2 burn complete. The burn was on time. The burn time was 17 seconds. The residuals were plus 0.3, 0, plus 0.1. Delta V c was minus 4.4, fuel 35.4, oxidizer 35.9, increase 110. We're in a 66.3 by 54.7 according to us. Over to you.

a12a_088_01_31.speaker: Conrad
a12a_088_01_31.text: And we have Bat B on the charger at this time.

a12a_088_01_31.speaker: Conrad
a12a_088_01_31.text: We're in the process of - Al is photographing off the target-of-opportunity chart here in order, and we're trying to get as much of that stuff done as we can.

a12a_088_09_24.speaker: Conrad
a12a_088_09_24.text: Okay, Houston; Apollo 12. We've gone to LM Press on our valve to bring the LM up.

a12a_088_09_24.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_088_09_24.text: That was spacecraft commander Pete Conrad reporting that their pressurizing the LM at this time."

a12a_088_09_24.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_088_09_24.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. We have had no contact with Apollo 12 for the last several minutes. However, Flight Director, Pete Frank, has gone around the room. consulting with his Flight Control personnel and all data appears quite nominal at this time. As Apollo 12 progresses on its third revolution around the Moon.

a12a_088_22_00.speaker: Weitz
a12a_088_22_00.text: 12, Houston. If you'll give us P00 and Accept, we'll give you a clock update.

a12a_088_22_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_088_22_00.text: Okay. P00 and Accept it is.

a12a_088_22_00.speaker: Weitz
a12a_088_22_00.text: And, 12; Houston. I have a map update PAD and a landmark tracking PAD, when you're ready.

a12a_088_22_00.speaker: Weitz
a12a_088_22_00.text: Okay. The map update for Rev 4. 89:13:09, 89:37:59, 89:59:18. Over.

a12a_088_22_00.speaker: Weitz
a12a_088_22_00.text: That's affirm. Are you ready for your landmark tracking PAD?

a12a_088_22_00.speaker: Weitz
a12a_088_22_00.text: Okay. And the computer's yours, and the H-1 PAD: T-1 is 90:35:41; T-2 90:40:50; the offset is 12 miles North. Over.

a12a_088_22_00.speaker: Conrad
a12a_088_22_00.text: Roger. Twelve miles North. Okay. 90:35:41, 90:40:50, and 12 North.

a12a_088_55_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_088_55_01.text: And if you have the DSKY or the torquing angles.

a12a_088_55_01.speaker: Gordon
a12a_088_55_01.text: Okay. I'm torquing at this time.

a12a_089_05_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_089_05_25.text: Roger. The tunnel's clear, and we're going into the LM.

a12a_090_00_34.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_00_34.text: Very good. Nice to hear your, voice.

a12a_090_00_34.speaker: Gordon
a12a_090_00_34.text: Roger. I answered you before. You must not have picked it up.

a12a_090_00_34.speaker: Gordon
a12a_090_00_34.text: That's okay. Pete and Al are in the LM - or Pete's in half and half, and they're going down through their checklist stuff, and I'm standing by ready to hear the P22.

a12a_090_00_34.speaker: Gordon
a12a_090_00_34.text: In fact - In fact, I want to go ahead [garble].You'll probably lose me on the high gain; I'll give you Omni B when I [garble].

a12a_090_00_34.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_00_34.text: And, Houston; 12. We just finished checking out our OPS's, and they checked out 40, both of them.

a12a_090_05_44.speaker: Bean
a12a_090_05_44.text: Roger. We're just standing by until time 90:30 where we do our Comm activation. Everything looks good in the LM. We've checked all the things we're supposed to, and they're all ship-shape, ready to go.

a12a_090_05_44.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_05_44.text: Roger. We're ready to go down here whenever you want to do the Comm checks.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_14_34.text: Houston, Apollo 12.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_14_34.text: Apollo 12, go ahead.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_14_34.text: Houston, Apollo 12.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_14_34.text: Apollo 12, go ahead.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_14_34.text: Roger. We're powering up LM Comm at this time starting with our voice check on VHF A with the CSM.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_14_34.text: Roger. You're coming in with a lot of background right now, Pete.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_14_34.text: Houston, Intrepid. How do you hear?

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_14_34.text: Read you well except for your background, which is very high.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_14_34.text: Roger.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_14_34.text: Yankee Clipper, Intrepid on VHF A. How do you hear?

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Gordon
a12a_090_14_34.text: Intrepid, Yankee Clipper. VHF A loud and clear. How me?

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_14_34.text: Read you the same. [Long pause.]

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_14_34.text: Yankee Clipper, Intrepid. How do you read VHF A.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Gordon
a12a_090_14_34.text: Intrepid, Yankee Clipper. VHF B loud and clear. How me?

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_14_34.text: Read you the same.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Gordon
a12a_090_14_34.text: Hey, that's really sterling. [Pause.]

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_090_14_34.text: That's Pete Conrad aboard Intrepid talking to Dick Gordon who is singularly manning the Yankee Clipper this time. We're at 90 hours, 17 minutes."

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_14_34.text: Houston - Houston, Intrepid. How's the S-Band Downvoice Backup and Low Bit Rate? Over.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_14_34.text: Intrepid, Houston. We're still reading you well except for your background, which is still high.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Bean
a12a_090_14_34.text: Okay. We're going to PCM High now. How do you pick it up?

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_14_34.text: Roger. Give us just a moment to reconfigure the site.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_14_34.text: Go ahead, Intrepid.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Bean
a12a_090_14_34.text: How's the Voice and High Bit Rate?

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_14_34.text: Roger. You're just the same, Pete. We're still reading you satisfactorily; again, you've got a lot of buzz in the background.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Gordon
a12a_090_14_34.text: Houston, this is Apollo 12. I'm talking to you on the CSM S-band, and Al's talking to you on the Intrepid S-band. Are you sure that that's not a ground problem? We're getting - Al's getting good reception up here on S-band with no noise.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_14_34.text: Roger. We'll check. [Pause.]

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Bean
a12a_090_14_34.text: Houston, Intrepid. Just went by on that [garble]. How do we look now?

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_14_34.text: You're somewhat weaker, but still readable. Still considerable background noise.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Bean
a12a_090_14_34.text: Roger. That's the way it should be.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Bean
a12a_090_14_34.text: Okay. How do you read now, Houston? Down Voice Backup Biomed, Low Bit Rate.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_14_34.text: Roger. Again, you're still somewhat weak, readable, and the background is dropping just slightly.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_14_34.text: [Garble] Intrepid.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Bean
a12a_090_14_34.text: Low Bit Rate with Biomed. How do you copy? Over.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_14_34.text: Read you very good on this one; your background has dropped considerably.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_14_34.text: Houston, we just went Telemetry High . How do you read us now, Voice?

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_14_34.text: Read you fine on this one, Pete.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Bean
a12a_090_14_34.text: And we are coming at you Telemetry Low and S-Band Range to Range. And will you copy the [garble] on hot mike?

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_14_34.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_090_14_34.text: That is Al Bean and Pete Conrad interchangeably coming on the line as we are under going a voice communication check.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_14_34.text: Intrepid, would you standby on this mode, so we can try a range acquisition?

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_14_34.text: Affirmative. [Long pause.]

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_14_34.text: Intrepid, Houston. How do you read?

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Bean
a12a_090_14_34.text: Loud and clear, Houston.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_14_34.text: Very good. Read you the same.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_14_34.text: Intrepid, Houston. We're...

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Bean
a12a_090_14_34.text: Did you pick up our range then?

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_14_34.text: That is affirmative. We finished that acquisition. Thank you.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Bean
a12a_090_14_34.text: Okay. And that completes our Comm checks. We're going to deactivate Intrepid and go back to Yankee Clipper.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_14_34.text: Very good. Thank you.

a12a_090_14_34.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_090_14_34.text: That was Al Bean, reporting that they've completed their communication check, they plan to depart Intrepid shortly and return to the Yankee Clipper. Moving somewhat ahead of the Flight Plan schedule. We're at 90 hours, 23 minutes now into the flight and this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a12a_090_28_20.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_28_20.text: Roger. Two items we'd like to get from you before you close that out and that's the OPS storage pressure and also the GET of activation of LM power.

a12a_090_28_20.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_28_20.text: Okay. I gave you the OPS; they're 5800 each and let me - and let me look in the book and find out what time we went on the LM power; just a second.

a12a_090_28_20.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_28_20.text: We went on LM power at 90:08:13.

a12a_090_32_26.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_32_26.text: We'd like you to confirm that you're going to pull the circuit breaker on the floodlights so that the light will go out when you close the refrigerator door.

a12a_090_32_26.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_32_26.text: Hey, Al - see these straps? I'm just going to leave them in here to do that job. They'll do it even better. Okay? We got plenty of those in the Command Module, don't we?

a12a_090_32_26.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_090_32_26.text: The reference there by Don Lind is a floodlight on the Lunar Module which did not turn off at the time of our first transfer to the LM by the two crewmembers. We're at 90 hours, 33 minutes now into the flight.

a12a_090_44_17.speaker: Gordon
a12a_090_44_17.text: Hello, Houston. Let me know when you've copied that.

a12a_090_44_17.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_44_17.text: What the hell we doing with all that roll in there?

a12a_090_44_17.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_44_17.text: Say again.

a12a_090_44_17.speaker: Gordon
a12a_090_44_17.text: Let me know when you've copied the P22.

a12a_090_44_17.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_44_17.text: Pretty well, I think.

a12a_090_44_17.speaker: Gordon
a12a_090_44_17.text: It's going to be easy to do.

a12a_090_44_17.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_44_17.text: Roger. We've got it. Thank you. [Pause.]

a12a_090_44_17.speaker: Bean
a12a_090_44_17.text: [Garble] really smoking over [garble].

a12a_090_44_17.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_44_17.text: Okay? He's getting Copernicus again, Al; he's rolling back.

a12a_090_44_17.speaker: Bean
a12a_090_44_17.text: Okay [garble].

a12a_090_44_17.speaker: Gordon
a12a_090_44_17.text: Houston, I'm going to look at the latitude and longitude from these marks.

a12a_090_44_17.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_44_17.text: You want to incorporate them in the state vector, wouldn't you say?

a12a_090_44_17.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_44_17.text: That's affirmative. We've got the data, Dick. You can proceed.

a12a_090_44_17.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_44_17.text: 2 o'clock.

a12a_090_44_17.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_44_17.text: Going to wind up in what attitude?

a12a_090_44_17.speaker: Gordon
a12a_090_44_17.text: 291 pitch. On this ball; let it go, just let it go.

a12a_090_44_17.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_44_17.text: 291; we're going the wrong way. We're going...

a12a_090_44_17.speaker: Bean
a12a_090_44_17.text: Yes...

a12a_090_44_17.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_44_17.text: ...all the way around.

a12a_090_44_17.speaker: Gordon
a12a_090_44_17.text: No. It'll stop and go back. Just let it go.

a12a_090_44_17.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_44_17.text: Take the roll out. What do you have?

a12a_090_53_18.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_53_18.text: Okay, Houston. We have you on the high gain, and I'll go to Accept at this time, and to wrap up to you with 91:11:37; 91:36:21; 91:57:45. The TEI-11 PAD SPS/G&N: 37358, minus 0.65, plus 0.94, plus - no - no, excuse me, it's just 105:23:55.20, plus 3192.1, plus 0725.8, minus 0139.8; NA, 107, NA; four jets, 11 seconds; undocked.

a12a_090_53_18.speaker: Lind
a12a_090_53_18.text: Roger. On Noun 48, the Y-trim was plus 049. All the rest was correct.

a12a_090_53_18.speaker: Conrad
a12a_090_53_18.text: Okay. That's what I have on the PAD. I don't know what I read back to you. I have 049, and how's the LM current look to you at this time?

a12a_090_53_18.speaker: Bean
a12a_090_53_18.text: Okay. We're in the process of buttoning the tunnel back up.[Long pause.]

a12a_091_00_30.speaker: Lind
a12a_091_00_30.text: We did not get your state vector completed before we lost you on the pitch there, so we'll continue that now.

a12a_091_00_30.speaker: Gordon
a12a_091_00_30.text: Roger. On this DAP load for the rest attitude, do you want me to use A-C per roll or B-D? Will you get the readings from G&C on that please? The Flight Plan or simulation.

a12a_091_00_30.speaker: Lind
a12a_091_00_30.text: Roger. We want to use B-D, Dick. Bravo Delta.

a12a_091_00_30.speaker: Gordon
a12a_091_00_30.text: Okay. Thank you. I thought so. [Long pause.]

a12a_091_00_30.speaker: Lind
a12a_091_00_30.text: Apollo 12, Houston. We're through setting up your state vector, and we'd like to try to get an E-dump before you go around the corner.

a12a_091_00_30.speaker: Conrad
a12a_091_00_30.text: And we have you out our window for the first time since we've been in lunar orbit. We've been too busy to get a look at you. Look pretty nice out there.

a12a_091_10_23.speaker: Lind
a12a_091_10_23.text: Apollo 12, Houston. We're about 1 minute from LOS here. We'll see you at 91:57.

a12a_091_10_23.speaker: Lind
a12a_091_10_23.text: Roger. So you can adjourn to the wardroom.

a12a_091_10_23.speaker: Conrad
a12a_091_10_23.text: Pretty soon we're going to have movies on the fantail.

a12a_091_10_23.speaker: Bean
a12a_091_10_23.text: [Laughter] We may not be good, but we can sure claim to be colorful.

a12a_091_10_23.speaker: Lind
a12a_091_10_23.text: So long. We'll see you coming around the other side.

a12a_091_10_23.speaker: Conrad
a12a_091_10_23.text: You've checked this, now? Verb 21 Noun 01, 32 55, Enter, 16; 16, Enter?

a12a_091_10_23.speaker: Conrad
a12a_091_10_23.text: That son of a bitch has gone all over the sky. It shot way past 291, the other direction.

a12a_091_10_23.speaker: Conrad
a12a_091_10_23.text: What kind of a deadband you got set?

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: Okay. I - I got minus - I got minus 1 and nothing. So forget it.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Intrepid, Houston. Looks good.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: How's the tube, Jerry?

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Real good, Dick. Real good.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: Okay.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: Okay, Dick. Yawing left, 60.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: Hey, Pete. You're cutting in end out to me.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: Roger. Go off Vox. [Pause.]

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: Pete, give me a radio check?

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: How do you read, Yankee Clipper?...

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: Okay.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: Pick up your yaw.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: How's that picture, Jerry?

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Clipper, Houston. The picture's beautiful.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: Quite a sight, isn't it?

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: It sure is, Dick. We're copying Pete's yaw maneuver now.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: Affirm. Just about got it completed.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: Okay, Dick. How do you read me?

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: Loud and clear now, Pete.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: All right. Pitching up 90.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Clipper, Houston. Your FM is breaking up on occasion.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: What - what's breaking up?

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Your FM is breaking up. It's looking good now. [Pause.]

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Intrepid, Houston. If you'll give us P00 and Data, we'll start your uplink.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: You're got it.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Roger. You're on the way, Pete.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: Hey, you look pretty nice over there, Yankee.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: Hey, Dick, you read me?

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Yankee Clipper, Houston. How do you read?

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: Houston, Clipper. Loud and clear.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Roger. Intrepid's on.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: Hey, Houston, tell him to turn off his Vox because he's cutting out his own VHF.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: Intrepid, Yankee Clipper. Say again.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: Okay. You were cutting out your own VHF, being on Vox. Your camera was keying it.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: Okay. I'm off of Vox now, and you're cutting out on me now.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: Okay. How's that?

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: Okay. That's better. Stay there. [Long pause.]

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: Okay. You've got it on me. I'm not going to touch anything again.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Bean
a12a_107_54_36.text: Yankee Clipper. I'll turn on my tracking light for a minute. See if you see it.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Intrepid, Houston with a DOI PAD.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: I've got it, Al. I've got your light.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Bean
a12a_107_54_36.text: Okay, this is Intrepid, Houston.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Okay. Standing by. [Long pause.]

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Bean
a12a_107_54_36.text: Go, Houston.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Yankee Clipper, Houston. Try pitch, minus 78; yaw, plus 225 on your high gain.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: Yes. That's where it's been, Jerry.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Roger. You're breaking up pretty badly. Intrepid, Houston. P30 LM maneuver DOI PAD: Noun 33, 109:23:39.41; Noun 81, minus 0070.8; all zeros, plus 0015.1; Noun 42, 0060.5, plus 0008.3, 0072.4; burn time, 0.29, 000, 297; AGS, minus 0070.9; plus all zips; plus 0014.4. The rest is NA. Over.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: That's affirmative, Al. Break. The computer's yours.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: Okay. Houston, is ...

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Bean
a12a_107_54_36.text: Okay. That's what I wanted to know. Thank you.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: Can't get any good pictures of you today, Dick. You - the Sun's not in the right place.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: Okay. We'll do it tomorrow.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Clipper, Houston.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Roger. Have you tried reacquisition on the High Gain? And if you have, why don't you try secondary transponder? Intrepid, Houston with a no PDI plus 12 PAD.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: Break, break, Houston. This is Intrepid. If it would be any help to you, Yankee Clipper's S-band antenna is just wandering - it's just oscillating back and forth in two directions, like it can't hold Lock.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Roger, Pete. Thanks.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Bean
a12a_107_54_36.text: It looks like it's in some sort of continual search mode.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Bean
a12a_107_54_36.text: Ready to copy the no PDI plus 12.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Roger, Al. Noun 33, 110:32:04.70; Noun 81, plus 0116.9, All zips, plus 0131.0; Noun 42, 0147.6,plus 0013.3, 0175.6; burn time 041, 000, 199; AGS, plus 0114.8, all zips, plus 0132.8; Noun 11, 111, 17, all zips; Noun 37, 112, 58, all zips. Over.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Bean
a12a_107_54_36.text: Roger, Houston. Copy. 110:32:04.70; plus 0116.9, all zips, plus 0131.0; 0147.6, plus 0013.3, 0175.6; 041, 000, 199; plus 01114.8, all zips, plus 0132.8; 111, 17, all zips; 112, 58, all zips.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: That's affirmative, Al. I've got your PDI PAD and your PDI is less than 10 and greater than 10.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Bean
a12a_107_54_36.text: Let her go, then.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Roger, Al. PDI T IG , 110:20:37.58; Noun 61, 09.42, minus 0004.9; FDAI, 356, 110, 000; DEDA 231 is plus 56960; PDI less than 10; Noun 37, 112:58:00.00; PDI greater than 10; Noun 37, 114, 57, 00.00. Over.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: That's affirmative, Al. I have T-2 for you now. [Pause.]

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Bean
a12a_107_54_36.text: Go.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Roger. T-2 abort. T IG ; 110:42:02.00; Noun 37, 116, 56, all zips; T-2 at PDI plus 21 minutes, 25 seconds. Over.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Roger. T-3, if you're ready?

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Bean
a12a_107_54_36.text: We are ready.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Roger. T-3 T IG ; 112:27:42.00; P22 acquisition at 112:25:00. Break. Yankee Clipper, you are coming on loud and clear on the TV now.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: Roger. I had to go to Manual on my High Gain. It won't stay locked on.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: It's nice and steady over there, now, Dick. I guess something went wrong with the Auto track.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: Yes. It's because I'm in Manual that I'm staying in there now.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: Yes. It's pretty solid. It just wobbles a little bit when you fire a thruster.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Bean
a12a_107_54_36.text: Readback, Houston, is 112:27:42.00; 112:25:00.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: That's affirmative, Al. Clipper, Houston. Did you try the secondary transponder before you went to Manual?

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: That's affirmative.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Roger.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Intrepid, Houston. I have your gyro torque angle.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: It must be something in the Auto lock mechanism.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: Hold it just a minute. We'll be right with you.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Okay. Standing by. [Long pause.]

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Bean
a12a_107_54_36.text: Go ahead, Houston. Ready to copy.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Roger. Your LM gyro torque angles: X, minus 00045; Y is minus 00035; Z is minus 00092. Over.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Bean
a12a_107_54_36.text: Roger. Copy. Minus 00045, minus 00035, and minus 00092.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Affirmative. Break. Clipper, Houston with a map update, Rev 14.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: Okay, go, and I copied all the other.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Affirm.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: And I'm standing by for Sep.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Roger, Dick. [Long pause.]

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: Say, Houston, the SIM went pretty smooth today.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Affirmative, Pete.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Bean
a12a_107_54_36.text: Looks like, because of your tracking, Dick, they raised their landing site altitude about 2,400 feet.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: That's not hard to believe, Al. Looked like it was in a hole to me.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: And, Houston, I guess you saw the landing radar self-test. That came out 40.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Roger, Pete. We copy that.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Intrepid, Houston. We'd like to get your value on transmitter power, on that.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Bean
a12a_107_54_36.text: Okay. Wait 1. They were both 3.6.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Roger. Copy.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: Actually - actually the velocity Xmitter was 3.62, and the altitude Xmitter was 3.60.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: Houston, Yankee Clipper.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Go ahead, Clipper.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Gordon
a12a_107_54_36.text: I'll go back to primary transponder, here, as soon as we separate [garble] hasn't helped it a bit. Looks like I've lost the Auto track feature in the high gain.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: Roger, Dick. We concur on that.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: Dick, you're - we're still in secondary servo's there. You might go back to the primary ones.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Carr
a12a_107_54_36.text: All right, Conrad. You're stealing our thunder now.

a12a_107_54_36.speaker: Conrad
a12a_107_54_36.text: Okay. Just trying to help out.

a12a_108_19_42.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_19_42.text: Clipper, Houston. Are you going to try those primary servo electronics?

a12a_108_19_42.speaker: Gordon
a12a_108_19_42.text: It's been tried. How's it looking?

a12a_108_19_42.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_19_42.text: Yes. The antenna's not moving around at all. It appears to be locked on tight.

a12a_108_19_42.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_19_42.text: Clipper, Houston. Are you in Auto now?

a12a_108_19_42.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_19_42.text: Forget it, Dick. Go back to Manual.

a12a_108_19_42.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_19_42.text: Roger. We copy your Auto, Dick. You're better off in Manual.

a12a_108_19_42.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_19_42.text: Is it still in Auto, Dick? It is just locked up solid if it is.

a12a_108_19_42.speaker: Gordon
a12a_108_19_42.text: I can move around in here pretty good when I've got all this room.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: This is one of the better visuals I've seen, Dick.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Gordon
a12a_108_22_25.text: Yes. You are right. I've been taking stills, and I let it get out of view of TV. I got to get you back.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: I got you 1 minute and 40 seconds ...

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: Mark.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: ...to Sep. [Pause.]

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_22_25.text: Clipper, Houston. You're Go for Sep.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Gordon
a12a_108_22_25.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_22_25.text: Intrepid, Houston. Give us a mark with 1 minute to go to Sep, would you?

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: It is already 1 minute. I'll give you one at 45 seconds. [Pause.]

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: Mark.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: Forty-five seconds. [Long pause.]

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: You concur with that, Yankee Clipper?

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Gordon
a12a_108_22_25.text: I don't have average g yet, Pete.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: Okay. I - I may have copied the time down wrong or something.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: Okay; 42. I got 22 [garble] time.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Gordon
a12a_108_22_25.text: Average g is on. Average g.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: Very good.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Gordon
a12a_108_22_25.text: I'll be watching you.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: Okay. We'll be looking for you, too. Okay, there he goes. He's burning. [Long pause.]

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_22_25.text: Intrepid, Houston. You were off on that figure by 20 seconds. CSM was right.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_22_25.text: Yes. I had the wrong time. He's burning now, and he looks good out there.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_22_25.text: Roger.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Gordon
a12a_108_22_25.text: Burn's complete.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: By-by.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Gordon
a12a_108_22_25.text: See you, troops. [Long pause.]

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_22_25.text: Clipper, Houston. You can terminate average g now.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Gordon
a12a_108_22_25.text: It's done. It's done.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: Okay, Houston. We're in Update Link for you any time you want to send this state vector.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_22_25.text: We'll be ready in about 3 minutes, Pete.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: Okay, and meanwhile, I'm going to take the computer. Give me a holler when you're ready.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_22_25.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: Boy, do you look neat down there against the Moon, Dick.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: We're taking them. We're taking them. [Long pause.]

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: Dick, do you want to get your transponder on?

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_22_25.text: Clipper, Houston. Try Omni Bravo.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Bean
a12a_108_22_25.text: They want Omni Bravo. [Long pause.]

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Gordon
a12a_108_22_25.text: Hello, Houston.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_22_25.text: Clipper, Houston. Loud and clear.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Gordon
a12a_108_22_25.text: Still have the TV on the Omni?

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_22_25.text: That's negative, Clipper.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Gordon
a12a_108_22_25.text: Okay. I'll secure it.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_22_25.text: Clipper, Houston. Would you check your Delta-V CG switch to CSM?

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Gordon
a12a_108_22_25.text: CSM. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Gordon
a12a_108_22_25.text: Intrepid, Clipper going to Duplex B and Ranging.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: Okay. We're not ready for you yet, but you can go ahead there, and we'll come up in a minute. Okay. We're coming up now.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Gordon
a12a_108_22_25.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Gordon
a12a_108_22_25.text: Okay. Loud and clear, but let me get locked on. Don't talk to me for a minute.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: Are you ready with that updata link yet, Houston?

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_22_25.text: That's affirmative, Pete. Go P00 and Data.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: You got it. P00 and Data.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_22_25.text: Roger, Intrepid; Houston. We got another delay. It'll be another minute before we can start it up. [Pause.]

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_22_25.text: Intrepid, Houston. It's on its way. [Long pause.]

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_22_25.text: Intrepid, Houston. You ready for your data?

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: Yes. Go ahead.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_22_25.text: Okay. It's on the way.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Gordon
a12a_108_22_25.text: I got you at 0.2 of a mile. [Pause.]

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Gordon
a12a_108_22_25.text: Pete, I show you locked on with the radar.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: Okay. I got Auto track. [Long pause.]

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: For some reason, we show a great deal out of plane. [Pause.]

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_22_25.text: Intrepid, Houston. The computer is yours. Break. Clipper Houston. If you'll go P00 and Accept, we've got your uplink.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Gordon
a12a_108_22_25.text: Okay. It's all yours.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_22_25.text: Roger, Clipper. It's on the way. [Long pause.]

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: Okay. I hold you at 1.3 - No, excuse me, Dick. I'm looking at the wrong register; 0.22 at about 3 feet per second.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Gordon
a12a_108_22_25.text: I've got it - I've got you at 0.2526 on the VHF.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: And the tapemeter looks good? [Long pause.]

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_22_25.text: I also show you going a good ways out of plane to me for some reason.

a12a_108_22_25.speaker: Gordon
a12a_108_22_25.text: I've got the same thing myself. I don't understand it. Coming - think I'm coming back a little, though.

a12a_108_42_25.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_42_25.text: Intrepid, Houston. We're copying your P40.

a12a_108_42_25.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_42_25.text: Dick, I'm going to start my yaw maneuver in a minute.

a12a_108_44_44.speaker: Bean
a12a_108_44_44.text: Houston, Intrepid. How do you think the AGS and PGNCS compare?

a12a_108_44_44.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_44_44.text: Intrepid, Houston. You're PGNCS and AGS look real good.

a12a_108_48_31.speaker: Gordon
a12a_108_48_31.text: Are you copying my gyro torquing angles? [Long pause.]

a12a_108_48_31.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_48_31.text: Clipper, Houston. We've got them now.

a12a_108_52_34.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_52_34.text: Intrepid, Houston. LOS is coming up in 4 minutes. [Pause.]

a12a_108_52_34.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_52_34.text: Okay. We'll try and have this alignment finished for you, so you can look at it.

a12a_108_52_34.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_52_34.text: Here's a star-angle difference, Houston. Four balls 2 coming at you with the torquing angles.

a12a_108_52_34.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_52_34.text: How's that grab you? Are you looking at the DSKY?

a12a_108_52_34.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_52_34.text: Those are great. You're Go for DOI. [Pause.]

a12a_108_52_34.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_52_34.text: And, Clipper; Houston. We're looking for your AOS at 109:41.

a12a_108_55_58.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_55_58.text: Intrepid, Yankee Clipper. You're looking good. One minute to LOS; we'll see you on the other side.

a12a_108_55_58.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_55_58.text: Yes, sir; and after all that jazz about the LPD, old Aldebaran is a half a degree off of in yaw and a half a degree off of in pitch, which is in the noise level; and I can see it out the window; no strain.

a12a_108_55_58.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_55_58.text: Okay, it's 1 degree off. Forget it.

a12a_108_55_58.speaker: Bean
a12a_108_55_58.text: You want to mark it; you want to mark it with this thing right here?

a12a_108_55_58.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_55_58.text: No, hell no; I know where it is.

a12a_108_55_58.speaker: Bean
a12a_108_55_58.text: All right, babe. Get some lights in this thing.

a12a_108_55_58.speaker: Carr
a12a_108_55_58.text: Intrepid, Houston. Is that in relation to your new mark or the old one?

a12a_108_55_58.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_55_58.text: No. That's right around the 40 mark. It's off about three quarters of a degree to the right and about a tenth of a degree down in pitch.Beautiful. Not even worth fooling with.

a12a_108_55_58.speaker: Bean
a12a_108_55_58.text: Okay. Now wait a minute. Where was I?

a12a_108_55_58.speaker: Conrad
a12a_108_55_58.text: Hey, Dick, go ahead and start catching my data, babe.

a12a.1140206.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1140206.text: Houston; Intrepid. In case you want to know where we are. We'll be with you with the PLSS comm checks in just about 2 (or) 3 minutes.

a12a.1140206.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1140206.text: Roger. Intrepid. Standing by. [Long Comm Break. They are on Surface 28 in the checklist and will start the comm check at about 114:08. The PLSS comm check begins 39 minutes before the planned start of the final depressurization. This would get them out at about 114:47, only 27 minutes behind the planned time. They will actually get out at about 115:08 - about 48 minutes late - with the additional loss primarily due to problems they have yet to experience with the comm system. Gerry Griffin is the EVA Flight Director. The NASA Public Affairs commentator optimistically notes, paraphrasing Griffi

a12a.1140206.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1140206.text: Roger, Intrepid. Standing by. (Long Pause) [At Pete's next utterance, we will pick them up in the middle of the section "Audio (CDR)" on the right-hand column of page Surface-28 . CDR is "Commander". VOX is the voice-activated comm mode. Note that only Pete is audible. After he changes some switch settings on his audio panel, Al will reset switches and circuit breakers on his side.]

a12a.1140206.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1140206.text: (Mode) VOX and full increase on the sensitivity. All right; wait a minute. Wait a minute. VHF A - I know - VHF A, Transmit. VHF B, Receive. (Starting Al's audio) Audio LMP: S-Band to T/R; ICS to T/R; Relay On; Mode VOX; VOX Sens(itivity), Max; VHF A, Transmit/Receive; VHF B, Receive.

a12a.1140206.speaker: Conrad

a12a.1142756.text: Okay. [Jones - "SRC is the Sample Return Container, the rock box."] [Conrad - "That must be the area in which we were going to stow them when we got them. The boxes were outside on the MESA."]

a12a.1142756.text: Okay. (Pause) Here it comes.

a12a.1142756.text: Okay. (Pause)

a12a.1142756.text: A little chill down.

a12a.1142756.text: Yeah, leave it on for a second. (Long Pause)

a12a.1142756.text: That it?

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: That's it.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: Okay.

a12a.1142756.text: (Reading) "CB(16), ECS LCG pump (breaker), open"

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: Open. [CB(16) (Circuit Breaker panel 16) is on Al's side of the cabin, at his right shoulder. Panel 11 is in the corresponding position on Pete's side of the cabin.]

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: "Disconnect (LM water hoses)." Let me disconnect yours.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: Okay. (Pause)

a12a.1142756.text: Okay. Just a second; let me get yours. (Pause) Okay; just hold that a second.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: In?

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: It's in, babe.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: Okay; thank you. Hang on to your (LM) water hose, here. (Pause) No; your right hand. That a boy.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: Okay. (Pause) Now, rotate...

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: Huh? (Pause) It's in.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: (Did the) locks go in?

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: Yes, sir.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: Okay.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: Both locks are in.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: Okay, let's stow these (LM) hoses. Just a second. (Pause) You've got to route yours up there on the wall.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: Yeah. [The LM oxygen and water hoses come to them from the ECS cabinet behind Al's station and they are stowing the hoses out of the way on the forward face of the cabinet.]

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: While you're doing that, I'll get this in.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: I'm afraid I can't do it with you standing there. I'm going to have to wait until you turn around.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: Okay.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: Get yours in there.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: Okay. (Pause) [A portion of the dialog is lost under a Public Affairs statement about Dick Gordon's sighting of the LM on the northwest rim of Surveyor Crater.]

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: (Garbled) back off into your corner.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: Okay. (Pause)

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: Can I get up on the step a little bit?

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: Yep. (Long Pause) [Pete is probably referring to the decking that surrounds the ascent engine cover. This midsection deck is eighteen inches above the cabin floor where the astronauts stand and the front part of the midesection deck - and the transition between the two areas - is called the midstep . The front part of the decking on Pete's side of the cabin is clear and, with the suits still unpressurized, he may be talking about partly sitting or kneeling on the midstep so he can reach across to the ECS cabinet. In stowing the hoses on the front of the ECS cabinet, Pete is going to try to rea

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: Can you hold these (LM water) hoses?

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: Sure. (Long Pause)

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: Turn around.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: Okay. (Long Pause)

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: I wonder if I need to get the water (hoses?) in there? Maybe you could do that.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: Okay.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: Everything else is in.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: Will do it.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: Wait a second. Got it.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: Okay. (Long Pause) You got the window heater on over there? Pete?

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: No. I'll have to wait until you turn around. (Pause) How you doing over there?

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: Good. Just about got it done.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: Okay. I'll turn on your window heater in just a second.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: All right; that's it.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: Get in your corner again. (Pause)

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: Okay.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: I don't know about you, but my suit is collapsing around me. How about you?

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: That's right.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: Huh?

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: Yeah; so's mine. Cabin pressure must have pumped (up) a little. [They have their helmets on but haven't turned on the PLSS O2. Later crews ascribed the collapse of the suits during this phase of the EVA preparations to breathe-down. That is, they are using up the oxygen in the suits and, as they exhale carbon dioxide, it is being removed by the lithium hydroxide canisters. The net result is a pressure drop in the suits which, consequently, are being squeezed around them by the cabin pressure. In 1991, Al speculated that the suit collapse might, instead, have been due to any increase in cabin p

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: It (the window heater)'s the last breaker in the upper left.

a12a.1142756.speaker: LM Crew
a12a.1142756.text: Okay.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: Now,...

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: (Reading) "Verify..."

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: (Reading) "Don EV gloves"...Wait a minute. [They already have their gloves on. Al is at the right place in the checklist, at the beginning of the last paragraph on Sur-30 . Pete is on the top of the next page. Readers should note that, as per Sur-21 , Pete and Al are using a cue-card version of the checklist which they have mounted on the panel in front of them. It has a different layout from the book form reproduced here.]

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: (We're) right here (in the checklist).

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: Mine's okay.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: All O2 connectors locked.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: Check mine; I'll check yours. (Pause) I'll look at yours again. (Pause) It's locked; that one's locked. It's locked. They're vertical. And that diverter valve's vertical.

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: Yes, sir; your diverter valve's vertical. Everything looks locked here. (Pause) [As shown in Figure I-23 in the EMU Handbook , the diverter valve is part of the oxygen inflow connector. The valve has two positions. In the Open (horizontal) position, used in the cabin, all the incoming oxygen stream is divided between a duct leading to the helmet vent and a duct leading the vents in the torso. In the Closed (vertical) position, used outside, all the oxygen goes to the helmet vent. Figure I-10 from the EMU Handbook shows the layout of the ducts.]

a12a.1142756.speaker: Bean
a12a.1142756.text: (Garbled) Make sure the water lock is in. Is the water lock in?

a12a.1142756.text: You don't have a lock on your water...(garbled)

a12a.1142756.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1142756.text: Okay.

a12a.1142756.text: I think we ought to get over here (on the cue card) where we turn on the oxygen.

a12a.1142756.text: (Garbled)

a12a.1142756.text: PLSS O2 on. (Pause)
