a12a.1180736.text: Get it? Push it over here and I'll get it. (Pause) Push her over here. (Pause) (Garbled) [It sounds like Al is leaning on a larger rock while Pete pushes the rock over to him with either his boot or the tongs. He may be presenting his saddlebag so that Al can put the sample in without having to get up. Bailey and Ulrich speculate that, here, Pete and Al are collecting sample 12016, a 2 kilogram piece of basalt. Certainly such a rock would have been too big for the tongs but not too big for Al to have picked up with one hand.]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Drop it in my (saddle) bag.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay. You got anything else you want to put in your bag? Go ahead and push another one over here.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Okay, in just a minute.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay. Get a couple of big ones.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Oh, I wish that we could get that, Al.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Try that one. That's a good one.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Huh?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: A couple of nice ones right here. (Pause)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Wait a minute. (Garbled)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: There you go.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Oops. (Pause)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Wait a minute.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Here; let's just get this real good one.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Yeah.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay. We're getting you some of this rock, Houston. Hope it's (garbled)...

a12a.1180736.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1180736.text: Roger, Pete and Al. We copy. We suggest you start smoking on back there. You're 3:13 and I'd like you back there in 4 minutes. 118:21:21 Conrad: Okay. We're on our way. Let's go, Al. [They may actually start back at this point.]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Hey, Pete?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Yeah.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Let me ask you something.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: What?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: What...

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Huh?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: That's interesting, isn't it?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: What?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: I was looking at that rock perched right over on top of the hill, there.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: (Garbled) my distance here, because there's nothing but...

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Here.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: ...all the same. Yeah.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: You got it, babe. (Pause)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Must have been 1200 (to) 1300 feet, huh?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: At least.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: At least. [It is not clear what distance they are estimating. Their distance from the LM and the diameter of Middle Crescent Crater are both about 1000 feet.]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: You could travel a lot further than that, you know it?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Yeah. 118:21:55 Bean: You could really make a long traverse if you had a good long-term OPS. [Al is talking about the walkback constraint.]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: What do you figure my strides are? Ten feet?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Oh, I'd say (that) each step you're only going about... When you're running normal, I'd say you go about 3 or 4 feet. But you could just go indefinitely at this pace.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Yeah.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: You don't get tired! Pete, if you land flat-footed and then you just push off your toes and on you go. (Pause) [Bean - "We were loping along and it seemed like, because there was so much time between each step, that you were leaping great lengths."] [Conrad - "Turned out it was about six feet (per stride), wasn't it?"] [Bean - "I remember dropping back and watching Pete run. We were running together and I dropped back. 'Cause I felt like I was doing it, too, (that is, getting ten feet per stride). And then I watched him and his feet marks were really 3 or 4 feet apart, instead of this ten feet

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: (Chuckling as they run)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: This is fun!

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Yeah.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Well, we got that ALSEP up. (Pause)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: (Garbled) this rock box, I get some more rocks! Turned us all around and we didn't get any rocks! (Pause)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Let's get some up here. We'll fill it.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Just a minute. (Pause) Hey, Houston. We're approaching the ALSEP, headed back to the LM. [They sound a little winded. Their heart rates are a bit over 150. Since leaving Middle Crescent Crater, they have been running for 1 minute and 40 seconds and, if they were actually at the ALSEP, the distance from their stopping point on the rim of Middle Crescent would be 190 meters and their average running speed 6.8 km/hr. However, based on the experience of the J-mission crews - who had the advantage of a more flexible suit - this estimate is implausible and, as indicated by the dialog over the next t

a12a.1180736.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1180736.text: Roger, Pete. We copy. (Pause)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: (Garbled)...

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: (Garbled) run all the way.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Hey, Pete?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Yeah.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Ease over this way a little.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Which way?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Over toward your left.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: What you want to do?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: I thought there were a couple of good rocks over there.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Where? (Pause)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Be about half way... Why don't we grab a couple of rocks here? 118:23:26 Conrad: All right. Here's one right here.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay. Let me get a photograph of it.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Hurry.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: We're on the way. Coming? [That is, they can get the sample without detouring.] 118:23:38 Bean: Okay. Here's a good one. (Pause) Wait a minute. (f/)8. (Pause) (I'll) step in and get the picture.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Got it? 118:23:49 Bean: Got it. (Pause while Pete gets the sample) There you go. Good boy. (Pause) [Al's photo is AS12-47- 6940 .]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Okay. (Pause) Here's another good one. Forget the picture. [On tape, Pete's last statement sounds like "Better get the picture". Evidently, Al heard it that way, too.]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay. You're in the shadow. Step back just a little. [Evidently, Pete is standing up-Sun of the rock and his shadow is falling on it. Al wants him to step back and get his shadow out of the way. The problem with shadows is best illustrated by photos Pete took at Sharp Crater starting at 132:56:44 : AS12-49- 7263 to 7277.]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: I said forget the picture.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1180736.text: Pete and Al, we're picking up your heavy footprints going by the seismometer.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: That's great.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Hey, Pete.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Yeah. 118:24:27 Bean: Let's get one last shot of this thing (the smaller of the two mounds).

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: You could... Look, I got to get going on the rock box, Al.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Oh, okay; let's go. (Pause) [If they are really near the small mound, they have run about 150 meters and, with a minute subtracted for the sample stop, they have been running for about 2 minutes. That would imply a plausible speed of 4.5 km/hr.]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Go ahead and get one more. Aghh! (Pause) Boing! I feel like Ebenezer Scrooge - or something - whistling across the plain. [Scrooge is, of course, the central character in Charles Dickens' A Christmas Carol The reference here may be to Scrooge's journey with the Ghost of Christmas Present, speeding through the air over moor and sea.]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Boy, there's a lot of that glass here.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Yep. Okay. We're (within) about 300 feet of the LM now, Houston.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1180736.text: Roger, Pete. We copy. 118:25:03 Conrad: (Garbled) full gallop. There's a good rock. Halt, halt, halt! Look at that! [Bean - "Pete was telling himself stop, more than me, because he was going by it."]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: I swear there's a...

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Never saw one like that before. Look at that! (Pause)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: That green?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: What is it? (I) see it.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: No, it was grinning at me. That's why I stopped.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: The heck with it. Put it in the rock bag.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Let's go.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Yes, sir. 118:25:23 Bean: Okey-doke. (Pause) [Based on Pete's comment about the green color, Bailey and Ulrich speculate that this rock is either 12006 , a 200-gram piece of olivine basalt, or 12020 , a 300-gram piece. During the second EVA, Pete and Al will put most of the samples in individually numbered bags and, consequently, there is little doubt as to which sample is which. For this first EVA - and especially for samples such as this one for which there are no documentation photographs - unambiguous identification is all but impossible. The rock they are collecting here has to be one of

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: (Laughs) Here, let's pick up a couple of these. 118:25:32 Bean: Okay. (Pause) Hey, real good. They're a little different. They're more the gabbro type. [A gabbro is a relatively coarse-grained basalt, with the large crystals indicative of relatively slow cooling at the base of a lava flow. This is one of the few instances where Pete and Al use a technical geology term.]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Yeah. Yeah, that's... (Pause) Wait a second.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Wait a second. (Pause) [Jones - "I gather that you went on geology field trips intermittently through the years. Did those intensify in any way after you got assigned to 12 or did they get dropped?"] [Conrad - "The only thing I remember we did for 12 was go to Hawaii at the end."] [Bean - "After the assignment to 12, they became more field exercises. Before 12, it was general geology field trips, where you went out and looked at outcropping and contacts and talked about them and tried to decided whether this one was older than that and that sort of stuff. After (the assignment to) 12, the only

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Thank you. Let's go.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: What I hate to see is an LMP laying on the lunar surface. (Pause) [Bean - "I think, maybe, I could have fallen down here. I fell down a couple of times. And I think maybe it was here. And I never fell down flat. I was always able to turn around and land on my hands and then push up."] [Conrad - "You go down and you go right back up."] [Bean - "So maybe this is where it was; and you were watching."] [Jones - "What I've seen in the TV of the later missions is that, once you get on your hands and knees, you just push off with your hands and basically rotate your PLSS back so your center of gravit

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Son of a gun! I got to have that. Look at that. A pure bead of glass! See that?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Yup. Grab it. (Pause)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: (To himself) Oh, come on! (To Al) Hold my hand.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay. (Pause) [Bean - "I'm probably holding Pete's hand and he's leaning over and he picks something up and then I pull him back upright. It's real quick that way; you don't have to get out the tongs and all that other stuff. You just do it real quick."]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Oh, I'm losing it. (Pause)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Got it. [Bean - "It was more tiring to lean over than it was to run."]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Pure glass or something, huh?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: It's one of those black beads, only different. It's about...

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: It looks green to me. Okay.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: ...three-eighths of an inch in diameter...

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: (Breathing heavily) Here's our old, friendly Intrepid. (Pause) [At 118:15:37 as they were approaching the rim of Middle Crescent Crater, Ed told them they had to be back at the LM in ten minutes. Despite the number of times they stopped to sample, they are only a minute 'late'. Ed gave them reminders at 6 minutes and four minutes remaining.] 118:27:04 Conrad: Okay. What do I got to do here? (Pause) [Now that they are back at the LM, Pete will stow his camera in the ETB for transfer up to the cabin, stow the hammer , the tongs, and the extension handle on the HTC for use during EVA-2, unstow a

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay...

a12a.1180736.speaker: LM Crew
a12a.1180736.text: (Garbled) 118:27:12 Conrad: I'll tell you something you can do.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Take the pan photographs again. I took them at 15 feet (focus instead of 74), I think, by mistake.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: And I'll get the rock box out.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: All right. Real good.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Hey, Houston. We're back at the LM.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1180736.text: Roger, Al... (correcting himself) Pete. We copy. After you get finished with the core tube, Al, we'll have some instructions for you with the TV. 118:27:35 Bean: Sounds good. Okay. Pete, where are the tongs for a moment?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: The tongs are on the MESA.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: (Working at the MESA, getting the rock box out of its storage slot) There you are.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: I'll bring 'em back. Now, which pans do you want me to take? Over here?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: No, the... Yeah. Front and over on the left and (right) rear. [These are retakes of the pans Pete took starting at about 116:22. They were taken at roughly the 12 o'clock (west), 4 o'clock, and 8 o'clock positions about 20 feet out from the LM.] [Brian McInall has created a planimetric map for EVA-1 Close-out activities , including these three pans.]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Sixteen (frames per pan)? Or twelve each or...

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Yeah, take 15.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay. Will do. I'll take them again. (Pause) I'm going to take a few pans first, Houston, if that's okay. It'll take about an additional 3 minutes. (Pause)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: (Possibly having trouble getting his camera off his RCU ) Hey, Al.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Yes, sir.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Never mind. Wait a minute. I think I'm getting it. (Pause) No, I got it. 118:28:21 Bean: Okay. (Long Pause) [Pete's breathing is much more audible in this section than usual, in part because he has his head forward in the helmet so that he can see the camera bracket.] [Bean - "He's leaning over and he's breathing a little harder than he ever was running. It's a lot more trouble to bend the suit than it was just to run along. And it's hard to get the camera off the suit."] Al's 12 O'Clock Pan (frames 6941 to 6960 )

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: One camera in the ETB. (Long Pause)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: That Surveyor sure looks neat sitting on the side of that crater. Pretty steep walls down there. (Long Pause) 118:29:43 Conrad: Not going to have any trouble sleeping tonight. [Conrad - "And I'm saying 'I'm not going to have any trouble sleeping tonight' because it's been a long day. Remember, we got up in the Command Module, so we've been (awake) 17-18 hours right now, probably (actually 17.5 at this point). A lot of time."]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: (Agreeing with Pete) Don't think so. Okay, let me go get the other two pans, Pete. Be finished in a minute. (Pause)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Okay. (Reading his checklist) Stow 70 millimeter (camera in the ETB), the hammer (on the HTC)...

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Hey; stop it, handle. [The handle assembly on Al's camera may be coming loose. During the second EVA, the thumb wheel on his camera will fall out entirely shortly before they make their way into Surveyor Crater, forcing them to make do with one camera.]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Getting it right now. (Pause) (Struggling with the SRC?) Good night Godfrey. (Garbled) (Pause) [Pete is speaking subvocally. "Good night, Godfrey" could be a substitute for a more colorful word choice.]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Okay, SRC (Sample Return Container or rock box) number 1 coming out. (Pause)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Another pan here. Get up (on) a higher place.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Say again? 118:30:43 Bean: Oh. I was (standing in a low spot and was) too low for the pan. (Pause) Okay, this is a good spot, I think. (Long Pause) Al's 6 O'Clock Pan (frames 6961 to 6981 )

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: (Subvocal, to the rock box) Come on.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay. That's it for the pans, Pete.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Okay. One rock box open.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay, one more set (of pictures) to go.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Okay.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: I've got this bag of rocks on me, here. Want me to bring them to you in a minute? 118:32:03 Conrad: Well, I'm having trouble over here with the rock-box holders. [The MESA is equipped with an elevated "table" which has latches to hold the SRC in place while Pete removes the core tubes and other gear and then stows the rocks. He is having trouble getting the rock box latched into place.] [Conrad, from the 1969 Technical Debrief - "The sample return container worked as advertised. I do want to comment here that I feel the practice we did on the K-bird (a Boeing KC-135 aircraft flying repeated pa

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay. If you have a little trouble, I can help you with it.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Yeah. This rock box keeps wanting to go up in the air. (Pause) Nope. The heck with it. I ain't got time to mess with it. (Pause, taking the scale out of the rock box) One scale. (Long Pause) [Once they get back in the cabin, Pete and Al will use the scale to weigh the rock box so that the flight engineers in Houston will know the launch weight of the LM and can make sure that, with the box stowed in the planned location, the weight distribution in the spacecraft will be as planned. In addition, Pete and Al will use the scale to weigh the PLSS feedwater remaining at the end of the EVA to give e

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Got to get this core tube, buddy.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: I know it. (Pause) As fast as I can. (Pause) 118:33:10 Bean: Okay, all the pans are done, Pete. Okay? Al's 4 O'Clock Pan (frames 6982 to 7006 )

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Come get the core tube.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay. Time to get working. (Pause) Okay. (Pause) Here's this (probably the tongs that Al borrowed at 118:27:35 ). I'll put it back (on the MESA).

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Oh, put in the Hand Tool Carrier.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Yes, sir. (Pause) I'm just going to lay it in there. I'm not going to...

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Yeah.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: ...fit it in there right now, so we can get finished.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Okay. Here, hang those on there, too. [Pete has removed or is removing weigh bags, flat sample bags, and core tube caps from the SRC and may be asking Al to get them out of the way by putting them on the HTC.]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: What? (Pause) (Garbled) hung on there, Pete?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: (Garbled)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: You bet. Got it. I'll go get that core tube.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad

a12a.1180736.text: (Laughing)

a12a.1180736.text: Just a minute, I...

a12a.1180736.text: That's affirmative, Al. First, we'd like to take and put the...

a12a.1180736.text: Okay. Go. (Pause) Hey, you're right. That thing doesn't want to stuff, does it? Kind of flimsy. (Pause) They better start making this lunar equipment a little more sturdy.

a12a.1180736.text: Loud and clear. [The "organic thing" is the Organic Control Sample which is a Teflon bag containing rolls of a very clean mesh made of aluminum. a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Okay.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Sounds good.

It's hard to quit doing the next one (that is, to get off the checklist) and go do other things that you hadn't planned to do."] [Conrad - "To go back."] [Bean - "It really is, and we should have been aware of that when we went. Because I think they're say

a12a.1180736.text: (Garbled)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Wait a minute. Hold it up just a little bit, Pete. Lift it up just a little.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1180736.text: Pete, will you confirm that you have the stereo camera (Gold camera) over in the Sun? (Pause) [The formal name of the stereo camera is the Apollo Lunar Surface Close-up Camera or ALSCC, and there was a checklist item just after 1+08 to "Place ALSCC on Surf(ace) in Direct Sun". In part because of the disruption of their schedule caused by the TV accident, Pete neglected this step prior to starting his pans at about 116:22.]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Is your stereo camera in the Sun, Pete?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Ah (thinking), no. Just a second.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: I want to see that first.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: (Chuckling) Okay. (Pause) Okay.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Stereo camera going into the Sun.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: (Garbled; Pause) Wait a minute. I've got to take this tool off. 118:47:32 Conrad: Remove the (Gold) camera. Okay. (Garbled) over on the Y-pad, next to my handy-dandy rock box 2, which is neatly covered. You want it sitting in the sunshine, is that correct, Houston?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1180736.text: That's affirmative, Pete.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Watch that cable, Pete; you're bothering your S-band.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Did I hit it?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Yep. You clipped your left foot on it.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Did I move the S-band?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: I don't think so but you ought to check it before you go in.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Okay.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Don't think you did, but the danger is great.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Don't fall over, (Gold) camera. (Pause)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: There you go. Why don't you walk around and check it? MP3 Audio Clip ( 21 min 40 sec) )

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Okay. (I'm getting in trouble from) getting in a hurry.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Oops. (Laughs)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Let me help you.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: (Melodically) Dah dah duh. (Pause)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Hey, Al?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Yeah, I'm coming.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Oh, okay.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: I don't like to come across that area. That S-band line is too tender!

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Okay. Get that. (Pause; light, brief static) Thank you.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: That's good.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Okay. (Pause)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: That's a pretty good idea, putting that foil over there. (Keep it) cool.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Hey, Al, let me check the S-band.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay. And then, we ought to dust each other off and get in.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Man, we are filthy!

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: We need a brush, a whisk broom. Okay. (Reading his checklist) "S-band antenna, lunar stay" I can get in there and try that? Okay, all I got to do is get in, soon as we dust off.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1180736.text: Roger, Pete. [Once Al gets back in the cabin, he will reconfigure the comm to transmit through the erectable S-Band antenna. On Apollo 14, Ed Mitchell will climb back up to the cabin to make the change before he and Shepard start the ALSEP deployment.]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Okay. We're looking at the Earth. [Pete is checking to make sure that Earth is still centered in the sighting scope.]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay, dust me off; and I'll dust you and get in. (Pause) I don't know what good you're going to do.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Hey, it does dust off a little bit!

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Does it? [Pete is using his gloves to scrape a little of the dirt off Al's suit. Later crews will have a substantial dustbrush , one about the size of a house painter's brush. The later crews found that the dustbrush worked best when the duster used it to beat the dustee's suit.]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Stand still.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Yeah. Yeah.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Yeah, I guess it does. Gets some of that loose stuff. (Pause)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Hey, come over here by the ladder where...

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: It's going to be dark (garbled)...

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: No, I can see. Let me... Just come over here by the ladder.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay. (Pause) There you go. (Pause) Oh, I see why; you can get lower that way.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Yeah. [The two possibilities here are (1) Al holds the ladder and bends his knees so that Pete can reach the upper surfaces of his suit and backpack and (2) Pete holds the ladder and gets low enough to get some of the dust off Al's legs. With the brush available, the later crews used the first of these techniques and then got the dustee up on the ladder so that the duster could get his legs.]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Good idea. Good idea! (Pause)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Kick your boots real hard when you (get up on the ladder)...

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay. [All of the crews used this technique to good effect. A few good boot stomps always shook loose a great deal of dirt. Of course, the other crewman had to make sure that he was standing back far enough not to get a dust shower.]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Okay, now turn around this leg this way... Other way.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: I can crawl up the ladder halfway if you'll get my upper; and I can crawl up the ladder and knock it off.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: There you go. That's a good idea; go ahead and do that.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: See anything else above me?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: No. Just go ahead and start up the ladder.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay. Okay, babe. (Perhaps reading the plaque on the landing strut as he jumps up to the first rung) Apollo 12.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: There you go. You didn't quite make it (to the first rung). There you go.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Oh, yes I did.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Stay put.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Okay.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1180736.text: Al, would you give us a mark when you're on the footpad?

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Let me kick this.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Wait a minute. Wait, wait.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: (To Gibson) Roger. I'm off the footpad right now. I'm standing on the ladder. Pete's dusting the boots off, trying to keep some of this dust out of the LM.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1180736.text: Roger, Al. Thanks. [Readers will note that they never get Pete dusted.]

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Oh, man, is it dusty. Just hold still for a while.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Let me...

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Wait, wait, wait.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: ...(garbled) a couple.

a12a.1180736.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1180736.text: Yeah, but let me brush... (Pause)

a12a.1180736.speaker: Bean
a12a.1180736.text: Well, you can get rid of a lot of it, kicking that way...

a12a.1184813.text: Oops. (Laughs)

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Let me help you.

a12a.1184813.text: That's good.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Okay. (Pause)

a12a.1184813.text: That's a pretty good idea, putting that foil over there. (Keep it) cool.

a12a.1184813.text: Hey, Al, let me check the S-band.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay. And then, we ought to dust each other off and get in.

a12a.1184813.text: Man, we are filthy!

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: We need a brush, a whisk broom. Okay. (Reading his checklist) "S-band antenna, lunar stay" I can get in there and try that? Okay, all I got to do is get in, soon as we dust off.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1184813.text: Roger, Pete. [Once Al gets back in the cabin, he will reconfigure the comm to transmit through the erectable S-Band antenna. On Apollo 14, Ed Mitchell will climb back up to the cabin to make the change before he and Shepard start the ALSEP deployment.]

a12a.1184813.text: Okay. We're looking at the Earth. [Pete is checking to make sure that Earth is still centered in the sighting scope.]

a12a.1184813.text: Stand still.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Yeah. Yeah.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Yeah, I guess it does. Gets some of that loose stuff. (Pause)

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Hey, come over here by the ladder where...

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: It's going to be dark (garbled)...

a12a.1184813.text: No, I can see. Let me... Just come over here by the ladder.

a12a.1184813.text: Okay. (Pause) There you go. (Pause) Oh, I see why; you can get lower that way.

a12a.1184813.text: Yeah. a12a.1184813.text: Good idea. Good idea! (Pause)

a12a.1184813.text: Kick your boots real hard when you (get up on the ladder)...

a12a.1184813.text: See anything else above me?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay. Okay, babe. (Perhaps reading the plaque on the landing strut as he jumps up to the first rung) Apollo 12.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: There you go. You didn't quite make it (to the first rung). There you go.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Oh, yes I did.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Stay put.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Let me kick this.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Wait a minute. Wait, wait.

a12a.1184813.text: (To Gibson) Roger. I'm off the footpad right now. I'm standing on the ladder. Pete's dusting the boots off, trying to keep some of this dust out of the LM.

a12a.1184813.text: Roger, Al. Thanks. [Readers will note that they never get Pete dusted.]

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Oh, man, is it dusty. Just hold still for a while.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Let me...

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Wait, wait, wait.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: ...(garbled) a couple.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Yeah, but let me brush... (Pause)

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Well, you can get rid of a lot of it, kicking that way...

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Yeah.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: ...Get it out of your soles of your boots.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Okay; go ahead on up.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Oh, okay. (Pause)

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Ohh, I'm in this dingy television wire again. (Pause)

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: There we go.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: All right; I'll help you from back here as best I can. [Pete will talk Al through the hatch.] 118:51:38 Bean: That's a good idea. I'm going to raise my gold visor here so I won't scratch it; and just put my protective visor down. (Pause) There. (Pause) Now, see the hatch? When you come up, take a good look at the hatch (and look at the scratches it got when they got out at the start of the EVA). (Pause) I'm really going to have to be tender about it. I'm not sure we're not going to want to put some tape over it or something. (Pause) Okay.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: All the way down. Raise your rear end. (Pause) That a boy. Got her. (Pause)

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: That's as far in as I can go. I'll just do a pushup. [Al has gotten as far in as he can without scraping his visor on the midstep . He does a push up to raise his head above it and then pulls himself farther into the cabin and into something approximating a kneeling position before he stands.]

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Slide in some more. I'm in.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Very good.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: In the hatch, Houston.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1184813.text: Roger, Al. Copy. You're in.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Maybe your old friendly "Cerd" (that is, CDR) will get the ETB.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay; just a second. Let me get my gear (the LEC). (Pause) Okay. Just a second.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: An ETB and two cameras (inside the ETB) ready to come up. (Pause) Oh, there's my friend (the TV wire), again. Al Bean?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: What?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: That thing's going to drive me buggy. Guess what.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Houston?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1184813.text: (Making a mis-identification) Go ahead, Pete.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Do you want me to switch to lunar stay antenna right now while Pete's on the surface? Over. [They want to make sure that they get a signal through the erectable S-band antenna before Pete climbs the ladder.]

a12a.1184813.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1184813.text: Roger. That's affirmative. And Track Mode, Off.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay. I'm going to Lunar Stay right now; but we may lose comm for a second. If I don't hear from you, I'll come back up. 118:53:24 Gibson: Roger. [Al will switch from the LM S-band antenna to the erectable S-band antenna . The switch for Track Mode and the S-Band selector are on Panel 12 .]

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Stay. (Long Pause) Houston, Apollo 12. How do you hear on Lunar Stay?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1184813.text: Intrepid, you're loud and clear. Sounds like Pete did the job (of erecting the S-Band correctly). [The change in signal quality is not dramatic but, during EVA-2 the quality of the comm will be much better than during EVA-1. Because of this successful experience, on Apollo 14, Ed Mitchell went up into the cabin to throw the switch shortly after he and Shepard erected the antenna at the start of their first EVA and had use of that antenna throughout the ALSEP deployment.]

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: (Garbled) start this ETB and... (Stops to listen to Gibson) Sure did.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Got good signal strength, Houston?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Go ahead and start the ETB up.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: (To Gibson) I'm going Track Mode to Off.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1184813.text: Roger.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: (To Conrad) Okay. Now... Just a second, Pete, I haven't got this ETB (means LEC) rigged. One second.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Okay. (Pause) [Before going out through the hatch at the start of the EVA, Al would not have put his end of the LEC outside the hatch, nor would he have pulled Pete's end in. The LEC strap still went through the hatch, but off to one side.]

a12a.1184813.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1184813.text: Intrepid, signal strength is good. (Pause)

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Matter of fact, you sound stronger, Houston.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1184813.text: I believe so, Pete.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Okay.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Need to mount it.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Got it. 118:54:35 Bean: We've got it. Wait a second; let me clear a nice little room here for it. (Pause) Say, are we going to jettison this garbage bag at the end of this EVA, Pete?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Yes, sir.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay, let me get it in good position.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Why don't you throw it out right now?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: That's a good idea.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: And I'll get rid of it (by tossing it under the descent stage).

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: That's a good idea; you can move it out of the way. That's a smart one. (Pause) Okay, here it comes. (Pause) Just a second.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Okay.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Just a second. (Pause) [What may have happened is that, when Al kicked the jett bag out through the hatch, it didn't clear the porch and he is now unable to reach it with his foot. A similar thing happened on Apollo 17 when Cernan and Schmitt jettisoned their PLSSs at the end of their 3rd EVA. In that instance, Cernan was finally able to get his foot out far enough to dislodge the hung-up PLSS.]

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Don't worry about it.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay. It won't bother us (during the LEC operations). Get it when you come up.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Haul her (the ETB) up.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay. Just a second. (Pause) Let me try something that might be just easier on all of us. I don't have to run one over a pulley; I can just pull it up, Pete.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: It doesn't weigh anything.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: That's right! Who needs a pulley? It's easier this way.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Wait a minute. Go ahead, pull. (Counting quickly) 1, 2, 3. That a boy.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Hey, I got an idea. Now, you pull. You pull.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Wait a minute. Nah; it's making a mess (by throwing dirt everywhere)! Never mind. Just keep on pulling.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay; just a second.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: All right. (Pause)

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Equipment transfer bag, in. Secured. (Long Pause) Okay, bring her (the LEC hooks) on back, Pete.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Okay. Wait, wait. Don't let it get hung up. Keep coming.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Let her go.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: No, wait a minute, now. Just keep it taut.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Ahhhh! See, you can't do it that way, Al. Take it easy. Just get it out slow. That a boy. That a boy. Now. Now, you can let go of it. (Long Pause) Here is that. (Pause) We got one rock box coming up. Okay, Al. Easy does it; easy does it. Wait a minute, now. Easy does it. Easy, easy! Easy! Easy! Easy! You're pulling when I don't want you to pull! Okay; now pull. (Pause) Okay. Now we've got to give it the heave-ho (to get it over the porch lip). Ready? 1. 2. Pull.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Got it made. Okay, lift her up a little bit, Pete. Let it come forward.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: That baby is heavy.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: That's right in the door, though! Let me slide that in here.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Okay. Okay, Houston. One rock box inside.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1184813.text: Roger, Pete. Copy. One SRC in. (Long Pause)

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay, bring her out.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Okay. (Pause) Wait, wait, wait, wait, wait! This thing is like playing with a snake. (Al laughs) Okay. That a boy. Now; easy does it. Get all this good stuff (his end of the LEC) and put it over here in the gear pad. Okay; now. Hey, Al? Now, you're going to hang on to it (Al's end of the LEC) and hand it to me, right? So I can tie it on the porch? Al?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: That's right! [In order to close the hatch, they need to have all of the LEC either in the cabin or outside. Because the LEC is so dirty, the latter choice is an easy one and, to keep the LEC handy for the start of the second EVA, Pete will tie Al's end to the porch rail and leave the rest of it hanging over the side.] [Conrad - "The LEC went back out on the porch."] [Bean - "Oh, so we could close the door."] [Conrad - "Right. We attached it to the porch."] [Bean - "So it wouldn't fall off, but it wasn't inside. Okay."]

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Okay. (Pause) Am I dirty. (Long Pause) Okay, Houston. What do you want me to do? Get in?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1184813.text: That's affirmative, Pete. If you've got the ETB and the rock box in, then climb in yourself. (Long Pause) [Jones - "Al, did you stow anything before Pete came through the hatch, or did you just put the ETB and the rock box on the engine cover or in a corner and stow things later?"] [Bean - "We didn't want to do anything but get inside and get out of our helmets and gloves; and then we could do all that other at our leisure."] [ Because the Moon can only be seen from one half of the Earth at any one time, Houston uses three receiving stations in succession to pick up the signals from Intrepid.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1184813.text: Intrepid, Houston. (No answer; Long Pause) Intrepid, Houston. (No answer; Pause)

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: You all ready for me to come in, Al?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: I'm ready. It's up to them.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Wonder what happened to Houston.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: I'm not sure that that Lunar Stay didn't do it. I'd rather go back on Track and get them back.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1184813.text: Intrepid, Houston. Stand by.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: (Hearing Houston) Okay. What's your problem?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1184813.text: Okay, we had a changeover from one site to another, down here. It was all on our end. No problem with your antenna. It's working well. 119:01:51 Conrad: Okay. You guys ought to call those things (the site handovers) out in advance. That's been happening all the way through this flight.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1184813.text: Roger, Pete. We concur. [The next handover will be at 129:57:03 and, as per Pete's request, Ed will give them a few minute's warning.]

a12a.1184813.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1184813.text: And go ahead and press on on the ingress.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Okay. (Pause) All right, Houston. Mark. I'm on the footpad.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1184813.text: Mark. (Long Pause)

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: (Jumping up to the first rung) That was easy.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: I just closed my feedwater. You might want to do that, too. [The Apollo 12 PLSSs have two feedwater controls: an on/off switch and a control that allowed them to choose a flow rate. Both controls are on the front-right corner at the bottom of the PLSS.] [Bean - "There was one with two little levers (rather like rabbit ears protruding from a knob) and that's how you got intermediate, medium (means 'minimum') and high. And the other one (H2O Shutoff and Relief Valve), which was the outside one, just had one lever that was on and off. And so you would kind of flip it up or down. And that's what y

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Probably a good idea. Let me see if I can find it back here. (Pause) Okay, I just closed mine. Coming up the ladder.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Gosh, you're shaking the whole LM.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Sorry about that.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: You'll get a warning, because you haven't got your feedwater, but that's okay. You've got cooling for quite a while.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Yeah. Understand. Okay, one garbage bag (meaning the jettison bag ). Anything else in there you want to get rid of?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Not a thing.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: All right, hand me the LEC.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay, the LEC's got kind of a little slip knot in it because the... Got it?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Yeah.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1184813.text: Pete, on your way through the hatch, will you give a check on the seal?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Check on the seal.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay; I can see it probably better than he could from this side, Houston. Seal looks real good. I'll tell you what we did do; when we got out, we...

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: I can't believe I did that.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Yeah, you did. Because I remember, you were hitting here and then when I backed up. I could... I'll tell you, we probably just ought to put a piece of tape over it.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Okay. (Hearing a warning tone) That's my feedwater (garbled).

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: (Garbled) the skin on the hatch, and for about a 10-inch cut, there. And it didn't hurt the insulation; didn't hurt the hatch. And I don't know whether you want us to put a piece of tape on there or just forget it. It doesn't look like it's going to bother anything.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: I'd say just forget it.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay, Pete.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Why don't you get over on your side?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay. Let me move over.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Okay. [Al has had the hatch fully open and, now, to let Pete into the cabin, he has to move over to Pete's side, close the hatch, get over on his side, and reopen the hatch as far as it will go against his legs. As he comes in through the hatch, Pete will get in as far as he can without bumping his visor on the engine cover and then, keeping his rear end as low as possible, push up with his arms so that he clears the engine cover and can pull himself far enough into the spacecraft that everything but his calves and feet are in. Only then can he stand up.]

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: I just checked your circuit breakers, and they're all good.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: All right. (Pause)

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Just a second; I'm not out of the way, yet.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: All right; but I want you to hold the door for a minute while I...

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: ...close this front ( dump valve )...

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Well, I've got to get out of the way.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: ...front thing here.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1184813.text: Pete, we concur. No tape.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: (To Al) All right.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: (Responding to Gibson) Okay.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Okay.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Now, wait a second, Pete. Let me back up a little better. 119:04:50 Conrad: Okay. Tell me which way to go.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Just a second. Okay, you're just perfect. Shoot right on in. Put your chest down and your rear end up (probably to get the OPS and the top of the PLSS in)... There you go; got it. Go a little bit to the left. Get a little further (into the cabin) until your head bumps (against the midstep ). Do a pushup and you're fat. Little bit to the left, little bit further to the left. That's it. Up. [The slang term âphatâ, a deliberate misspelling of âfatâ, is used here to mean âexcellentâ or âin great shapeâ.]

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Okay. [Conrad - "I couldn't see anything; not with my face in the floor."] [Jones - "And you'd reset the dump valve ."] [Conrad - "From outside. It's on the door; you can set it from either side."]

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: You're in the best possible position. Scoot in a little more. There; you got it.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: I'm in; no sweat.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay. Now careful when you turn around. You've got... (Garbled).

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Yeah.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay. Boy, you look dirty.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Oh, you do, too. [They will now follow the procedures on Sur-60 .]

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay; once you turn around, I'll get this hatch. Okay, it says "PLSS feedwater, close." We did that. " Forward hatch close and lock." When you're out of the way, I'll slide over and lock it.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Am I out of the way?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Not yet. [Pete is probably turning to his left so that, when he is done, he will be facing inboard with his PLSS out of Al's way.]

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Wait until I turn around. Just a minute.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Okay.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Get down on my hands and knees and lock this thing.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Yeah.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Need a push down.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Wait just a second. Let me raise my visor so I can see what's going on in here. Okay? [Jones - "It was my understanding that you could lean down, but that you couldn't get down on your knees by any stretch of the imagination in the Apollo 12 suit. Is that right, or were you literally getting on your knees?"] [Bean - "You can get down on your hands and knees. We did that. Sometimes."] [Conrad - "You probably got down part way, with your knees bent."] [Bean - "And then I want you to push me all the way down so I can reach the handle."]

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Can you give me a push-me-down?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: I am pushing you down. (Pause) Need further (push down)?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Just back up and let me tilt further forward, which is just as good.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: I can't go back any further. (Pause) Why don't you let me close it?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay, see if you can reach it. It's just a little bit out of my reach; you might be able to get it. Okay, easy.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: I'm ready.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Let me get back here in the corner. Watch your PLSS. (Pause) There you go. (Pause)

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Hatch closed.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Did you get it?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Yep.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Good show.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Okay.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay, next one. "Dump valve, both Auto." I've verified this one; (and) verified that one. [Al is verifying the settings of the dump valves in both the forward and overhead hatches.]

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: That one's Auto.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay. Let me look at something (in the checklist?) first. (Pause) Okay. (Reading) "PLSS O2 and Press flags may come on during Repress. If PLSS O2 less than 10 percent, manually control cabin Repress to maintain positive PGA pressure." Forget it. [They both have more than 10 percent oxygen left.]

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay; "Lighting Annunciator and Numerics, (change from Dim to) Bright."

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Wait a minute, easy. (Pause) There you go.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Okay. Now I'm going to go over here, (please move) over just a little so I can turn around. Oh, you did your circuit breakers.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: (I've gotten out of the way) the best I can; easy does it. What are you trying to do?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Lookit, that stop button's depressed. [' Lookit ' is a non-standard pronunciation of 'look at that'. Hearing it in Al's excited voice takes your editor 65 years back to his own childhood in the late 1940s and early 1950s.]

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Yeah. [Al may have noticed something out of the ordinary on the control panel, but we have not been able to figure out what he meant here. On all of the Apollo missions, various buttons and switches were sometimes hit accidentally - despite switch guards - as the astronauts turned in the cramped cabin. This is an important reason for the frequent checks of circuit breaker configuration.] [Al is turning around to face aft so that he can reach the controls on the Environmental Control System ( ECS ). The Cabin Repress Valve is on the front surface of the ECS cabinet at about waist height and, fr

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: I've got to turn around. Repress valve. Okay?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Well, I can reach the Repress valve, if you want.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: No, I've got it here. (Garbled) it. (Pause) Why don't you reach it? It may be better if you could. Can you reach... [In order to reach the valve, Pete probably has to face at least partly aft, lean over the engine cover to get around Al, and then reach across with his left hand to get the valve.]

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Cabin Repress to what? Auto?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: "Cabin Repress to Auto. Press Regs A and B to Cabin."

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Okay. [The controls for the pressure regulators are in the same group with the repress valve, but closer to Pete.]

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: "Master Alarm and Cabin Repress (warning light comes on)". Let's watch the pressure. (Pause) [With the pressure regulators set to cabin and the repress valve set to Auto, the ECS monitoring system thinks that the cabin should be pressurized and, because the cabin is currently at zero pressure, turns on the Master Alarm and the CABIN warning light. A parenthetical remark in the checklist reminds the astronauts that this will happen. The CABIN light is at the top of the rightmost column of Caution-and-Warning lights on Panel 1 . Like all the C&W lights on Panel 1, the CABIN light is red to indic

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Cabin pressure is starting up. (Pause; re-pressurization is audible)

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: One psi. (Pause)

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Coming in.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Huh?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: It's coming in good. (Pause) (Garbled)

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Repress is looking good. (Pause)

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Going ahead, "PLSS O2, Off." (Garbled) That's it; a little bit more. (Long Pause)

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: Okay. PLSS O2, Off.

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Can you verify that I've got mine off?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1184813.text: What?

a12a.1184813.speaker: Bean
a12a.1184813.text: Will you verify that I got mine off? I'll pull your diverter valve up, and check the water, and you do have it up. [The sound of re-pressurization ends.] ALSEP Deployment Apollo 12 Journal Post-EVA Activities in the LM

a12a.1190918.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1190918.text: Okay, Houston. There's the cabin at 4.6.

a12a.1190918.speaker: Bean
a12a.1190918.text: Okay. Master Alarm. Let me turn it off.

a12a.1190918.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1190918.text: Roger, Pete; we copy. We show that (4.6 psi) down here.

a12a.1190918.speaker: Bean
a12a.1190918.text: (reading from the last paragraph on the righthand side of Sur-60 ) "Operate OPS Purge Valve to Depress suit as required." (Pause) Let me operate yours.

a12a.1190918.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1190918.text: Yeah, here. [They have the option of deflating their suits by opening the purge valves.]

a12a.1190918.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1190918.text: Okay.

a12a.1190918.speaker: Bean
a12a.1190918.text: Here it comes.

a12a.1190918.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1190918.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay.

a12a.1190918.speaker: Bean
a12a.1190918.text: Okay. (Pause) " Cabin Repress valve closes at 4(.4 psi). Verify Cabin Press stable." It is. (Pause)

a12a.1190918.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1190918.text: " Cabin Gas Return (Valve) to Auto."

a12a.1190918.speaker: Bean
a12a.1190918.text: Okay, Cabin Gas Return (valve), Auto. [They are opening the valve to allow flow of oxygen from the cabin into the ECS suit circuit.]

a12a.1190918.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1190918.text: Wait a minute. Get over here.

a12a.1190918.speaker: Bean
a12a.1190918.text: Okay. (Pause)

a12a.1190918.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1190918.text: Auto.

a12a.1190918.speaker: Bean
a12a.1190918.text: " Suit Circuit Relief (valve), Auto."

a12a.1190918.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1190918.text: That's already Auto.

a12a.1190918.speaker: Bean
a12a.1190918.text: That's right, (because the checklist indicates "verify") " Suit Gas Diverter (Valve) , Push/Cabin."

a12a.1190918.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1190918.text: Push/Cabin. [Both the relief valve and the suit gas diverter valve will now permit oxygen flow from the suit circuit into the cabin, the latter through the O2 hoses which, of course, are not yet hooked up to the suits.]

a12a.1190918.speaker: Bean
a12a.1190918.text: "Verify EVA circuit breaker configuration." On your side (that is, CB panel 11): Suit Fan number 1, Close.

a12a.1190918.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1190918.text: Wait just a second. (Pause) Suit Fan 1, Closed.

a12a.1190918.speaker: Bean
a12a.1190918.text: And I'll close the Suit Fan Delta-P (on CB panel 16).

a12a.1190918.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1190918.text: Okay. [They are turning on the ECS fan to actually start the flow of oxygen through the suit circuit. The Delta-P sensor looks at a pressure difference across the fan to confirm proper operation.]

a12a.1190918.speaker: Bean
a12a.1190918.text: And I'll also... Notice " ECS caution (and) H2O SEP (lights out) ." And I've got them (that is, the two lights are out). And "Comm (section of CB panel 16), TV (circuit breaker), Open." Houston, do you want me to turn off the TV or leave it on?

a12a.1190918.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1190918.text: That's affirmative, Al. Turn it off (by opening the circuit breaker). (Pause)

a12a.1190918.speaker: Bean
a12a.1190918.text: Okay, and it says "Doff gloves, helmets, visors," and all that; and let's go off relay. We're going off relay right now, Houston.

a12a.1190918.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1190918.text: How do you want me to go, Al?

a12a.1190918.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1190918.text: Roger. Copy, you're going off relay. [They are going into push-to-talk.] [Comm Break. There is no on-board recording until about 131:02:11.] 119:12:11 Gibson: Intrepid, Houston. (Calls at increasing intervals, with no response) [Long Comm Break. During this comm break they remove their gloves and helmets, remove the purge valves, connect the LM O2 hoses so that they can have some air flow through the suits, turn off the PLSS pumps and fans, disconnect the PLSS water and connect the LM water. a12a.1205026.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1205026.text: Roger. Okay. Number 1 would be F, and that's Head Crater; number 2, B, Bench Crater; number 3, A, Sharp Crater; and we might possibly delete this depending on how you are doing on the timeline at that point. Number 4 is C, Halo Crater; number 5, D, Surveyor Crater; 6 is E, Block Crater; and we'll omit G. (Pause) [As can be seen on the traverse planning map, Station G is a small doublet (that is, crater pair) west of Bench and north of Sharp.]

a12a.1205026.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1205026.text: Okay. Now where is A? (Pause) Oh, it's Sharp Crater, is that right?

a12a.1205026.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1205026.text: That's affirm. A is Sharp Crater. And we may just cut across that corner depending upon how you are doing with the timeline. [Houston is suggesting that, if the early part of the traverse takes more time than they anticipate, they can eliminate the Sharp Crater stop and go directly from Bench to Halo. As Pete notes in his next statement, eliminating Sharp would eliminate their only sampling point on the supposed Copernican ray. The dotted line on the Site 4 map indicates the supposed northern boundary of the Copernican Ray material. Ulli Lotzmann has provided an annotated telescopic view . Cop

a12a.1205026.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1205026.text: Yeah. But don't we also want to get out here on this possible Copernican ray stuff? (Pause) Oops, excuse me, Uel Clanton, "material". [Conrad - (To Al) "Remember, (during the EVA-2 traverse) you didn't know where you were going. You followed me."] [Bean - "I didn't. I didn't copy this down. You had the map. I didn't have the map. So, while you were copying this down, I was over there eating, probably."] [Jones - "Tell me the story behind the apology to Uel Clanton."] [Conrad - "'Stuff'. I said the word 'Stuff'."] [Bean - "Uel Clanton was one of the guys that trained us. He was the chief traini

a12a.1205026.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1205026.text: Roger. We do want to get off after (that is, "go get") that Copernican ray material. Two points: one is it's further out than you might be able to hack in a normal traverse for the documented samples; and, two, we're not too sure exactly where that line (that is, the edge of the supposed ray) really lies. If you can, go on over into that area without taking a lot of time away from the other documented sampling; press on.

a12a.1205026.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1205026.text: Okay. Now, in looking at the map, we got all the way over to... If you go to, what is it, the general map, map 5, or whatever you want to call them, we got over in that Shelf Crater (Middle Crescent Crater). That's where you sent us, and we got to that fellow, so some of that stuff we picked up might be of that Copernican ray material. We also had photographs down there of that shelf, which everybody thought was interesting. I took a set of stereos in that thing, all the way around that big crater. Now, we made it over there with no strain. Matter of fact, we ran over and ran back in nothing f

a12a.1205026.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1205026.text: Roger, Pete. That sounds real good. Understand you'd like to go Sharp (Crater) and then Bench (Crater).

a12a.1205026.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1205026.text: Well, yeah; we can try that.

a12a.1205026.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1205026.text: Rog. No problem. (Pause) Okay, Pete, if you would, take a look at the information you have there on those sites, and we'll be getting back to you in the pre-EVA briefing and talk a little bit more about the location of the sampling, the core tubes, and the trench site sampling.

a12a.1205026.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1205026.text: Okay.

a12a.1205026.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1205026.text: You may have some pretty good ideas on that now, after being able to look at it first hand. (Pause) And, Pete, we have several questions for you related to the EVA. We'd like to move through these pretty quickly, as we know we ought to get you off to bed pretty quickly.

a12a.1205026.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1205026.text: Okay. [They have been awake for about 20 hours.]

a12a.1205026.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1205026.text: First, a question on the water in the boots. When was the first time you got water in the boots, Pete; and, Al, do you have any (in yours) at the present time?

a12a.1205026.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1205026.text: Al doesn't have any. I noticed it just starting before... I just got off the suit loop to Prep for EVA. It started in my right boot when I came back in. And these hoses - blue hose, of course - pumped out about three or four three-quarter-inch balls of water when I first disconnected it, just a few seconds ago. 121:31:06 Gibson: Roger. Thank you, Pete. (Pause) Question for you, Al. In the EVA Prep, the PLSS Comm check took longer than nominal. What corrective action did you take; and do you think we may have a problem the second time around? 121:31:26 Bean: None at all. It was completely my er

a12a.1205026.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1205026.text: Roger. 121:31:45 Bean: It was entirely an onboard problem. [They began the comm check at about 114:07 and found the error at about 114:29. Journal Contributor John Pfannerstill notes that the switch in question, which is located on the bottom of the RCU, can be seen in AS12-49- 7278 . From our perspective, the switch is just to the right of Al's camera.] [Jones - "You both sound a little stuffed up to me."] [Bean - "Yes, we do."] [Jones - "Jack had a mild allergic reaction to the dust. Did either of you notice anything like that?"] [Conrad - "You could sure smell it. Very distinctive smell. I'

a12a.1205026.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1205026.text: Question for you, Houston. How long was our total EVA Prep time?

a12a.1205026.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1205026.text: Stand by on that one. (Pause) Pete, your total EVA Prep time was 2 hours and 8 minutes.

a12a.1205026.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1205026.text: Okay. I believe we'll do it in about 1 plus 45 tomorrow as planned. Like Al said: one, we made a couple of mistakes; and the other one, we just had our heads up and locked. Something we didn't have on the checklist and we should have known better. [Conrad - (Laughing) "(The full expression is) Heads up our ass and locked!"] [Thomas Schwagmeier found a explaination at a website dedicated to Slang Used in the 5th AAF in the SWAP during WWII : Head Up and Locked = A term applied to a person reacting stupidly to an emergency. ('He had his head locked up his a--'). Other synonyms might be 'useless'

a12a.1205026.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1205026.text: Al, second question. When you put the core tubes in, do you now think it's feasible to join two core tubes together and perhaps get at least one and a half core tube lengths in? Something on that order?

a12a.1205026.speaker: Bean
a12a.1205026.text: Yeah. It was getting harder as I drove it in, just like it does back on Earth. But I think if you wanted to stand there and pound, maybe three times as long as you would have to drive in one, you could do it. And I don't know if we could do that now, though, with those pins in, but maybe we could take those pins out and put two of them together. I'd sure be willing to give it a try if you'd want to do it. [There was a pip pin (a removable, pull pin) near the top of the core tube, perhaps to keep a follower from coming all the way out, that would have made it impossible to join two core tubes.]

a12a.1205026.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1205026.text: Okay. We'll be thinking about that one and get back to you with it. Apparently, the augering is what made the difference there. If you're looking at your map...

a12a.1205026.speaker: Bean
a12a.1205026.text: That and you've got to pound the... (Stops to listen to Gibson)

a12a.1205026.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1205026.text: Go ahead.

a12a.1205026.speaker: Bean
a12a.1205026.text: No comment there. (Long Pause) 121:34:11 Conrad: Okay, Houston. If you're watching the computer, I'm going to bring it out of Standby and put it back in again to update the clock time.

a12a.1205026.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1205026.text: Roger, Intrepid. (Long Pause)

a12a.1205026.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1205026.text: There's another one of those downlink too-fast alarms. [Long Comm Break with the LM. A conversation between Gibson and Gordon has been omitted. ]
