a12a.1330926.text: I'm not sure we're at the right place, either. Let me look at the top of this hill here.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: This is Surveyor Crater. Let me look at the chart. There's a nice rock right there.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Here's Surveyor.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Let me look at the map. Not even hardly a crater worth looking at where we are. (Pause) Okay.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1330926.text: Okay, Pete. It's your call there. You're the local experts. If you see a better location for that double core tube, go ahead.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Yeah. We're trying to find the right crater, Houston. [According to the detailed traverse map published in the Apollo 12 Preliminary Science Report (Figure 10-1 ), they have been sampling at a spot about 50 to 60 meters northwest of Halo Crater.] [Conrad - "Well, here's where we did the double core tube sample, and this is Halo crater. So we went all the way around it. We never did find it."] [During the next few minutes, they will move south, away from Surveyor Crater, looking for Halo. They will pass near its west rim and finally stop to take the double core tube about 30 to 40 meters south

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Hey, Pete. I think it's that area right over there. Halo is this first one right here, the little one, and then all those others are next over according to the chart.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Okay.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: So we can just go over there and...

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Which one's Halo? This one right here?

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: No; it's right...You see where I'm pointing!

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: No.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: As I see it, it's that one right over there.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Okay. Let's go.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Okay.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: I have the double core tube.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: All right.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: And you want what, Houston, a partial pan?

a12a.1330926.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1330926.text: That's affirmative. (Pause) We'd like a full pan at that point, Pete.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: I just (garbled)...

a12a.1330926.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1330926.text: And also, Al, if you could give us some sort of an estimate of how hard it is to get the core tube in. That is, what the force history is; how many pounds and how much force.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Sure will.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Hey, look at this little neat-o crater right here. (Pause) It's a good place to sample. (Pause) Oh, look at all the glass in the bottom of that baby.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Got a lot of that (in sample bags), though.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Huh?

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Got a lot of glass. Now, there...

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Yeah.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: I think that's Halo right there.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Which one?

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: (Garbled).

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: (Garbled) looking at.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Right over (garbled) that one right there.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Too big.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Too big, huh?

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Let's take this one right here.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: All right. That's good. (Pause) Lots of glass down in the bottom of this baby... [Bean - "I'll bet you did see Halo and we decided it was too big. Dumb thinking."] [Conrad - "Listen, we worked hard finding those things."] [Bean - "Yeah, but Halo Crater was pretty much an arbitrary choice on their part. I mean, they're making an estimate from Earth that it's going to be a very interesting geological point. And it may or it may not be. And the one we got may have been better or it may have been worse."]

a12a.1330926.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1330926.text: Pete and Al, could we have a readout on the cameras at this point?

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Sure could. Just a second. (You can) see mine probably, Pete.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: You'd better take all these pictures. I'm running out.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Well, I'd better change cameras because... [Al will do most of the photography of the Surveyor and needs to have enough film left to do that task.]

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Sixty for Al,....

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Let's see. You've got 110. You've got plenty to go.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Hey, you know what's happened?

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Uh-uh.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: This thing hasn't been taking every picture.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Take a picture and let's see.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: I just caught it. I mean, it's been doing it intermittently. [As they will discover in a few minutes, the trigger/handle assemblies on both cameras have come loose. See the discussion at 133:29:22 .]

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Okay. Now (garbled) get out and make the double core tube here. (Pause)

a12a.1330926.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1330926.text: Pete, we copy 60 and 110 on the film.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: That's affirm.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Here, look at the chart a minute, Pete, while (garbled)...

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Yeah. Okay.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: (Garbled). Be careful. (Garbled) (Long Pause)

a12a.1330926.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1330926.text: Pete and Al, we'd like you to go ahead and get the pans taken on the LMP's camera. You can either have Al do the pans or switch cameras. Your choice.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Okay. Roger-Roger. (Pause) [Houston has decided that Al has enough film left to do both the pan and the Surveyor photography.] 133:24:14 Bean: Okay, Pete. You'll have to pull the pin and unscrew that if you can.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Okay. [They are assembling the double core tube. Pete is probably pulling the pip pin in the section they will use for the bottom half of the double; and, then, is unscrewing the bit from the section that they will use as the upper half.]

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Good luck on unscrewing it. Hey, wait. Hold it just a second. [I asked about the relative difficulty of doing these tasks with the gloves on.] [Conrad - "It's just the same old business of it being difficult because of our moving around. It's tough being able to move our hands and hold things in the proper position - to get the right (correct) angle because you just can't do these kinds of things any old way. So I think any slow downs were suit restrictions. All that gear worked once we got our hands on it the right way."]

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: I'll get it.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Okay. (Pause) Hey, good show! 133:24:41 Conrad: Okay. (Pause) Double core tube. You can drive it.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: (I'll) give it a go.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: I'm going to hand you the hammer .

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: I'm not sure that double core tube screws on as far as it should. Try it again. [Gibson is talking with Gordon and, once again, Jack Schmitt takes over the comm briefly.]

a12a.1330926.speaker: Schmitt
a12a.1330926.text: Pete and Al, Houston. Be sure you give us the number of the lower core tube, please.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Okay. The lower core tube is number 3, I think.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Yeah.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Three?

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Three, and the upper one's 1.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Okay. Ready to pound it.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Where are you going to drive it?

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Where would you recommend?

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Well, let's go over to this crater right here.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Okay. (Pause) Boy, it's soft around those little craters. (Pause) How about right here?

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Yeah.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Want to take a picture? 133:25:34 Conrad: Yep. (Garbled)

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: I can shove it in a little. I hope this is a good soft place.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Yeah. [AS12-49- 7285 shows Al shoving the core tube into the ground by hand. In 7286 he has begun to hammer.] 133:25:41 Bean: It seems to be. Oh, I hit something solid there. (To Houston) Well, I used all my weight, Houston, and shoved it in about seven inches. Now, I'll just pound on it a while and see what we can do. (Pause) It (seems to) be going in okay. Yeah. It's going on down.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Keep augering.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Hope we got a good spot. I don't really think this is the right place. (Pause) Some of those things aren't so obvious.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Got awful solid, didn't it? [Unlike the core tube sampling at Sharp , we can not hear Al's hammer strokes here at Halo.] 133:26:13 Bean: Well, it's going. Let me wiggle it a bit. It's got one core tube completely in now. (Pause) Have to hit it harder. (Chuckles; Pause) Hey, Houston. This hammer - when you hit on the side of it, like you have to do to hit it within this suit - it knocks little chips of metal off the side of the hammer. I don't think that's too good. [In his post-Apollo career as an artist, Al uses the hammer, a core tube bit, and a replica of the soles of his lunar boots to tex

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: I'm afraid some of the fragments will damage the suit. It's not damaging itself. You know, it's just breaking...Hey, I'm better left handed than right. There goes another fragment. Do you see it, Pete?

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Yeah, I'm watching. [Conrad - "The hammer has a coating."] [Bean - "And probably for thermal reasons. It's probably a steel hammer with an aluminum coating or something. But it sure knocked it off."] [Conrad - "Yep. You (meaning Al) have the hammer (in your personal collection of memorabilia)."] [Bean - "Yes, and you can see (where the coating got) knocked off. And you can also see where I knocked into the shaft, just below the head, a number of times."] [Conrad - "Yeah, you missed (with the head) and hit (with) the shaft."] [Bean - "And then they made a bigger hammer that was heavier. Ours wa

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: You even hit it with the front end and some of them pop off. (Pause) They're flying all over the place.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Okay. He's up to the bottom of the handgrip portion of the upper tube. He's really driving that baby.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Look at that ham(mer). Look at that! Look at that! It looks like it's got a coating over the hammer, Pete, and I'm knocking the coating. Instead of being steel or aluminum hammer, it's...

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Yeah.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: ...some sort of coated arrangement.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Schmitt
a12a.1330926.text: That's affirmative, Al. There is a coating on that hammer and that's probably what you're knocking off. And also, we want to be sure to get the site there documented.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: We'll document it for you.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Coming up.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: We almost got it, Houston. Almost

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Hit something solid there, didn't you?

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: No. It's just getting down there, Pete.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Hey, that baby is in the ground.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: We've got a double. Now the question is can we pull it out? (Pete laughs) [Al's last phrase was delivered in a good imitation of Pete's distinctive speech pattern.] 133:28:04 Bean: (Garbled) Let me get the down-Sun shot, (that is, a picture taken from the east). (Pause) I hope that's a good spot.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: I do, too.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Ought to get some of these rocks nearby here. (Pause) Come on; let's see here. 250, 11. 133:28:24 Conrad: All right. (Pause) [Al's down-Sun pictures of the core tube at Halo Crater are AS12-48- 7077 and 7078 .] [Pete's cross-Sun's are AS12-49- 7287 and 7288 .]

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: (Could) you give them a little pan or something, so they can see where this came from? So they...

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: You do it. I don't have that much film. [They have a spare film magazine in the HTC but, not having planned to change magazines during the EVA, they aren't thinking in those terms. This seems to be an instance of training so tightly to the mission plan - a function of having a large number of tasks to accomplish in a short time - that it is difficult to switch gears. This topic will come up again in the context of the secret timer.]

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Okay. Why don't I just trade you cameras? That's probably the smart way.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: All right. (Pause) Hey, would you lift mine off when you're through?

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Sure will. [Pete is asking Al to lift the CDR camera/bracket assembly off the fitting on the front of Pete's RCU.]

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: I can't pull those things right. They tend to vacuum weld a little bit or something, I think.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Now, you hold that one (meaning the LMP camera).

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Hey, that (meaning the LMP camera assembly)'s about to come apart.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: I'll be darned if it isn't. I'll fix it; hold the handle there. (Garbled)

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Why don't I...

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Whoa!

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: It did come apart.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: It did come apart. Son of a gun. Well, that kind of bombed out. I tell you what, the only thing we can...(garbled) is it broke!

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Sure did break. 133:29:22 Bean: Well, I'll tell you what happened, Houston. The nut (the thumbwheel on the LMP trigger/handle assembly) that holds the handle of the camera on broke off. And so, the handle's free, but that's okay. We'll just carry it around. [The following is taken from the Apollo 12 Mission Report. See, also, Figure 14-45 . "During the second extravehicular period, the Commander's camera did not advance and count every time the trigger was squeezed. Shortly afterwards, when both the camera assemblies were being removed from the remote control units (RCU's) in order to exchange

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Let me ask you a question.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Schmitt
a12a.1330926.text: Roger, Al. We got you. We understand that the nut (thumbwheel) broke, but the camera is still usable, right?

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: (To Schmitt) Yeah. (To Pete) And your nut's loose too, Pete. Stay there. Let me tighten it up for you. Think they work loose in one-sixth g; we knew that, we should have watched it more carefully. Can you help do that yourself?

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Yeah.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Because it's hard for me to do (while Pete's still wearing the CDR camera).

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Yeah.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Let me go put the hammer up (on the handtool carrier) and (put) this (LMP) camera somewhere and (I'll) be right back. (Pause) There goes the bracket, but that's okay. Still got the camera. (Pause) [Because the thumbwheel fell of the LMP handle/trigger assembly , there was nothing to secure the bracket to the camera, so the bracket has fallen off.]

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: But you're going to have to help me get this (CDR) camera off (Pete's RCU) ...

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: All right.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: ...(Garbled) it off

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Okay. There's no need to get it off now.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Okay. I'll leave it on. No; I want to give it to you.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: And you're going to use this one?

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Al, you got to take the Surveyor pictures, so why don't I give you the (CDR) camera?

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Okay. That's good enough.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: And you've still got 50 pictures or so. So watch it. Make sure it takes a picture each time it turns.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Okay.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: And just...Why don't you....Your camera...

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: I'll tell you what...

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Well, here, I'll hold it (meaning the LMP camera) and you take this one off.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Okay. You got that (LMP) camera. (I'll) take this one (CDR camera) off. (Garbled) take it off and then I'll tighten the nut. (Pause) Okay; now, I'm going to (garbled) it down a little bit.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Wait a minute; I'll hold that down. [Pete is probably holding on to his RCU so that it doesn't move as Al removes the camera/bracket assembly .]

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: There you go. Push your RCU down a little bit more.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: I'm trying to. [The camera bracket comes up and out of the RCU mount and, while Al pulls up on the camera, Pete is pushing down on the RCU, essentially doubling the force they are applying to overcome friction between the bracket and the mount.]

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: A bit more. It's almost off, Pete.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Who put it on there?

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Got to push down some more.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: I can't. There you go.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Okay, now. (See if) I can tighten this thing. (Pause) Okay, I'm tightening it so it'll get tight. (Pause) Okay. I got enough there; that'll be enough. [Readers should note that, in the following exchange, it is not at all crystal clear what is being done with the cameras and in what order. See the discussion following 133:32:05 .]

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Drop it (the CDR camera/bracket assembly in right there (meaning onto the camera mount on Al's RCU).

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: All right.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Just drop that one (the LMP camera) in here (into the HTC).

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Well, why don't you...

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: No need to carry it.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Well, you could carry it.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Well, that's what I'd do. Carry it or something (in case they need to use the film in magazine 48).

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: But I got too much other stuff (the gnomon and the scoop)

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Let me carry part of it or something. Okay. Let me go pull out the core tube (which is still in the ground)

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: No, I tell you what. We can always take the magazine off this (that is, off the LMP camera) and put it on the other one (the CDR camera).

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: That's what we can do, I guess.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Yeah. We just drop it in here. 133:32:05 Bean: Okay. [Al has been using magazine 48 and Pete has been using 49. From here on, Al uses the CDR camera with magazine 49. During the mission review, it took some while to figure out what was going on here, in part because Pete and Al had mis-remembered the incident, thinking that it was Pete's camera that had fallen apart. The following is Al's summation after we got the matter more or less straight in our minds.] [Bean - "Here's what I think happened. Let's see if you (Pete) agree with this. You mentioned that you don't think your (CDR) camera was

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: All right. Let's go get your core tube. I'll go get it.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Okay. You go get it. And I'll...

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Take a cap off (the Hand Tool Carrier).

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Take the cap, right here. (Pause) Okay.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: (Looking at the damage to the top of the tube) Hey, you sure beat on it.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: That's what it took to get it in the ground.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: It's coming up real easy.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Good. (Pause)

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: (Straining) I say it's coming up real easy.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: Looked for a minute like you were going down real easy. (Hearty Laughter) The core tube hangs in and your feet just sink down. Okay, hold. (Pause)

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1330926.text: Hey, we made a tactical error here.

a12a.1330926.speaker: Bean
a12a.1330926.text: In what fashion?

a12a.1330926.speaker: Conrad

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Hey, Pete. I think it's that area right over there. Halo is this first one right here, the little one, and then all those others are next over according to the chart.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: So we can just go over there and...

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Which one's Halo? This one right here?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: No; it's right...You see where I'm pointing!

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: No.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: As I see it, it's that one right over there.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay. Let's go.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: I have the double core tube.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: All right.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: And you want what, Houston, a partial pan?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Gibson
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: That's affirmative. (Pause) We'd like a full pan at that point, Pete.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: I just (garbled)...

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Gibson
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: And also, Al, if you could give us some sort of an estimate of how hard it is to get the core tube in. That is, what the force history is; how many pounds and how much force.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Sure will.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Hey, look at this little neat-o crater right here. (Pause) It's a good place to sample. (Pause) Oh, look at all the glass in the bottom of that baby.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Got a lot of that (in sample bags), though.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Huh?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Got a lot of glass. Now, there...

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Yeah.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: I think that's Halo right there.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Which one?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: (Garbled).

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: (Garbled) looking at.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Right over (garbled) that one right there.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Too big.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Too big, huh?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Let's take this one right here.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: All right. That's good. (Pause) Lots of glass down in the bottom of this baby... [Bean - "I'll bet you did see Halo and we decided it was too big. Dumb thinking."] [Conrad - "Listen, we worked hard finding those things."] [Bean - "Yeah, but Halo Crater was pretty much an arbitrary choice on their part. I mean, they're making an estimate from Earth that it's going to be a very interesting geological point. And it may or it may not be. And the one we got may have been better or it may have been worse."]

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Gibson
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Pete and Al, could we have a readout on the cameras at this point?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Sure could. Just a second. (You can) see mine probably, Pete.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: You'd better take all these pictures. I'm running out.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Well, I'd better change cameras because... [Al will do most of the photography of the Surveyor and needs to have enough film left to do that task.]

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Sixty for Al,....

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Let's see. You've got 110. You've got plenty to go.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Hey, you know what's happened?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Uh-uh.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: This thing hasn't been taking every picture.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Take a picture and let's see.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: I just caught it. I mean, it's been doing it intermittently. [As they will discover in a few minutes, the trigger/handle assemblies on both cameras have come loose. See the discussion at 133:29:22 .]

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay. Now (garbled) get out and make the double core tube here. (Pause)

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Gibson
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Pete, we copy 60 and 110 on the film.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: That's affirm.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Here, look at the chart a minute, Pete, while (garbled)...

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Yeah. Okay.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: (Garbled). Be careful. (Garbled) (Long Pause)

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Gibson
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Pete and Al, we'd like you to go ahead and get the pans taken on the LMP's camera. You can either have Al do the pans or switch cameras. Your choice.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay. Roger-Roger. (Pause) [Houston has decided that Al has enough film left to do both the pan and the Surveyor photography.] 133:24:14 Bean: Okay, Pete. You'll have to pull the pin and unscrew that if you can.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay. [They are assembling the double core tube. Pete is probably pulling the pip pin in the section they will use for the bottom half of the double; and, then, is unscrewing the bit from the section that they will use as the upper half.]

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Good luck on unscrewing it. Hey, wait. Hold it just a second. [I asked about the relative difficulty of doing these tasks with the gloves on.] [Conrad - "It's just the same old business of it being difficult because of our moving around. It's tough being able to move our hands and hold things in the proper position - to get the right (correct) angle because you just can't do these kinds of things any old way. So I think any slow downs were suit restrictions. All that gear worked once we got our hands on it the right way."]

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: I'll get it.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay. (Pause) Hey, good show! 133:24:41 Conrad: Okay. (Pause) Double core tube. You can drive it.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: (I'll) give it a go.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: I'm going to hand you the hammer .

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: I'm not sure that double core tube screws on as far as it should. Try it again. [Gibson is talking with Gordon and, once again, Jack Schmitt takes over the comm briefly.]

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Schmitt
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Pete and Al, Houston. Be sure you give us the number of the lower core tube, please.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay. The lower core tube is number 3, I think.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Yeah.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Three?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Three, and the upper one's 1.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay. Ready to pound it.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Where are you going to drive it?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Where would you recommend?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Well, let's go over to this crater right here.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay. (Pause) Boy, it's soft around those little craters. (Pause) How about right here?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Yeah.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Want to take a picture? 133:25:34 Conrad: Yep. (Garbled)

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: I can shove it in a little. I hope this is a good soft place.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Yeah. [AS12-49- 7285 shows Al shoving the core tube into the ground by hand. In 7286 he has begun to hammer.] 133:25:41 Bean: It seems to be. Oh, I hit something solid there. (To Houston) Well, I used all my weight, Houston, and shoved it in about seven inches. Now, I'll just pound on it a while and see what we can do. (Pause) It (seems to) be going in okay. Yeah. It's going on down.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Keep augering.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Hope we got a good spot. I don't really think this is the right place. (Pause) Some of those things aren't so obvious.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Got awful solid, didn't it? [Unlike the core tube sampling at Sharp , we can not hear Al's hammer strokes here at Halo.] 133:26:13 Bean: Well, it's going. Let me wiggle it a bit. It's got one core tube completely in now. (Pause) Have to hit it harder. (Chuckles; Pause) Hey, Houston. This hammer - when you hit on the side of it, like you have to do to hit it within this suit - it knocks little chips of metal off the side of the hammer. I don't think that's too good. [In his post-Apollo career as an artist, Al uses the hammer, a core tube bit, and a replica of the soles of his lunar boots to tex

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: I'm afraid some of the fragments will damage the suit. It's not damaging itself. You know, it's just breaking...Hey, I'm better left handed than right. There goes another fragment. Do you see it, Pete?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Yeah, I'm watching. [Conrad - "The hammer has a coating."] [Bean - "And probably for thermal reasons. It's probably a steel hammer with an aluminum coating or something. But it sure knocked it off."] [Conrad - "Yep. You (meaning Al) have the hammer (in your personal collection of memorabilia)."] [Bean - "Yes, and you can see (where the coating got) knocked off. And you can also see where I knocked into the shaft, just below the head, a number of times."] [Conrad - "Yeah, you missed (with the head) and hit (with) the shaft."] [Bean - "And then they made a bigger hammer that was heavier. Ours wa

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: You even hit it with the front end and some of them pop off. (Pause) They're flying all over the place.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay. He's up to the bottom of the handgrip portion of the upper tube. He's really driving that baby.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Look at that ham(mer). Look at that! Look at that! It looks like it's got a coating over the hammer, Pete, and I'm knocking the coating. Instead of being steel or aluminum hammer, it's...

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Yeah.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: ...some sort of coated arrangement.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Schmitt
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: That's affirmative, Al. There is a coating on that hammer and that's probably what you're knocking off. And also, we want to be sure to get the site there documented.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: We'll document it for you.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Coming up.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: We almost got it, Houston. Almost

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Hit something solid there, didn't you?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: No. It's just getting down there, Pete.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Hey, that baby is in the ground.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: We've got a double. Now the question is can we pull it out? (Pete laughs) [Al's last phrase was delivered in a good imitation of Pete's distinctive speech pattern.] 133:28:04 Bean: (Garbled) Let me get the down-Sun shot, (that is, a picture taken from the east). (Pause) I hope that's a good spot.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: I do, too.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Ought to get some of these rocks nearby here. (Pause) Come on; let's see here. 250, 11. 133:28:24 Conrad: All right. (Pause) [Al's down-Sun pictures of the core tube at Halo Crater are AS12-48- 7077 and 7078 .] [Pete's cross-Sun's are AS12-49- 7287 and 7288 .]

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: (Could) you give them a little pan or something, so they can see where this came from? So they...

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: You do it. I don't have that much film. [They have a spare film magazine in the HTC but, not having planned to change magazines during the EVA, they aren't thinking in those terms. This seems to be an instance of training so tightly to the mission plan - a function of having a large number of tasks to accomplish in a short time - that it is difficult to switch gears. This topic will come up again in the context of the secret timer.]

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay. Why don't I just trade you cameras? That's probably the smart way.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: All right. (Pause) Hey, would you lift mine off when you're through?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Sure will. [Pete is asking Al to lift the CDR camera/bracket assembly off the fitting on the front of Pete's RCU.]

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: I can't pull those things right. They tend to vacuum weld a little bit or something, I think.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Now, you hold that one (meaning the LMP camera).

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Hey, that (meaning the LMP camera assembly)'s about to come apart.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: I'll be darned if it isn't. I'll fix it; hold the handle there. (Garbled)

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Why don't I...

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Whoa!

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: It did come apart.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: It did come apart. Son of a gun. Well, that kind of bombed out. I tell you what, the only thing we can...(garbled) is it broke!

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Sure did break. 133:29:22 Bean: Well, I'll tell you what happened, Houston. The nut (the thumbwheel on the LMP trigger/handle assembly) that holds the handle of the camera on broke off. And so, the handle's free, but that's okay. We'll just carry it around. [The following is taken from the Apollo 12 Mission Report. See, also, Figure 14-45 . "During the second extravehicular period, the Commander's camera did not advance and count every time the trigger was squeezed. Shortly afterwards, when both the camera assemblies were being removed from the remote control units (RCU's) in order to exchange

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Let me ask you a question.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Schmitt
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Roger, Al. We got you. We understand that the nut (thumbwheel) broke, but the camera is still usable, right?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: (To Schmitt) Yeah. (To Pete) And your nut's loose too, Pete. Stay there. Let me tighten it up for you. Think they work loose in one-sixth g; we knew that, we should have watched it more carefully. Can you help do that yourself?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Yeah.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Because it's hard for me to do (while Pete's still wearing the CDR camera).

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Yeah.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Let me go put the hammer up (on the handtool carrier) and (put) this (LMP) camera somewhere and (I'll) be right back. (Pause) There goes the bracket, but that's okay. Still got the camera. (Pause) [Because the thumbwheel fell of the LMP handle/trigger assembly , there was nothing to secure the bracket to the camera, so the bracket has fallen off.]

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: But you're going to have to help me get this (CDR) camera off (Pete's RCU) ...

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: All right.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: ...(Garbled) it off

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay. There's no need to get it off now.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay. I'll leave it on. No; I want to give it to you.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: And you're going to use this one?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Al, you got to take the Surveyor pictures, so why don't I give you the (CDR) camera?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay. That's good enough.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: And you've still got 50 pictures or so. So watch it. Make sure it takes a picture each time it turns.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: And just...Why don't you....Your camera...

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: I'll tell you what...

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Well, here, I'll hold it (meaning the LMP camera) and you take this one off.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay. You got that (LMP) camera. (I'll) take this one (CDR camera) off. (Garbled) take it off and then I'll tighten the nut. (Pause) Okay; now, I'm going to (garbled) it down a little bit.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Wait a minute; I'll hold that down. [Pete is probably holding on to his RCU so that it doesn't move as Al removes the camera/bracket assembly .]

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: There you go. Push your RCU down a little bit more.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: I'm trying to. [The camera bracket comes up and out of the RCU mount and, while Al pulls up on the camera, Pete is pushing down on the RCU, essentially doubling the force they are applying to overcome friction between the bracket and the mount.]

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: A bit more. It's almost off, Pete.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Who put it on there?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Got to push down some more.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: I can't. There you go.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay, now. (See if) I can tighten this thing. (Pause) Okay, I'm tightening it so it'll get tight. (Pause) Okay. I got enough there; that'll be enough. [Readers should note that, in the following exchange, it is not at all crystal clear what is being done with the cameras and in what order. See the discussion following 133:32:05 .]

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Drop it (the CDR camera/bracket assembly in right there (meaning onto the camera mount on Al's RCU).

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: All right.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Just drop that one (the LMP camera) in here (into the HTC).

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Well, why don't you...

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: No need to carry it.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Well, you could carry it.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Well, that's what I'd do. Carry it or something (in case they need to use the film in magazine 48).

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: But I got too much other stuff (the gnomon and the scoop)

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Let me carry part of it or something. Okay. Let me go pull out the core tube (which is still in the ground)

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: No, I tell you what. We can always take the magazine off this (that is, off the LMP camera) and put it on the other one (the CDR camera).

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: That's what we can do, I guess.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Yeah. We just drop it in here. 133:32:05 Bean: Okay. [Al has been using magazine 48 and Pete has been using 49. From here on, Al uses the CDR camera with magazine 49. The following is Al's summation after we got the matter more or less straight in our minds.] [Bean - "Here's what I think happened. Let's see if you (Pete) agree with this. You mentioned that you don't think your (CDR) camera was

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: All right. Let's go get your core tube. I'll go get it.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay. You go get it. And I'll...

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Take a cap off (the Hand Tool Carrier).

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Take the cap, right here. (Pause) Okay.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: (Looking at the damage to the top of the tube) Hey, you sure beat on it.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: That's what it took to get it in the ground.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: It's coming up real easy.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Good. (Pause)

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: (Straining) I say it's coming up real easy.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Looked for a minute like you were going down real easy. (Hearty Laughter) The core tube hangs in and your feet just sink down. Okay, hold. (Pause)

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Hey, we made a tactical error here.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: In what fashion?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: I think we dropped an end of the tube we shouldn't have dropped. [When Pete was assembling the double core tube at 133:24:14 , he dropped the top of what became the lower core section. The job of finding it again is made a little bit easier by the fact that, in the soft lunar soil, their footprints mark the few places where they have stood on this virgin surface.]

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Uh-uh.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Yeah. We got to take them apart. (which means the lower section still needs a top) Remember?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay. Well, what we'll have to do is pick it up, right over there.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Where is it?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: It's right over here.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay. (Pause) [Conrad - "We couldn't put the double core tube in the box, so we had to go find the top again, and put it back in the lower section."] [Bean - "We knew we had to put a bottom (cap) on..."] [Conrad - "Each one had an adapter top. We had three core tubes, each had an adapter top. We took core tube number 3, took the adapter top off, dropped it, screwed it in core tube number 1. And, now, we've got to pull it back out, we('ve) got to put a cap on the bottom, we('ve) got to go find that adapter, put it on the top of this one, put the bottom on that one, and we still got a cap on the

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Hold on. We'll find it.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: It's right back there. It's someplace buried in the dirt. I see it. Ha. Ha. Right here. Wait a minute. I'll get it with the...Here, you hold the core tube.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay. Just a second. Just a second. (Pause) Okay. I've got the core tube. I'll start unscrewing it.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Where's my sample stirrer (the tongs)?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Right there. You got it, Pete. Ah, you got your hose too. Pull...More...There you go. (Pause) Good show. (Pause) [In reaching for his tongs, Pete grabbed not only the tongs but also the hose to which the yo-yo is attached.]

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Uh-oh.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: What?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Hey, this ain't going to work, gang.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Why?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Well; see the...

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Here, wait a minute.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: See if you can slide that core tube...Wait. Which goes with...There you go. Beautiful. Right down in there. You got it. You got that one. Okay?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Yeah.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Boy, I drove a nice core tube in there. Well, it doesn't look any different, though, to the eye - halfway down. (That is, looking at the bottom of the upper section, the soil doesn't look different from the surface material) Try...(Pause) Loan me the tweezers (means tongs) a moment. See that cap right there? (Pause) The cap right there. (Pause)

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Yeah.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay. (Pause)

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Ohh. Can you haul the camera, Al?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Sure, I can just (garbled). Why don't I just lift this up? (Pause)

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Well, there goes the shovel (which has just fallen to the ground), but we can get that in a minute.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay. Help you, there.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Wait.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: (I'll stand) just a little closer. (Pause)

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Now; wait, wait. Hold it right there.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay. (Pause)

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: That a boy. Way to go. Thank you. (Pause) [In 1985, Artist Bean did one of his best known works, a painting called Helping Hands ( 37k ). The painting's only notable historical flaw is that they are both wearing cameras. It is a flaw of minor importance and the painting's popularity is well deserved.] [In 1996, Marv Hein pointed out that the side sunshields on the LEVA s are also missing in the painting.]

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Good show there, Commander! Let me hold on to that thing.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Wait.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay, twist it.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: You got her? (Pause) It's on there tight enough?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Yeah. 133:35:43 Bean: Okay. (Pause) Want the shovel back on here (on the extension handle)?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: I'll get it.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay. Looks good, Pete. (Pause)

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Gibson
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Pete, we copy that you finished the core tube. Is that affirm?

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Yes, sir. We got a double core tube, and all put together correctly.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Gibson
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Very good. Well done. Have you gotten the panorama? 133:36:15 Conrad: No, I'm going to get Al to do that right now. He's using my camera. His camera's had it. With the handle off it and everything, by the time we got done handling it, we got dirt all over the lens. We run out of film; we happen to have another magazine with us, or we could...

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: ...Don't change that; we just took that one off.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Well, we could do that or...

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Of course, we don't want to, but if we have to, I guess we can. Okay. Let me start this pan.

One thing we would like to make sure is that you remain away from directly below the Surveyor as you move up to it. That is, move up to it on one side or the other. Either north or s

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Okay. We concurred with that. We were talking about it last night. We're going to approach it from the side.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Gibson
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Roger. (Pause) [See, also, the discussion associated with LSE 7-6G .]

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: That's it, Pete. Pan's complete. Probably ought to get one of these rocks here and just throw it in the bag...

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Yeah. I think we ought to.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: You want to get this one? Or one (small enough) for a sample bag.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Let's sample a couple of these laying right over here.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Good idea. (Pause) Oh, boy.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Oh, wow; my ears just came back down. [Conrad - "I was stuffy. My inner ears were at 5 psi, and they just came down to three-seven."] [Jones - "It's been two hours and fifteen minutes since depress."]

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Bean
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: Just a second. (Pause)

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.speaker: Conrad
a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: I shouldn't have done that.

a12a_133_09_26_to_133_44_43.text: It's okay.
