a12a.1334601.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay. I got it, Pete.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Got her? [Al takes a down-Sun photo of the sampling area, AS12-48- 7082 , and then a cross-Sun, 7083 .]

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Yeah. Got a lot of those. We've got too many of them (that is, too many glass samples compared with rocks).

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Oh, we did get a lot of these?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Yeah. Why don't you get that? (Garbled)

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: We could get the rock with it. Look.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Okay. Get some rocks with it. That's a good idea. Hey, here's some rocks right here. There's a good rock. (Pause) You know, we keep collecting a lot of the same type of rock, because there just doesn't seem to be any other kinds around. (Pause) I haven't seen any microbreccia the whole day. I've looked around for it. All I have seen is some basalt; I've seen nothing that looked vesicular at all, except on the surface.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: I haven't either. [Al's "except on the surface" appears to be a reference to the numerous, small impact craters - known as zap pits - on the rocks.]

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: You know, that's real strange. It's not at all like Neil's rocks.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1334601.text: Roger. We copy those comments. Pete and Al, we show you're 2 plus 23 into the EVA and, based on a 4-hour EVA, you would be leaving the Surveyor at 2 plus 50. But don't rush; we'd like to make sure you get a good rest before you go into it (the crater).

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Okay.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Why don't you give me a rock or two, Pete? And I will stick in there. Got any spares? (Pause) There you go. Good rock. Good rock! (Pause)

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: (Chuckling) The world's greatest juggling act. (Garbled)

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Okay. That'll be it. (To Ed) We just made a sample of a glass bead and some local rock on the south edge of the Surveyor Crater, Houston. And they're going into bag 14D.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1334601.text: 14D. [Sample 12043 is a 4-cm, rounded, potato-shaped piece of basalt with zap pits. Sample 12044 consists of 92 grams of soil. The piece of 'beaded glass' Pete mentioned at 133:50:16 is labeled in a detail from 7083 but wasn't recognizable in the sample when it was examined at the Lunar Receiving Lab.]

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: (Garbled) brings back all of our training. I'm trying to remember who the guy was that kept saying "whatever you do, don't get dust on the gnomon." (Hearty laughter from both) Okay. We are going to jog on here for a little bit, Houston, and get a little bit closer to the Surveyor and look her over. (Pause)

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Yeah. Hey, that's...coming in from the south; looks like a good way, Pete.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: I'll tell you what I'm going to do, Al. I am just gonna lope right around here.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: That's what I mean. If you stay at this level, you'll end up at Surveyor.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: You're right.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Follow the contour lines.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: No problem at all, Houston! (Pause) Look at the (Surveyor) scoop sticking out. You couldn't see that before.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1334601.text: Pete and Al, could you give us a comment on how far you're sinking in?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1334601.text: Pete and Al, could you give us a comment on how far you're sinking in? [By now, Houston has realized that Pete has already started into the crater. Plans for this part of the traverse, while not spelled out in the checklists, were cautious. Al is carrying a tether (30-foot safety line) in his saddlebag. Because no one has yet worked on a slope as steep as the inner wall of Surveyor Crater, the plan is for one of them to stay on the rim, paying out the tether while the other makes his way part way down the slope. If the surface proves to be too soft for a safe descent, they can use the tether t

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Not sinking in very far at all. This is fairly firm stuff. And I'm down in the crater about the same distance down that Surveyor is. I'm just going around it radially (means "circumferentially"). Wouldn't you say so, Al?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Yeah, I would say that...I think Houston is just as concerned about us getting down in this crater. We been thinking about it, too, Houston. (Garbled under Pete)

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Okay. Yeah, don't worry about it, Houston, because, really, it's no strain; I'm 200 feet away from it; I'm at the same level; the ground is firm; and I can go right back up the way I came down with no strain at all.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: That's right.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1334601.text: Roger. Sounds good.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: It's just exactly the way we thought it was going to be when we were talking about it. (Responding to Ed) Yeah, it is. I don't think there'll be any sweat about it.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Al, I'll tell you what let's do. Get right over here, and we'll park all of our gear, take ourselves a little rest, go over your photo plan, and then we'll have at it. [Pete's statement about going over the "photo plan" may be a reference to the secret timer, although it may also refer to their official photography of the Surveyor. They won't get serious about looking for the timer until about 133:59:53 , once they've had a good look at the Surveyor and have described its condition to Houston.] [Conrad - "He asked us to take a rest, and we gave him a lot of smoke."] [Bean - "We told him, 'Yeah

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Okay. Let's go right over here.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: I will tell you what, why don't you get a photograph of it right now?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: It's a good place. Okay. Will do. Stop and do it right here. [Al takes AS12-48- 7084 to 7087. Their approximate location is marked in a labeled detail from the 5 February 2010 LROC image.]

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: (I'm) trying to see which way it landed.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1334601.text: Okay, Pete and Al, when you are looking at it there, would you also try to determine whether there is any effect from the dust during the (LM) descent? That is, could you determine whether there is more dust on either the west or the east side of any of the bays, and the north or the south side of the (Surveyor TV) camera? [The Surveyor III TV camera is on display at the National Air and Space Museum in Washington D. C. Photo by Ulrich Lotzmann. See, also, a photo of the camera being examined at the Hughes Aircraft Company in April 1970.]

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Okay. We sure will. I actually flew around it; however, I probably passed closer to it (on the north side of the crater) than I am parked to it right now. No, that's not really true. I'll tell you, the way that dust was going, it probably went right over top of it.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: You know, that's right. Any dust you had on the edge would never go down to this crater. [In the absence of an atmosphere, once dust and small rocks blown away by the LM exhaust have traveled very far, the exhaust gases become too tenuous to have any further effect and they follow ballistic trajectories. If the particles were launched at any appreciable distance from the rim and at the apparent speeds Pete was seeing, few would land in the crater. However, it is not clear that this happened. They will find dust on the spacecraft, some of which may have been blown on during the descent. An alte

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Yeah. What happened to your volume, Al?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: I don't know. It sounds good to me.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Yeah, you just...

a12a.1334601.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1334601.text: We read you both loud and clear.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Okay. I'm not talking loud enough.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Okay. No problem.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: I'm going to mosey up here just a little, Pete, without any tools, which makes it pretty easy. [For the next minute, they engage in excited, overlapping conversation.]

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Look, I'll tell you what. Let's leave the whole...(Very brief pause while he reconsiders) I tell you what; let's take the tool carrier with us!...

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Yeah. ...

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: ...I think we can go right up the other rim and around to...

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: ...Sure. Right on out...

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: ...that big blocky baby (Block Crater) there and...

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: ...Hey, I'll bet we could get...

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: ...we could get...

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: ...bedrock right over there at that...

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Huh?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: ...neat crater (Block, again). Where all that rock is just...

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: (Garbled)

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: ...back of the LM. (Pause) Turned up (garbled)...

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: You know, I could have landed the LM in the bottom of that (Surveyor) crater. It would have scared me to death, but...(Chuckles) (Pause) [Pete's comment at 133:55:35 about taking the HTC with them when they move down closer to the Surveyor may be related to the secret timer, but it is also related to an option they have had - if the walk from the rim to the Surveyor was proving at all hazardous - of putting the HTC down at any point during the trip and then, after completing their work at the Surveyor, retrieving it before continuing the geology traverse. In indication of this option is the no

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Let's see. Okay, Pete. Would you carry the hand-tool carrier down there?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Whoop.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: You want me take some pictures up here around it?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Okay. Now look. You can see which way it came in. See the way this gear pad dug in over there...

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Yeah.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: ...dug up dirt? They're still setting there.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Yeah. It's going to make a good shot. [The Surveyor bounced after landing and slid a short way downhill. As Pete and Al can already see, the downhill gearpad dug itself into the surface a few inches as it slid.] [Apparently, Al moves counter-clockwise around the crater, taking pictures as he goes. His movements can be seen from the changes from frame to frame of the relative positions of Surveyor III and the LM. Their approximate location is marked in a labeled detail from the 5 February 2010 LROC image. The frames in this sequence are AS12-48- 7088 to 7093 .] [Frame 7088 shows Surveyor III wi

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: (According to the checklist) we're not supposed to take pictures of that leg. We'll have to do it, though. (Pause; breathing fairly heavily as he maneuvers to take pictures). Beautiful. Beautiful sight. You know, this one (meaning Surveyor III)'s brown and I don't remember ours being brown there at the Cape. [During training in Florida, they used a mock-up of the Surveyor, which was white and not brown.]

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: (It's) kind of a light tan or maybe that's the way it's changed color. What color was this one, Houston? White? When it started out?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1334601.text: Stand by on that.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Yeah. It looks a light tan now. (Pause) Hey, this crater isn't as steep as we thought, Pete.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Uh-uh. And I'd better be careful. I'm going to get dust on her (the Surveyor).

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Yeah. (Pause) I'll stop here, and this will be my last picture. (Pause) [This last picture in the approach sequence may be AS12-48- 7093 .]

a12a.1334601.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1334601.text: Al, the equipment bays were white on the side, and the scoop itself was a light blue.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Well, it's kind of a...Well, we'll get down there and get closer inspection. What was the general color of the structure? For example, all of the struts and the like?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1334601.text: That's all white. The equipment bays and the primary structure was all painted with a white paint.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Sort of turned tan or something. We'll have to look at it more closely.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: No; that's what happened.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Just changed color, huh?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: It sure has. The Sun's cooked that paint brown. [At 134:29:54 they realize that the brown color is the product of a fine coating of dust.] [Conrad - (Having read ahead) "You're talking about it way out here at 134:29:54 ."] [Jones - "That's where you rub it."] [Bean - "I don't even remember that."] [Conrad - "I don't either."] [Bean, from the 1969 Technical Debriefing - "One comment about the comm between MCCH (Mission Control Center, Houston) and ourselves up there; I don't know, from their point of view, what they thought, but we were getting about the right amount of information every time

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Can't imagine what. You know, it's funny. On the slopes here, it's just a little bit softer. But there's no tendency to slip down or anything like that.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: I know.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: I don't think it (the soil)'s any deeper. A little softer maybe. Maybe a little deeper. Why don't I move this (HTC) down here just a little bit closer, Pete?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Okay.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Then we'll take the rest down here where we can see it better.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Okay. Let's just make sure we don't get any dirt down there on it.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Okay. We'll walk real slow. (Pause) Hey, you can see...Look at there where it dug those scoops. You can still see the...Boy, that's going to make some beautiful pictures on the way that's weathered since...Doesn't look like the pictures we saw of this a long time ago. That's going to be good. [The accompanying illustration shows the locations of the Surveyor III scoop marks. The figure was taken from page 58 of the NASA report SP-284, "Analysis of Material and Photographs returned by Apollo 12" and was digitized by Marv Hein. Jon Hancock has scanned a diagram found in a Hughes Corp. house maga

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Oh, that is interesting! What in the hell...

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Look at how it's kind of made them into...Once again, it looks like something has rained on it. They've taken on a little...

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Wonder if that was from us?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Oh, no! I don't think so. (Pause) Hey, you notice, there's a general trend of lines along here from the north...that would be the northeast to the southwest. See those little lines running along through the crater here?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Yeah.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: I think I'll take a picture of that. (Pause) [Al takes a mini-pan of the "little lines", AS12-48- 7094 , 7095 , and 7096 . Assembly by Dave Byrne.] [Al then turns to his right and takes a picture, 7097 , of Block Crater, and finally, turns back to his left to take 7098 . Al's approximate location is marked in a labeled detail from the 5 February 2010 LROC image.] [Vlad Pustynski has combined 7094-97 with a portion of 7092 to make a high-resolution, seamless version ( 9 Mb ).

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Boy, this thing (the 70 mm camera) is dusty. 7, 8. (Pause) Just do this. (Pause) Yeah, this has those lineal patterns here, Houston. Right down inside the crater.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: And they're not laying at all in the same direction - I mean, it's not from us - not from the LM.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Uh-uh.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1334601.text: Roger.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: I tell you what...

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Hey, Al, did you get a picture right across there?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Yes, I did, Pete. Why don't you go ahead and put this together?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Okay. (Pause) [This is where they start preparing for the Dual Photo. Al's statement "Why don't you go ahead and put this together" probably means mount the extension handle on the HTC.] [Conrad - "Yeah, I think this is where we start trying to do that. I think it fit on the tool carrier. Let's take a look at the drawing."] [We looked in Judy Allton's Apollo tool book and found a relevant photo ( Fig. 61 ) and drawing ( Fig. 62 ). The drawing shows the Apollo 14 configuration with a camera staff holding the 16mm movie camera and the photo ( AS14-68-9405 ) shows the Apollo 14 HTC mounted on the

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Borrow your tongs while you're there. Just a second. I'll give them back to you. (Pause) [Al may want the tongs to fish around in the bag for the timer or, perhaps to get a sample bag that's dropped out.]

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Good place to rest. (Long Pause; searching unsuccessfully) I'll be darned.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: (Installing the extension handle) Is that the way that thing goes?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Now...What's that? Let me hold one end of it. There you go. There you go. I think that's it. (Long Pause)

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Pete, could you hold that a minute?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Wait just a second.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Okay. [Al may be asking Pete to take some of the things he's taking out of the bag as he searches for the timer.]

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: What are you trying to get?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: (Garbled) I dropped something down in there. (Pause)

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: (Putting something down) Okay there. Now I can hold it. What do you want me to hold?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Hold that (LMP) camera a second. (Pause) Got it?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Why don't we just throw that (LMP) camera away?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Well, I was thinking of that earlier and decided that, since this one broke, we might have to put that one on. [Al seems to be saying that, although the CDR camera he is currently wearing seems to be working, he'd like to keep the LMP camera as a backup. Because the LMP camera no longer has a thumbwheel they might have to use it handheld, but they would be able to take pictures.]

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: (Garbled)...

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: (Garbled) the reliability. Doesn't much make it. (Long Pause) [Although neither Pete nor Al remembers the details of the search, the flavor of their memories is that Al was holding the HTC, rummaging through it and pulling out sample bags which he loaded into Pete's arms; or that Pete was holding the HTC and, in his arms, the samples Al was pulling out.]

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: (Still unsuccessful) (Garbled, but originally transcribed as "Makes you kind of mad".)

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Huh?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Let me look down there just once more. (Pause) (Garbled) (Pause) There you go. (Long Pause)

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Oh, boy. (Pause)

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Look again.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Yeah. I'm holding it (the HTC) with this post.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Okay.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: (Hoping that the timer wasn't in the HTC after all) Wait a minute. (Pause) What's in your (saddle)bag, here? (Pause) Yeah; there's a film magazine (but no timer). (Long Pause)

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Let me borrow your little thing here while we rest. (Long Pause) [Again, Al may be borrowing Pete's tongs to retrieve dropped samples.]

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Remove that (Al's Hasselblad mount) handle and throw it away.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Okay. That's a good idea.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: (Get) junk out of there we don't need. (Long Pause)

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Try at this end. (Long Pause) Ahh! (I've) had it (that is, he's had enough).

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Huh?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: (Giving up) Forget it. (Pause)

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: I'll tell you what. Why don't you mosey down there and start taking some photographs?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: That's a good idea. Got your cuff checklist there?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Sure.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Okay. [Rather than take the time to look at his own checklist, Al will have Pete read the steps. They had planned to do this and, consequently, all the details of the Surveyor photo plan are also printed on Pete's cuff checklist pages 14 and 15 .]

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: The first thing is photo bay A: (f/)11, 15 feet (focus), one picture.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: 11, 15; let me get it set. 11, 15. Boy, that's turned just kind of a light tan hasn't it, Pete?

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: It sure has.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: And some of the things are even a dark brown.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: Yeah, you're closer than 15. Don't go any closer.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: Yeah. Maybe I'd better back up a little.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: That a boy.

a12a.1334601.speaker: Bean
a12a.1334601.text: How's that? [Al takes AS12-48- 7099 and 7100 . Jim Scotti has produced a anaglyph from his own scans.]

a12a.1334601.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1334601.text: That a boy...

a12a.1334601.text: My compliments to the CapCom. [Armstrong and Aldrin each had a single checklist page sewn onto their suit sleeve. Apollo 12 and the subsequent missions all involved so many EVA tasks that multi-page checklists were essential. For Apollo 12, the checklist became a set of moderately stiff pages bound in a spiral wire - rather like a school notebook - but with the wire fixed to a metal band that conformed to the cylindrical shape of the astronaut's arm, convex upward. This configuration ensured that, when a page was turned, it would lie flat along the arm. The design was one of elegant simplicity

a12a.1334601.text: Okay. [Pete's pictures of Al are AS12-48- 7135 and 7136 .]

a12a.1334601.text: Okay.

a12a.1334601.text: (Garbled)
