a12a.1351237.text: Okay, Pete. Go ahead. (Long Pause while they get the attachment hardware back out to Pete) [Pete will now hook the ETB to the line.]

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Dum, dum, dum, dum. Dum dee dum dum. (Pause) Really...Getting in and out of these shadows really gets eerie looking. Okay, Al, if you'll wait just a minute. (Pause) There you go.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Okey-dokey. Coming in. (Pause)

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Okay, just a second. Passing over the thing (the porch lip)?

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: You'd better believe it.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: I can't see.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Okay, pull up a little bit and I'll bring it in.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: The Sun's shining right in my eyes.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: That's it.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: In?

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: It's in.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Beautiful job; just throw the LEC out. Okay, Houston. ETB is in with the (LM TV) camera and all the film, and so forth and so on.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1351237.text: Roger, Pete. Copy you got the ETB in with the TV camera, close-up stereo (film magazine), and the (70 mm) film packs.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Okay, now, Pete, here comes the LEC, so watch out.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: All right. (Hearty Conrad laugh)

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Man, that really comes out, doesn't it? Gee, that went 50 feet!

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Okay, let's see. Have I forgotten anything? Forgotten anything?

a12a.1351237.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1351237.text: Pete, you didn't "roger" the film pack. Do you have all the film packs and the close-up stereo film, as well as the (LM) TV in that ETB? 135:17:59 Conrad: Okay. Close-up stereo film was in the ETB, two black-and-white magazines and one camera. I threw the other (70 mm) camera away because it was broken. And the TV camera went up, so I believe we've got everything, Ed.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1351237.text: Okay. You got the...Also the one camera which had the third film pack on?

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: The third film pack never got used.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Yeah, it did too, Pete.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Oh, did you?

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Yeah.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Oh, I'm sorry. Okay, we got three film packs and one camera up there right now. How's that?

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Did you send the film back up?

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Yeah.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Okay, we sent all three film packs back up. [As we will discover at 138:33:55 , the third film magazine was left outside, probably in Al's saddlebag. It was a color magazine with pictures of Earthrise, etc. taken prior to the descent. It was never used on the lunar surface.] [Bean - "We looked in the ETB later and found that it wasn't there."] [Conrad - "But we had both of the black and white magazines, and that was the most important."] [Jones - "The other mag hadn't been on your checklist."] [Bean - "Well, why was it on the pad? Did we just stick it over there?"] [Conrad - "I don't know how

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Oh, oh, oh, oh. There is something I wanted to...

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: That's my low water pressure, Houston. I just turned off my water. That's good.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1351237.text: Stand by on that, Al. Pete, also how about the tools?

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Yes, sir. (Long Pause)

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: You might want to turn off your water too, Pete.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Yeah, I knew...I was sitting here thinking there was something I ought to do. (Pause) Mine's off.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Okay. (Pause) (I'm) out of your way. [Al has gotten behind the hatch, opening it as far as possible against his legs so that Pete can get in.]

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Okay. Houston, I guess you can mark me off the lunar surface; I'm on the footpad.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1351237.text: Roger. We got that, Pete, at 3 hours and 50 minutes into the EVA. (Pause)

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Okay, up-a (sic) the ladder I come. Heigh-ho, heigh-ho, heigh-ho. Boy, I'll tell you, Al, that LEC really got me dirty.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Yeah, it flips that dirt all around. (Long Pause)

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Heigh-ho. Oh, wait a minute; I know what I want to do. (Getting the map, see comments below) There we go. (Long Pause)

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: You want to give me that piece of paper?

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: I couldn't get it up. I dropped it.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: That's too bad. [Bean - "'Piece of paper', what's that? Do you suppose you started up the ladder and dropped the map?"] [Conrad - "I don't remember."] [Bean - "I'll bet this all has to do with the map. I bet when you said, 'I've got something else I want to do' you go over and get the map (out of the HTC)."] [Conrad - "Probably."] [Bean - "You start up the ladder, the thing falls out of your hand - as I remember - and then you don't want to get down and go find it, 'cause you've already said you're off the surface. That's what I think happened. You went over and remembered it, and then it just

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Okay, Houston, that's my PLSS feedwater (tone because the supply has been turned off), no sweat.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Head down, come down. That's better. Move to your left slightly.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1351237.text: Roger, Pete.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: That's it; come on in. Come to your left a little bit. Okay, come on up. Little more to the left. Just right.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Huh?

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: You're just right. Scoot in there. Got to kind of scoot a little bit further in. You got it made! Bump into me, now. Okay. Okay.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: (Garbled) let me close the hatch.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: " Forward hatch , closed and locked" as soon as you're out of the way. [They are now on Surface Checklist page Sur-92.]

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Say again?

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: And I wonder what that's from.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: What?

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: That little...Wait, you need to kick out that piece...

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: I think that came from off of the landing gear. (Pause; Garbled)

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Lock her up, babe. (Joking about how dirty Pete has gotten) You are nice and clean. (Dick) Gordon will be glad to see you.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: One hatch closed.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Okay, check that ( dump valve ) for Auto. I think it is, but you can see...

a12a.1351237.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1351237.text: Yankee Clipper; Houston. (No answer)

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Yeah. I'm flipping. You just...One hatch (dump valve), Auto.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Okay. Okay, let me move out of the way. "Both ( dump valves ) to Auto."

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Tell me when (to start the repressurization).

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: "Lighting: Annunciator and Numerics, Bright."

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Wait a minute. (Pause as he turns to change the lighting)

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Okay. " Cabin Repress Valve Auto." (Pause)

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: It's Auto.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: " Press Regs A and B (to) Cabin." Master Alarm will come on, and CABIN warning light . Okay, here comes the O2. (Repress audible) And the pressure is rising. Looks good right this minute. (Pause) Okay, that's normal. PLSS O2, Off. [Al's O2 and pressure warning flags may have come on, a possibility mentioned in the checklist. Like all the Caution-and-Warning lights on Panel 1, the Cabin light is red to indicate a warning. All the C&W lights on Panel 2 are yellow to indicate cautions.]

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Say again?

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: PLSS O2 Off when you get 3.6 (psi). (Pause) [There is no mention in the checklist of turning the PLSS O2 off at a specific pressure, only that they verify that the cabin pressure is increasing before they do so. However, 3.6 is about the pressure they've been using in the suit and it seems a reasonable decision point on turning the PLSS O2 off.]

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: I can't get mine. Can you get it?

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Let me see if I can.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: I can't get it, Al.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Just a second. Let me get mine, too. (Pause) Okay.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Did you get mine off?

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: (Garbled), just a second.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: I can't hear you. (Long Pause)

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Your O2 is Off. Everything's Off, Pete. (Pause) And the cabin pressure is...

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Cabin's 4 pounds.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Okay, going to be taking mine (his PLSS O2) off. (Pause)

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: (Sound of repress ends) That's it.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: That's it, babes.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: What's the rest of the checklist?

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: I hope that (hatch) seal is good.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Say again?

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: I didn't check that seal real closely (for dust).

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: I didn't either.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Gibson
a12a.1351237.text: Yankee Clipper, Houston. 135:24:50 Bean: Okay. It says here: "Verify cabin pressure increasing." (Garbled) "PLSS O2, Off. Activate OPS purge valve to depress suit as required." (Pause)

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Wow, that's better. (Pause) Hey, don't take your helmet off! [They will do a jettison in a little while and don't want to take their helmets off until that is done.]

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: That's right. Just your gloves.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Do we do that?

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Yeah, we do, because we have to put on our other ones. (Pause) Okay. [There is no mention of any but the EV gloves in the surface checklist prior to the jettison. They need to get their gloves off, primarily because they have quite a bit to do to get ready for the jettison, such as doffing the PLSSs and OPSs, checking the OPSs to make sure they are in good working order, getting the jettison bag packed, etc.]

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Okay, let me read to you.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Yeah.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Okay. "Cabin Repress valve closes at 4.4. Verify cabin pressure stable at 4.6." Looks good to me, Pete. "Post-EVA systems Config(uration): Verify EV circ..." Look over there and make sure Suit Fan 1 (circuit breaker) is closed. And I'll make sure that Suit Fan Delta-P (breaker) is closed.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Okay, just a second. (Pause as he turns) Suit Fan 1 is closed.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Suit Fan Delta-P, closed. Okay. We're going to get some ECS caution and H2O SEP component lights out.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: I can't hear you. What?

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Our ECS Caution and H2O Sep(arator) component lights will go out in a minute. Doff your gloves.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Conrad
a12a.1351237.text: Everything's out.

a12a.1351237.speaker: Bean
a12a.1351237.text: Okay. "Descent H2O valve open." Okay, that (getting a drink of water)'s a good idea, boy. (Pause) (Remove) purge valves. (Pause) Surveyor Crater and Surveyor III Apollo 12 Journal Return to Orbit

a12a_139_03_02_to_139_03_11.speaker: Conrad
a12a_139_03_02_to_139_03_11.text: Houston. Intrepid, picking up the launch Prep Verb 98 at LO minus 02:50.

a12a_139_03_02_to_139_03_11.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_139_03_02_to_139_03_11.text: This is Apollo Control Houston. We're at 139 hours, 5 minutes into the flight. Meanwhile in Mission Control Center Houston, we are having a shift change. Flight Director, Pete Frank, and members of his Orange Team are now aboard, and a News Conference will be held in the News Center within the next few minutes with Flight Director, Gerry Griffin. We're at 139 hours, 6 minutes into the flight and this is Apollo Control Houston.

a12a_139_12_05_to_139_12_12.speaker: Bean
a12a_139_12_05_to_139_12_12.text: Okay, Houston. You see that 2127. That's the same thing we had before, also.

a12a_139_12_05_to_139_12_12.speaker: Gibson
a12a_139_12_05_to_139_12_12.text: Roger, Intrepid. Me copy, and we concur. We expect it.

a12a_139_14_05_to_139_14_58.speaker: Gibson
a12a_139_14_05_to_139_14_58.text: We have a update on the star Ar - Arcturus on page 102 of the Surface Checklist. We'd like you to use Procyon, 16, or Sirius, 15, and that's detent 1. [Pause.]

a12a_139_14_05_to_139_14_58.speaker: Conrad
a12a_139_14_05_to_139_14_58.text: Okay. And we passed self-test all right.

a12a_139_14_05_to_139_14_58.speaker: Conrad
a12a_139_14_05_to_139_14_58.text: Are you ready for E-Mod dump?

a12a_139_14_05_to_139_14_58.speaker: Gibson
a12a_139_14_05_to_139_14_58.text: That's affirmative. We're ready for the E-Mod.

a12a_139_16_31_to_139_16_45.speaker: Gibson
a12a_139_16_31_to_139_16_45.text: If you will give us P00 and Accept, we'll give you a CSM state vector and RLS update.

a12a_139_20_09_to_139_21_10.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_20_09_to_139_21_10.text: Yankee Clipper, Houston. Loud and clear.

a12a_139_20_09_to_139_21_10.speaker: Gordon
a12a_139_20_09_to_139_21_10.text: Well, hello there, stranger. How are you?

a12a_139_20_09_to_139_21_10.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_20_09_to_139_21_10.text: Morning, Dick. We are fine. How are you?

a12a_139_20_09_to_139_21_10.speaker: Gordon
a12a_139_20_09_to_139_21_10.text: Well, pretty good. I hope you would like to have some company for a change.

a12a_139_20_09_to_139_21_10.speaker: Gordon
a12a_139_20_09_to_139_21_10.text: As a matter of fact, I just finished that. I sure do; got everything in order; ready to go towards the LM and bring back [garble] that's quite a chore; keeping this thing clean.

a12a_139_20_09_to_139_21_10.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_20_09_to_139_21_10.text: Roger. You got a couple of coal miners coming up to see you.

a12a_139_20_09_to_139_21_10.speaker: Gordon
a12a_139_20_09_to_139_21_10.text: That's okay. I'll be glad to see them.

a12a_139_20_09_to_139_21_10.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_20_09_to_139_21_10.text: Intrepid, Houston. The computer is yours. Break. Yankee Clipper, if you will go P00 and Accept, we have an uplink.

a12a_139_23_14_to_139_23_57.speaker: Conrad
a12a_139_23_14_to_139_23_57.text: Houston, you got the lift-off time for me?

a12a_139_23_14_to_139_23_57.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_23_14_to_139_23_57.text: Intrepid, Houston. Your lift-off time is l42:03:47.

a12a_139_23_14_to_139_23_57.speaker: Gordon
a12a_139_23_14_to_139_23_57.text: Okay. And Jerry, will you find out what they want to do about this battery charge, because I'm using the bus ties during the rendezvous?

a12a_139_23_14_to_139_25_41.speaker: Conrad
a12a_139_23_14_to_139_25_41.text: Houston, you got the lift-off time for me?

a12a_139_23_14_to_139_25_41.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_23_14_to_139_25_41.text: Intrepid, Houston. Your lift-off time is l42:03:47.

a12a_139_23_14_to_139_25_41.speaker: Gordon
a12a_139_23_14_to_139_25_41.text: Okay. And Jerry, will you find out what they want to do about this battery charge, because I'm using the bus ties during the rendezvous?

a12a_139_23_14_to_139_25_41.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_23_14_to_139_25_41.text: Yankee Clipper, Houston. Why don't you figure on terminating the battery charge at LOS?

a12a_139_23_14_to_139_25_41.speaker: Gordon
a12a_139_23_14_to_139_25_41.text: All right; I could let it go until I [garble] just before lift-off. That way it might take it all the way up.

a12a_139_23_14_to_139_25_41.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_23_14_to_139_25_41.text: Clipper, Houston. We prefer that you terminate at LOS on this pass.

a12a_139_23_14_to_139_25_41.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_23_14_to_139_25_41.text: Roger. That would be one less thing for us to keep track of prior to lift-off.

a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.speaker: Conrad
a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.text: Say, Houston; Intrepid.

a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.text: Intrepid, Houston. Go.

a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.speaker: Bean
a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.text: Roger. When you look out the AOT in the dark quadrant? You can see these lights - particles of light, flashes of light just seem to come from - in this case, I'm looking in quadrant 1 which is the left one. It's coming from behind me, the left, and they're just sailing off in space. I was thinking they're dropping from my water boiler, but it looks like some of those things are escaping the Moon. They really haul out of here and just press off at the stars.

a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.text: Yankee Clipper, Houston with a P22 tracking PAD.

a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.speaker: Gordon
a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.text: Go ahead.

a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.text: Roger. Your target is LM; T-1 is 139:57:39; T-2 is 140:02:38; south 05; latitude is minus 3...

a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.speaker: Gordon
a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.text: Roger. T 112...

a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.text: Latitude, minus 3.036; longitude over 2 is minus 11.709; altitude minus 1.13. If you want to take photos, your DAC settings are 1/60th, 1 over 60, one SP, 1 FPS, and C-EX film. You're - you should be at zero local horizontal rather than 22-degrees pitchdown. Over.

a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.speaker: Gordon
a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.text: Roger. Understand. T-1, 139:57:39, T-2, 140:02:38, 5 miles South, latitude is minus 3.036, longitude over 2 is minus 11.709; altitude minus 1.13 and [garble] information. I will not use it.

a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.text: Roger, Dick. And I've got a Rev 30 map update when you're ready. [Pause.]

a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.speaker: Gordon
a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.text: Go ahead.

a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.speaker: Gordon
a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.text: Roger. Yankee Clipper, we copied.

a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.text: Okay. And, Dick, I've got your consumables update when you are ready.

a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.speaker: Gordon
a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.text: Go ahead.

a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.text: Roger. At a GET of 139 plus 20, RCS total was 56 percent; Alfa is 58; Bravo, 56; Charlie, 56; Delta, 55; hydrogen tank 1 is 49.9; tank 2 is 49.8; oxygen, 52.7 and 54.4. Over.

a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.speaker: Gordon
a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.text: Roger. I copy that. And my rendezvous radar transponder self-check is okay.

a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.text: Roger.

a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.speaker: Gordon
a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.text: Hey, Jerry, I would like to have a DAP update also, please.

a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.text: Roger, Dick. Stand by. We'll get it for you. [Long pause.]

a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.speaker: Conrad
a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.text: Okay, Houston. Looking at the DSKY torquing angles?

a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_27_17_to_139_34_13.text: Roger. We see them, Pete.

a12a_139_35_19_to_139_35_35.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_35_19_to_139_35_35.text: Roger, Pete. How's your drinking water intake then since you got back in? You been replacing quite a bit of it?

a12a_139_39_19_to_139_41_35.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_39_19_to_139_41_35.text: Yankee Clipper, Houston. If you'll give us P00 and Accept, we have another LM state vector for you.

a12a_139_39_19_to_139_41_35.speaker: Gordon
a12a_139_39_19_to_139_41_35.text: Okay, Houston. I'm going to stop my roll [garble] here. Okay. Go ahead.

a12a_139_39_19_to_139_41_35.speaker: Conrad
a12a_139_39_19_to_139_41_35.text: All right, Houston. Is there any objection if we track him when he goes by this time? And do you have the OSCIL[?], or don't you want us to do it?

a12a_139_39_19_to_139_41_35.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_39_19_to_139_41_35.text: Intrepid, Houston. We hadn't really planned on doing a P22 on this pass.

a12a_139_39_19_to_139_41_35.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_39_19_to_139_41_35.text: Okay. Break. Yankee Clipper, Houston. I've got your DAP update.

a12a_139_39_19_to_139_41_35.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_39_19_to_139_41_35.text: Okay. About the only change you need is you need to go to 0.5-degree deadband, so R1 should read 1110.1.

a12a_139_39_19_to_139_41_35.speaker: Gordon
a12a_139_39_19_to_139_41_35.text: Okay. Are the weights and trim verified yet?

a12a_139_39_19_to_139_41_35.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_39_19_to_139_41_35.text: Roger, Dick. Your weights and your trims are good.

a12a_139_39_19_to_139_41_35.speaker: Gordon
a12a_139_39_19_to_139_41_35.text: Okay. That's what I was worried about. Thank you. I'll probably go to a half a degree a second during the rendezvous because those maneuvers are pretty long.

a12a_139_52_15_to_139_53_15.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_52_15_to_139_53_15.text: Stand by, Clipper. Break. Intrepid, this is Houston. Clipper wants to know if you're up VHF.

a12a_139_52_15_to_139_53_15.speaker: Conrad
a12a_139_52_15_to_139_53_15.text: No, but we will come up VHF.

a12a_139_52_15_to_139_53_15.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_52_15_to_139_53_15.text: Roger. Break. Clipper, Houston. Intrepid says he'll be up.

a12a_139_52_15_to_139_53_15.speaker: Gordon
a12a_139_52_15_to_139_53_15.text: Okay. Ask him whether he wants us up VHF A or B Simplex.

a12a_139_52_15_to_139_53_15.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_52_15_to_139_53_15.text: Clipper, Houston. What would you like, VHF A or B Simplex?

a12a_139_52_15_to_139_53_15.speaker: Gordon
a12a_139_52_15_to_139_53_15.text: How about the normal VHF ranging [garble]?

a12a_139_52_15_to_139_53_15.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_52_15_to_139_53_15.text: Intrepid, Houston. Come up on VHF ranging configuration. Over.

a12a_139_52_15_to_139_53_15.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_139_52_15_to_139_53_15.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. We presently show Yankee Clipper in an orbit of 61.7 nautical miles by 58.7 nautical miles. We're now at 139 hours, 53 minutes into the flight. This is Apollo Control, Houston. We're at 139 hours, 58 minutes now in the flight. Our display here in Mission Control shows that the concentric sequence initiate burn...

a12a_139_58_26.speaker: Carr
a12a_139_58_26.text: Roger, Dick. Are you going to use the zero-degree pitch or 22-degree pitch down for this pass?

a12a_139_58_26.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_139_58_26.text: The concentric sequence initiate burn is scheduled for 143 hours, 1 minute, 50 seconds with a Delta-V of 49.2 feet per second. This burn done at apolune following lift-off has the effect of raising the perilune a half a revolution later. We would look at numbers at that time for Intrepid of 46.8 by 43.6, some 15 nautical miles below the Yankee Clipper. We're 2 hours, 4 minutes, 18 seconds away from Time Of Ignition. And this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Intrepid, Houston. Go.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Bean
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Got sort of an interesting thing going on AGS right now. I didn't notice earlier, but it may just be because the lights are brighter now. I'm getting an all 8's flash on both the address and the information registers at about one-fifth the brilliance of the normal numbers. And a - it's pulsing every second.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Roger, Al.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Bean
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: If I turn down the illumination level just a little bit, it's not noticeable. [Long pause.]

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Bean
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Hello, Houston; Intrepid. You ready for my RCS hot fire?

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Intrepid, Houston. Roger. Fire away.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Conrad
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Okay.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Intrepid, Houston.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Bean
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Go.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Roger, Al. Fredo is here. He and I have both seen that phenomena on your DEDA during testing of most all the spacecrafts up at Bethpage, and it's probably an EMI.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Conrad
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: That's what we've been talking about, but we thought we'd just touch in on it.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Bean
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: When you go to your roll rate, roll left, pitch up...

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Roger. I think TRW's got a workup on this problem.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Conrad
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Okay.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Conrad
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Here you go, Houston, with roll, pitch, and yaw.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Roger, Pete. [Long pause.]

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Intrepid, Houston.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Conrad
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Don't panic. We just blew over our S-band erectable, and we're up on our steerable.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Roger. I was just going to tell you, Pete, we lost some of the data on that fire check.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Conrad
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Okay. You want me to give to you again?

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Stand by. I'll tell you what we need.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Conrad
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: I never gave you yaw anyway.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Pete, can you just start over from the beginning?

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Conrad
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Conrad
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Pitch up is the only one that didn't sound right.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Intrepid, Houston. I've got a K-factor update for you when you're ready.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Conrad
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Okay.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Roger. R-1 is 00140; R-2 is all zips, R-3 is 00033.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Conrad
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Okay. 000 - 00140; all zips; three zips 33.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Roger.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Conrad
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Okay. How'd the hot fire look?

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Intrepid, Houston. That went kind of fast. Give us a chance to take a look at our tapes.

a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.speaker: Conrad
a12a_140_09_30_to_140_14_47.text: Okay.

a12a_140_15_50_to_140_17_54.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_15_50_to_140_17_54.text: Intrepid, Houston. The passive seismometer just verified that you did do your hot fire.

a12a_140_15_50_to_140_17_54.speaker: Conrad
a12a_140_15_50_to_140_17_54.text: Does the passive seismometer say my hot fire is Go? [Long pause.]

a12a_140_15_50_to_140_17_54.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_140_15_50_to_140_17_54.text: This is Apollo Control Houston. Jerry Carr reported recordings of the panel on the passive seismometer verifying the hot fire on the RCS. This data was received in our Experiment Staff Support Room.

a12a_140_15_50_to_140_17_54.speaker: Gordon
a12a_140_15_50_to_140_17_54.text: Houston, are you ready for our gyro torquing angles?

a12a_140_15_50_to_140_17_54.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_15_50_to_140_17_54.text: Clipper, Houston. Roger. Go ahead. [Long pause.]

a12a_140_15_50_to_140_17_54.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_15_50_to_140_17_54.text: Intrepid, Houston. I have a LM ascent PAD and a CSI PAD.

a12a_140_15_50_to_140_17_54.speaker: Conrad
a12a_140_15_50_to_140_17_54.text: Okay. Just a second. Are you ready for my - the rest of my hot fire?

a12a_140_15_50_to_140_17_54.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_15_50_to_140_17_54.text: Roger. We're ready. Go ahead. Break. Clipper, you can go ahead and torque.

a12a_140_19_08_to_140_24_48.speaker: Conrad
a12a_140_19_08_to_140_24_48.text: Okay. I gave you an extra pitchup fire because we were photographing the effects on the ground. It's quite spectacular.

a12a_140_19_08_to_140_24_48.speaker: Bean
a12a_140_19_08_to_140_24_48.text: And we're ready to copy the launch PAD.

a12a_140_19_08_to_140_24_48.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_19_08_to_140_24_48.text: Roger. LM ascent PAD follows: T IG 142:03:47.00; Noun 76, 5535.0, 0037.0, plus 000.2; DEDA 47 is plus 37364, plus 05607, plus 58642, plus 56955; DEDA 465 is plus 00370; DEDA 546 is NA; ignition one Rev late is 144:02:09; LM weight, 10789; CSM weight, 35390. Over.

a12a_140_19_08_to_140_24_48.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_19_08_to_140_24_48.text: That's affirmative, Al. P32 CSI PAD follows. Noun 11, 143:01:50.60; Noun 37, 144:38, all zips; Noun 81, 0492, all zips; DEDA 373 is 01818, 275 is 02780; AGS Delta-Vs, plus 0492, all zips, plus 0010. Over.

a12a_140_19_08_to_140_24_48.speaker: Bean
a12a_140_19_08_to_140_24_48.text: Roger. 143:01:50.60; 144:38, all zero's, 0492, all zero's, 01818, 02780, plus 0492, All zeros, plus 0010.

a12a_140_19_08_to_140_24_48.speaker: Conrad
a12a_140_19_08_to_140_24_48.text: Okay, Houston. I'm standing by for your up-data link and the LGC gyro compensation.

a12a_140_19_08_to_140_24_48.speaker: Gordon
a12a_140_19_08_to_140_24_48.text: Houston, this is Clipper. I copied those Pads.

a12a_140_19_08_to_140_24_48.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_19_08_to_140_24_48.text: Roger, Dick. You can terminate your battery Bravo charge now, and we'd like to have you put your O 2 tank 1 heaters and your hydrogen tank 2 heaters back to Auto. And dump your waste water to between 5...

a12a_140_27_22_to_140_29_47.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_27_22_to_140_29_47.text: Pete, we'll be setting your gyro compensation uplink to you after you've done your second P57.

a12a_140_27_22_to_140_29_47.speaker: Conrad
a12a_140_27_22_to_140_29_47.text: Okay, must be a mistake in the checklist.

a12a_140_27_22_to_140_29_47.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_27_22_to_140_29_47.text: Yes, that's right. It's not - it's poorly placed in the checklist.

a12a_140_27_22_to_140_29_47.speaker: Conrad
a12a_140_27_22_to_140_29_47.text: Okay. How'd the hot fire look all the way around? Everything okay?

a12a_140_27_22_to_140_29_47.speaker: Conrad
a12a_140_27_22_to_140_29_47.text: Got another question for you, too, Houston. What did Yankee Clipper's orbit finally decay down to? How well did you hit 60?

a12a_140_27_22_to_140_29_47.speaker: Carr
a12a_140_27_22_to_140_29_47.text: Roger, Pete. It's 61.9 by 58.4 at CDH. [Long pause.]

a12a_140_27_22_to_140_29_47.speaker: Conrad
a12a_140_27_22_to_140_29_47.text: Yes, that's pretty good, and we're targeted for zero CDH here on this thing, right?

a12a_140_38_16_to_140_38_18.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_140_38_16_to_140_38_18.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 140 hours, 46 minutes now in the flight. We're 1 hour and 17 minutes away from Time Of Ignition, away from Intrepid's lunar lift-off from the Ocean of Storms. Intrepid will ignite running almost 5,000 pounds of propellant through the upper stage ascent engine. Ignition will occur with Yankee Clipper passing just overhead about 80 nautical miles ahead of Intrepid. Intrepid goes through a short vertical rise and pitches over to climb to altitude horizontally inserting into orbit with a velocity of nearly 6,000 feet per second at an altitude of some 60,000 feet.

a12a_140_38_16_to_140_38_18.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_140_38_16_to_140_38_18.text: This is Apollo Control Houston now 140 hours, 52 minutes into the flight. We are still looking at a lift-off time of 142 hours, 03 minutes, 47 seconds. This ascent from the lunar surface is designed to put Intrepid in an initial orbit of 46.3 nautical miles by 8.8 nautical miles. For the burn we're looking for a Delta-V of 6,057 feet per second. The first maneuver following ascent, the concentric sequence initiate, is scheduled at 143 hours, 1 minute, 50 seconds with a Delta-V of 49.2 feet per second. The burn is scheduled to be done at apolune following lift-off and has the affect of raising

a12a_141_00_14_to_141_00_58.speaker: Conrad
a12a_141_00_14_to_141_00_58.text: Any objections to us starting P57 now?

a12a_141_00_14_to_141_00_58.speaker: Carr
a12a_141_00_14_to_141_00_58.text: Intrepid, Houston. We prefer that you wait until 45 in order to maximize the Delta-T there.

a12a_141_00_14_to_141_00_58.speaker: Carr
a12a_141_00_14_to_141_00_58.text: Yes. That's right - 15. We were thinking in terms of lift-off minus 45.

a12a_141_02_29_to_141_03_02.speaker: Carr
a12a_141_02_29_to_141_03_02.text: Roger, Al. Would you put battery 5 on the line now? Before, it wasn't really carrying it's load as well as it should have, and we'd like to pre-precondition that one, get it a little warmer and get it started early.

a12a_141_02_29_to_141_03_02.speaker: Bean
a12a_141_02_29_to_141_03_02.text: Okay. I noticed that; we'll do it.

a12a_141_02_29_to_141_03_02.speaker: Conrad
a12a_141_02_29_to_141_03_02.text: That's exactly what it did prior to descent - not much.

a12a_141_19_35_to_141_20_15.speaker: Carr
a12a_141_19_35_to_141_20_15.text: Roger, Dick. We're talking about it.

a12a_141_21_30_to_141_22_16.speaker: Carr
a12a_141_21_30_to_141_22_16.text: Intrepid. Houston. Your gravity angle difference looks good and, there'll be no uplinks to you this time.

a12a_141_21_30_to_141_22_16.speaker: Carr
a12a_141_21_30_to_141_22_16.text: Roger, Dick. Here's the Comm plan. About the time - When you get VHF communications established with Intrepid, we're going to dump the MSFN relay. If for some reason you lose it and you want to - you want to hear the - the Intrepid lift-off, let us know, and we can reconfigure in about 20 seconds; but we would prefer to leave the relay out as long az you've got VHF.

a12a_141_21_30_to_141_22_16.speaker: Gordon
a12a_141_21_30_to_141_22_16.text: Roger. I think that'll be fine. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a12a_141_21_30_to_141_22_16.speaker: Conrad
a12a_141_21_30_to_141_22_16.text: Boy, this place is fascinating, absolutely fascinating.

a12a_141_42_52_to_141_43_08.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_141_42_52_to_141_43_08.text: That was Capcom Jerry Carr telling Intrepid that their tank pressures look good. Meanwhile in the Control Center, our upfront displays have switched over from the Flight Dynamics Trajectory Displays, the lunar map being taken down for this ascent phase of the mission. We're at 141 hours, 44 minutes and 19 minutes, 45 seconds away from ignition.

a12a_141_49_09_to_141_50_03.speaker: Bean
a12a_141_49_09_to_141_50_03.text: Houston, Intrepid. Are you recommending VHF A Receiver On or Off for launch? Over.

a12a_141_49_09_to_141_50_03.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_141_49_09_to_141_50_03.text: We are 14 minutes away from time of ignition now - the...

a12a_141_49_09_to_141_50_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_141_49_09_to_141_50_03.text: Intrepid, Houston. Need to have your VHF A Transmitter to Voice Range and Receiver, Off.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Roger. Checklist is complete; standing by for T IG minus 2.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: T IG minus 2, 400 plus 10. Set your watch.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Gordon
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Houston Clipper. I have the LM.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Roger, Clipper. Intrepid, Clipper's watching you.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Howdy, Yankee Clipper. Okay. Very good. [Long pause.]

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: On my mark, Yankee Clipper, it will be 1 minute.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Mark. One minute. Master Arm is On [garble]...

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: I've got it. First stage push in 30 seconds, Pete.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Roger [Pause.]. Watch the ALSEP, and I'll fly the bird.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: DSKY's blank. Average g; abort stage...

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: All we lack is Pro and, then after, we get engine, start.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Intrepid, Houston. Copy ignition; guidance looks good.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Pitchover's looking good. Okay. Boy, you sure do [garble].

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Firing like I don't know what.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Thirty seconds. Thirty seconds; 177, 984.6, and out at 1900 feet.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: And at 1 minute, yaw right 20, Pete.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Say again? Pitch program looks good.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Kind of wobbles around up here [garble].

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Intrepid, Houston. Looking good at 1 minute.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Okay. We've yawed right 20. Keeping right down the pike.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Both tank pressures look good, Pete.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Sure jumps every time those thrusters fire.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Mark, 1 plus 30, 745, 156. We're out at 9,000 feet.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: I know it. It's still smooth.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: This thing is pitching over. It's right on the pitch profile.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: ...6. Just a little bit higher. Roger.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Everything looks good Pete, pressures look good.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Looks like the same territory we've passed over before, doesn't it? [Laughter].

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Two minutes and 30 seconds, looking at 1373, 187, climbing out at 19,700. Houston, you better clear me out of flight level 240 for flight level 600.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Okay. Squawking 21. How does your High Gain look, Al?

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: High gain looks real good, Pete. Hanging in there.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Gordon
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Houston, Clipper. If you can, have him transmit VHF also.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Dick would like you to transmit on VHF.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Roger. I am transmitting on VHF.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Three minutes and 30 seconds, Al. 2,130 feet per second, climbing 193, and we're out at 31,600.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Okay. Camera went off sometime after lift-off. I hope it got the ALSEP.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Oh, I see. Wonder why we got the Master Alarm? Never did see anything.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: No, I didn't either. Everything looks good.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Intrepid, Houston. You're looking good at 4.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Oh, look at that Rille down there. Wow!

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: That was part of Lansberg, I think, down there on the left.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: 4:30. 2,954 feet. This is a hot machine. 173, climbing out of 42,800. Glad you're happy. Okay.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Hey, I can move around a little bit more now as we lighten up.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Okay. You've got a big job now. Don't forget the ascent feed [garble]...[laughter].

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: I've been thinking about them since we lifted off.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Five minutes, 3,403, 156 feet, and out at 47,000.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Intrepid, Houston. You're looking good at 5. The harbor master has cleared you into the main channel,

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Look at that lunar surface, would you.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Man, look at that crater we're flying over.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Okay. I'm going to call it 500.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: 1,400 feet per second to go. Okay. Get a mark at 6 minutes.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Six minutes, 6 minutes, 4,382. Okay, I'm going to get over on Verb 16, Noun 85 right now. This thing's running a little bit hot.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Okay. 900 feet according to the AGS.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Standing by for 200 feet per second. 621 to go.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Now you've got 500 feet to go. Wow, we're really bumping along.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Going to close ascent feed, A1...

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Okay. Hey, I got to back off 32 feet [garble] thing. Agree to that, Houston? Master Alarm, but I don't know for what.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: I'll tell you what happened. I got to watching that problem, and I let her overspeed.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: [Garble] stage ready. I just figured we [garble].

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Okay. Does that look satisfactory to you?

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Looks good, Pete. We copied your overburn, and we see you're turning now.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Okay. I took it all out. I've got interested in this...

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Gordon
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Hello, Houston; Clipper. Still no VHF from Intrepid.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Main shutoff valve A indicated barber pole.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: So I tried and recycled it twice and then shut off both ascent feeds and left the crossfeed open as it is now. And I'm going to close both of them.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Okay. Mode Control, two, up to Att Hold. They are.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: And - on Inverter 2? I am on Inverter 2.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Intrepid, this is Houston. Punch your Engine Stop pushbutton.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Yes. Did it. Sorry about that. Everything's off.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: [Garble] let me get [garble] Gee, it's a dirty spacecraft in here.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Clipper, Houston. We're setting up the relay now.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Gordon
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: I wonder why he's not transmitting VHF.[Pause.]

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Intrepid, Houston. Clipper's not reading you VHF; we're configuring for MSFN relay now.[Long pause.]

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Intrepid; Yankee Clipper, how do you read Houston, now? We're in the Relay mode.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Hello, Yankee Clipper; Intrepid. How do you read?

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Gordon
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Intrepid, Yankee Clipper. Loud and clear now.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Intrepid, did you read Clipper's answer?

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Intrepid, Houston. Looks like you got a 47 by 8.8. Over.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Roger. What were we targeted for?

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Clipper, Houston. Give us P00 and Accept. We have a LM state vector for you.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Roger, Pete. Would you verify you're up on your forward VHF antenna? Break, Clipper, your computer's yours.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Gordon
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Houston, Clipper. Did you see the DSKY?

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: We got it, Dick. Go ahead.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Gordon
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Roger. I've got some good torquing angles here. I guess you really don't need them, do you?

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Gordon
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: That's affirm. I read you now, Pete, loud and clear.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Okay, Houston. You're looking at the DSKY there, the torquing angles.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Roger. We're looking at them, Pete. Sterling.

a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_00_57_to_142_23_52.text: Okay. Okay. We're going to Pro.

a12a_142_26_17.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_26_17.text: Dick, I hold you at 351 feet a second, at 200 miles.

a12a_142_26_17.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_142_26_17.text: That was Pete Conrad reporting to Dick Gordon the range and range rate readings he had on his onboard display. In Mission Control Center, Houston, we are presently reading a range of 198 nautical miles, between the 2 spacecraft, and a range rate of minus 331 feet per second. We are now at 142 hours, 28 minutes into the flight.

a12a_142_26_17_to_142_26_42.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_26_17_to_142_26_42.text: Dick, I hold you at 351 feet a second, at 200 miles.

a12a_142_26_17_to_142_26_42.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_142_26_17_to_142_26_42.text: That was Pete Conrad reporting to Dick Gordon the range and range rate readings he had on his onboard display. In Mission Control Center, Houston, we are presently reading a range of 198 nautical miles, between the 2 spacecraft, and a range rate of minus 331 feet per second. We are now at 142 hours, 28 minutes into the flight.

a12a_142_28_31_to_142_30_35.speaker: Bean
a12a_142_28_31_to_142_30_35.text: Houston, Intrepid. We're going to go over to Omni now.

a12a_142_28_31_to_142_30_35.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_28_31_to_142_30_35.text: Intrepid, Houston. You're about 45 seconds from LOS.

a12a_142_28_31_to_142_30_35.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_28_31_to_142_30_35.text: Intrepid, Houston. We'll see you at 143:16.

a12a_142_28_31_to_142_30_35.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_28_31_to_142_30_35.text: Intrepid, Houston. Your CSI Delta-V is going to be about 46.5. Over.

a12a_142_28_31_to_142_30_35.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_28_31_to_142_30_35.text: Intrepid, Houston. We've got LOS on the Clipper, and we'll see him at 13.

a12a_142_28_31_to_142_30_35.speaker: Conrad
a12a_142_28_31_to_142_30_35.text: Okay. Say again our AOS time?

a12a_142_28_31_to_142_30_35.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_28_31_to_142_30_35.text: Your AOS time is 143:16. It's nominal.

a12a_142_28_31_to_142_30_35.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_28_31_to_142_30_35.text: Roger. Nominal in the flight plan.

a12a_142_28_31_to_142_30_35.speaker: Carr
a12a_142_28_31_to_142_30_35.text: Intrepid, Houston. Go Low Bit Rate.

a12a_143_16_57_to_143_17_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_16_57_to_143_17_28.text: Okay. Sounds good. I'll be working on out-of-plane here for you.

a12a_143_16_57_to_143_17_28.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_16_57_to_143_17_28.text: Yankee Clipper, Houston. How do you read?

a12a_143_16_57_to_143_17_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_16_57_to_143_17_28.text: Hello, Houston, Clipper. Loud and clear.

a12a_143_16_57_to_143_17_28.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_16_57_to_143_17_28.text: Roger. CSI burn was good. Intrepid burned 45.3 feet per second. My solution was 45.9.

a12a_143_16_57_to_143_17_28.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_143_16_57_to_143_17_28.text: That was Dick Gordon reporting the Concentric Sequence Initiate burn was good. We're at 143 hours, 18 minutes. When we reacquire Intrepid we'll probably receive a status report on that burn. This is Apollo Control, Houston continuing to monitor.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Intrepid, Houston. How do you read?

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Bean
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Loud and clear, Houston.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Roger, Al. Read you the same.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Bean
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Residuals PGNS were plus 0.1, minus 0.1, and minus 0.3.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Intrepid, Houston. We'd like to know what your Delta-Vs were that you loaded.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: What do you mean, what Delta-Vs we loaded? We loaded 45.3 feet per second. Is that what you mean?

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Affirm.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: That was our CSI solution.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Okay.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Okay. And I've run CDH here, and it looks like minus 9 and minus 8 roughly. Shows me 59 seconds early at TPI.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Roger.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: And we're not going to make the system look like we need to make the out-of-plane. We are down in the noise level on out-of-plane. Dick's going 0.4 of a foot per second; and I haven't looked at it yet, but I will in a minute.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Roger. Intrepid, Houston. Can you give us High Bit Rate, please? [Long pause.]

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 143 hours, 21 minutes now into the flight. We presently show Intrepid and Yankee Clipper at a range of 310 nautical miles with a range rate of minus 75 feet per second.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: I tell you, Houston, I sure do enjoy flying this thing. It's - Both the ascent stage and the descent stage are both nice.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Roger, Pete.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: For - for your information, I crossed that on the CSI burn, and that pretty evened me up, and I also switched my DAP load to system A.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Roger. Copy.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: And my out-of-plane shows 0.31 miles and 0.3 of a foot per second, so I think we'll forget it.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Okay, Pete. That sounds good. While you got a minute, we had a question about the sequence camera. Did that camera stop right after lift-off?.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Apparently it did, and then it stopped again several times.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Bean
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: That's affirmative. It stopped, and then I started it, and it stopped two or three times.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Say, I guess nobody else has - Anybody else had to use these window heaters before? Our windows keep fogging over, and I have to run the window heaters all the time.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Intrepid, Houston. The folks here say that was pretty nominal on Apollo 11.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Oh, I didn't remember that. Okay. Very good.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Hey, Pete.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Go ahead, Dick.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: My CDH time on my computer is 143:59:46:70.47.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Okay. We're within a couple - about 15 seconds of one another.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Okay. We're going to use yours.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: I got it. Thank you.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Intrepid, Houston.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Go.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Roger, Pete. I sent you bum dope. 11 did not use their heaters.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Yes. I don't remember anybody having to use them, and both my docking window and - and both Al's window and my window - We collected moisture on the lunar surface and we've started collecting it here in flight, so I put the window heater back on.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Roger.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Just prior to this call up from Mission Control you heard Pete Conrad and Dick Gordon comparing onboard computation numbers for CDH, the constant Delta Height maneuver. We're at 143 hours, 26 minutes now into the flight; and this is Apollo Control Houston.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Sure do apologize, Houston, for the overburn. I got my head looking at Al there and I just shut her off late.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Roger. No sweat, Pete. [Pause.]

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: What did he do this time, Pete?

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Say again.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: What the devil did he do this time?

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Well, he didn't do anything. We had one main shut-off valve that barber poled over here, and it turned out to be an indicator. But, I got interested in that and I didn't de-arm the engine soon enough, and we shut down about 30 feet per second over. That's the reason I had to back her up. No big deal. [Pause.]

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: We presently show Intrepid and Yankee Clipper 126 nautical miles apart. We're at 143 hours, 28 minutes now into the flight.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Okay, Pete. My first try at it is [garble].

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: And what?

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: [Garble].

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Okay, Dick. You're almost unreadable.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Clipper, Houston. Your S-band is getting pretty ratty.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Okay, Dick. I'm showing on 17.6.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Are you looking at the recycle on the DSKY, Houston?

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: We're checking, Pete.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: It's minus 10 and minus 8.8.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Intrepid, Houston. We're watching. [Long pause.]

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: I finally - finally have a visual on Yankee Clipper, I think.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Roger.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Yes. I got you visually, Yankee.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: I'm still leading by 122 miles.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Okay. I show 122 on mine, closing at 95 feet a second.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: [Garble] That Omni PPI [garble] Hey, I saw your flash down there [garble].

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: That was Pete Conrad reporting he thought he had a visual sighting of Yankee Clipper. The two spacecrafts presently 122 nautical miles apart. We are at 143 hours, 32 minutes into the flight.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Pretty close to that rim.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: [Garble] on the Surveyor on the [garble] of that crater.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 143 hours, 37 minutes now into the flight.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Say, Houston, Al's working so hard keeping his AGS updated here, why don't we let him burn CDH?

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Roger, Pete.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Say again Jerry?

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Intrepid, Houston. Stand by on that. We're consulting our oracle right now.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: [Laughter] Houston, I'm only kidding, but he's all over the cockpit. Putting that range and range rate in.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Bean
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: [Garble] my burn.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: I think we ought to rename the Intrepid the flying junk pile. You ought to see it inside this spacecraft, Houston.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Roger. Copy.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: That was Pete Conrad coming to Mission Control with the suggestion that they do their CDH or Constant Delta Height maneuver, utilizing the AGS or the secondary guidance system. The point he made was that Al Bean was all over the cabin constantly updating their AGS numbers from the PNGS and I guess he thought why not use them. Presently we're showing Intrepid and Yankee Clipper 115 nautical miles apart. This through our displays, taking an over the shoulders look at Intrepid's computer readouts. We're at 143 hours, 39 minutes.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Okay. I'm minus 10.3. And my TPI's 2½ minutes early.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Bean
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Okay.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Say, Houston. With - with your concurrence - we'd like to go over into the cabin mode for a while, stay suited though, but in cabin mode and try to get rid of some of this dirt before we dock.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Roger, Pete. Stand by.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Intrepid, Houston. Go ahead, use the cabin mode.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: [Garble] canisters. Yes. Okay.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Intrepid, Houston. I've a PIPA bias update read-up for you.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Bean
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Okay.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Go ahead.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Okay. Verb 21, Noun 01, Enter, 1452, Enter, 77423, Enter; Enter, 1454, Enter, 00406, Enter; Enter, 1456, Enter, 00777, Enter. Over.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Okay. Let me see if I got those numbers all right. Verb 21, Noun 01, Enter, 1452, Enter, 77423, Enter; Enter, 1454, Enter, 00046, Enter, Enter, 1456, Enter, 00077?

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Intrepid, Houston. That's negative. Address 1454 should read 00406, and address 1456 should read 00777. Over.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: That's affirmative, Pete.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Hey, Al, have you ...?

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: [garble] burn [garble].

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Yankee Clipper, Houston. Over.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Roger. I've got some High Gain angles for you, Dick.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Go ahead [garble].

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Roger. Pitch is minus 23 and yaw is plus 171. Over.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: And we're on High Gain.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Pete, [garble] run your solution. I've only got 20 marks on [garble].

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Say again, Dick.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: [Garble] on that solution, we got enough marks here for five solutions. We ought to go ahead and press on.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: This is Apollo Control Houston. We currently show the 2 spacecraft at 103 nautical miles apart.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Yankee Clipper, Houston. We're going to have...

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: [Garble], Jer.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: ...a handover here now, in your case from Honeysuckle to Madrid. Over. At143:50.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Okay.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Very good.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Whichever way the world turns.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Pete, your out-of-plane for CDH is 0.4 plus.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: This is Apollo Control Houston. Meanwhile in the Control Center we have the ignition clock counting down for CDH. We show 10 minutes and 30 seconds until time of ignition. We're at 143 hours, 50 minutes now into the Flight of Apollo 12.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Okay. I'm getting ready to [garble] final Comp.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Bean
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: I just fired one.[Long pause.]

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Yankee Clipper, Houston. How do you read through Madrid?

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Hello, Houston; Clipper. Loud and clear by me.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: We read you the same.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Early, early, early, it's a minus sign. Seventy-five. Okay. Here's my solution. Delta-H is 0.8; 34.53 at 3 minutes early; Delta-V's, Noun 81, 10.3, zero, and 7.0. 7.0. would you read me your velocities again please? 5.3 is in Y, [garble] in Z. Okay. I copied minus 2.2 zip, plus 9.3. How about minus 10.2 and 7, [garble] for this 9.3?

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Now, wait, wait, wait, Dick. Call Houston and have them relay it to me. I can't understand you.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Clipper, Houston. Go ahead.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: [garble] That's okay. Go ahead.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Hey, Jerry. Just tell him I agree with his solution?

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Roger. Break, Pete. Clipper says he agrees with your solution.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Okay. Very good. And, Jerry, tell them that our Noun 81 was - Where did you put it, Al? Minus 10.7, or is that 2, minus 10.2 and minus 9.3?

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Roger. Copy. Noun 81, minus 10.2, and minus 9.3.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Roger - Roger.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Bean
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: That's affirmative.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: And Clipper Rogered that. He heard it.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Hey, you got any thoughts on the ground, Houston, why our Comm is so bad between each other?

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Pete, we're checking.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: There must be something - Could you just tell us how to fix it?

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Break. Did you get an out-of-plane from Dick?

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: We don't have any out-of-plane. It was 0.3 again or something.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: That was 0.4, Pete.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Oh; 0.4 of a foot per second.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Clipper, Houston.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Go ahead, Houston; this is Clipper.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Roger. Just thought we'd better make a check with you and see how your antennas are. Are you on the starboard antenna?

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: That's affirmative. I'm on the lower antenna, lower right.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Roger.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: The VHF is really horrible. [Long pause.]

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Bean
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Okay.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Bean
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Okay.[Long pause.]

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; the ignition clock in Mission Control shows now less than 3 minutes from Time Of Ignition for CDH, Constant Delta Height maneuver. Two minutes now away from CDH. This...

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Are you going to burn? [Long pause.]

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: You're right, Al. I picked it up on the sextant. [Long pause.]

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Less than a minute away now.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: It's smaller than the LM.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: I'm with you [Pause]. Let me know if I can help you. [Long pause.]

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Gordon
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Do you want a countdown? [Long pause.]

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Bean
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Okay, Pete.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Guidance says they are burning now.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Burn complete, Houston.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Carr
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Roger, Pete. Looks good.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Mission Control
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Burn is concluded.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Conrad
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: Okay.

a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.speaker: Bean
a12a_143_19_25_to_144_03_03.text: My TPI time was 144:34:54.87. That's pretty good.
